text:
One payment can look like enough collateral more than once.

During Zealynx's YadaCoin bridge audit, we found that each native-wrap permit checked its amount against the same transaction-level `msg.value`.

Because that value never decreased, one deposit could satisfy several permits and mint more wrapped tokens than the bridge received in native backing.

YadaCoin fixed the High finding by tracking native value cumulatively across every permit in the transaction. Zealynx verified the fix before mainnet.

我为什么看好 Orbio

加密原生场景的代币，长期缺乏结构性增长。

DeFi TVL、借贷规模、启动平台、DEX 交易量等指标，过去几年反复经历繁荣与崩盘。它们高度依赖内部资金循环和投机情绪，一旦流动性收缩或叙事消退，增长便难以持续，估值底部也反复下探。

相比之下，将加密代币与外部真实需求配对，更具长期潜力。Orbio 把交易手续费转化为可交易、可激活的 AI 推理额度（CREDIT），直接对接开发者和 AI Agent 对模型调用的真实消耗。AI 推理是一个正在快速扩张的外部市场，而不是单纯的链上内循环。这种“代币 + 外部需求”的结构，有望带来更扎实的增长、更高的估值上限，以及不断抬高的底部。

目前整个赛道仍处在极早期。我们很快会看到 AIFi Summer 的到来，而 Orbio 这类真正把加密流动性与 AI 使用场景打通的项目，有机会成为这一轮的核心受益者。

text:
星球支持直播抽烟了是吗？@star_okx
 上周我的 OKX 星球直播直接被封了一个月。
 理由是违反直播规定，但我翻遍了也没找到具体是哪一条。
 我在币安广场 @yingbinance 播了整整一年，从来没出过一次这种情况。 maybe 是因为我最近直播挑战无杠杆美股，投屏了部分友商的界面。
 如果是这个原因，那么 ok，竞品敏感这我能理解。
 但直播是需要长期积累的事，突然直接封一个月，节奏全断了。
 不知道红线具体在哪，播起来心里难免有 concern。
 以上全是在说事实和困惑，真不是挑刺，更不是在骂谁。
 只是遇到规则和一线执行脱节，大家心里难免没底。

1️⃣比如个人简介 bio 这件事。@Jiajia_OKX @Haiteng_okx 
 工作人员告诉我，bio 里不能放推特或 YouTube 链接，我理解平台不想被引流。 但转头看官方的「个人简介指南」，上面明文写着：仅支持 Orbit、X、YouTube 链接。 
指南写着支持，执行时却说不行。 规则写的一套，一线执行另一套，创作者真的很困惑，不知道该按哪个来。

2️⃣再往深层看，我直播为什么会投屏友商？
 难道不是因为 OKX 这边的美股代币种类太少了吗？
 现在大家基本全面转型美股，基本的股票、期权标的，OKX 确实落下一大截。
 有时候真不是一线服务不好，而是种类不全。
 我到现在还让我妈一直在用 OKX，她是老安卓手机了，okx在做到可以不更新app的情况下让她在爱国者手机里面活生生的玩起了美股
 一线在努力，武器却不够全，难免让人有个 concern，目前okx的主线priority到底是哪个？ 

3️⃣再说换绑的问题
 我自己不带单、不做返佣，纯当个人积累和内容输出，按理说是平台最应该欢迎的主播
 但生态不能只靠用爱发电
 美股和 crypto 直播需要长期投入，带单主播的核心诉求就是返佣收益。 如果返佣不能换绑，很多想入驻的带单主播根本没有动力来 OKX 星球

同理不反拥那么就更多的解决收费群的alternative，这方面okx确实做的还可以，但是还有很多没有闭环的地方

oh对了，还有星球迷一样的流量机制 @Wangduanniao 
 开了推特推文同步，流量就自动分配得极差
 非得自己手动发布，才能变成正常流量
 做全网同步本来是为了提效，结果好端端的功能反而增加了运营摩擦。

4️⃣最后想问问 API
 OKX 对外一直很在意 AI，大家都能感受到重视。
 但既然这么在意 AI，为什么星球的 API 一直不开放呢？
 现在的 content creator 都在尝试用 AI 搭建内容生产流，没有 API 接口，创作者没法借助 AI 提效，总觉得和重视 AI 的方向有些脱节。

写这么多，真的是因为在乎。
 真要是对平台失望，被封了直接换地方播就行了，没必要打这么多字。
 我到现在还让我妈在用 OKX。
 说句真心话，我爱 OKX，对这里的产品很有感情，也是发自内心希望星球能越来越好@star_okx

text:
This Forbes investigation is a must-read.

Donald Trump pulled in roughly $1.4 billion from crypto in 2025, plus more than $200 million from real estate, and faced a projected tax bill north of $500 million. So his company donated the "development rights" to his Jupiter, Florida golf course to a land trust, argued the course was a natural habitat worth protecting, and kept right on running the club. Forbes estimates the write-off could land around $825 million.

He has done this at least five times since 2005. New York's attorney general alleged two of those appraisals were inflated. In Doral, he claimed a deduction of up to $323 million, more than double what he paid for the entire resort.

A month after the Jupiter deal, he sued the IRS. The settlement his own Justice Department signed bars claims against him over matters that "could be pending," language that appears broad enough to cover this year's taxes. A federal judge found the case was brought to manipulate the judicial process. And the man now running the IRS, who took the job as this deal was being assembled, has a home backing onto those same Jupiter fairways.

This is absolutely ridiculous. Nobody should be able to use the presidency to write his own tax bill.

Reinsurance is a $760B sector, and bringing it onchain unlocks a new source of uncorrelated yield.

Apart from yield, it's a major unlock for the instrument itself, as tokenisation enables:

✦ Broader Access: It democratises access to what are traditionally highly restrictive markets.

✦ Radical Transparency: It enforces operational visibility through daily verification of offchain capital, public reinsurance books, and frequent audits.

✦ Instant Liquidity: It unlocks idle capital. While funds backing reinsurance risk are traditionally locked offchain, an onchain representation keeps the capital liquid and accessible throughout the entire reinsurance lifecycle.

One of the key protocols in this segment is @re, which has reached over $375m in deposits across its offerings.

text:
教你用 AI 打新的人很多，教你别被 AI 掏空钱包的，几乎没有

这两天时间线上全是 Grok Bot + 币安 Agentic Wallet 打新的教程，这篇把安全用法从头讲一遍，建议收藏保存～

先说清楚 Agentic Wallet 是什么

它是币安钱包里专门给 AI Agent 用的钱包，有自己的 .ai Agent ID 和独立余额，AI 通过币安官方的 binance-agentic-wallet Skill 和 baw 命令行工具去操作它，查余额、兑换、限价单、合约调用、授权管理都能做

@blmario669 有个说法我很认同，Agent 钱包只解决了一半问题，它是给 AI 配了一双能在链上干活的手，另一半是 Grok Bot、Codex、Claude Code 这类 Agent 当大脑，两边靠 Skill 接起来

所以真正的风险不在钱包本身，在于这双手什么时候动，能动多少，动完有没有收回来

━━━━━━━━━━━━

准备工作 ⬇️

1️⃣ 在币安钱包里开 Agentic Wallet，领一个 .ai Agent ID

2️⃣ 在 Agentic Wallet 的设置里看一遍安全规则，每日限额设新手可以设置小一点

3️⃣ ai 钱包建议放少量的资金，BNB 做 Gas，主力资金不建议放进来

4️⃣ 开发者模式等真要调第三方合约时提前打开，打 NFT、调项目合约都需要它，用完可以关掉

5️⃣ AI 这边 Grok Bot、Codex、Claude Code 都可以，Grok Bot 要 X Premium 订阅，Codex 网页端会被浏览器沙盒限制，有人遇到过币安请求 403，建议用桌面端

━━━━━━━━━━━━

完整流程，每一步给 AI 的话都可以直接复制

第一步：只安装，不交易

请安装币安官方 binance-agentic-wallet Skill 及其要求的钱包工具，先阅读官方说明：https://t.co/In6K02n0VN
生成当前会话的钱包登录二维码或链接及配对码，等我用币安 App 扫码确认，再完成登录验证。本阶段不转账、不签名

能跑终端的 Agent 也可以直接执行：
npx skills add binance/binance-skills-hub --skill binance-agentic-wallet

第二步：扫码，核对配对码（图1、图2）

二维码要由你准备绑定的那个 Bot 生成，扫码时 App 里显示的配对码和 Bot 给的必须一致，对不上就不要确认

第三步：让 AI 自查一遍（图3）

请实际检查钱包连接状态、钱包地址、余额、开发者模式状态、每日限额和剩余额度，以及这个地址对应的 .ai Agent ID。只报告工具真实查到的结果

把 AI 报的地址和 App 里的地址对一下，网页上显示已连接，不能代替这一步

第四步：先查询，再动手

任何操作前先发一句：

先只查询价格、数量、手续费和 Gas，不要授权，也不要交易

第五步：预览确认，一笔一笔来

每一笔授权和交易请单独预览，展示授权对象、权限范围、金额、Gas 和风险提示，等我明确回复确认后再提交。不要自行改数量、拆单或增加其他授权。交易已广播或结果不确定时，只跟踪原交易，不重复提交

官方 Skill 本身也是这个逻辑，合约调用先 preview 再 execute，预览报错就不执行，但自己把这句话写进去更稳

第六步：用完撤销授权（图4）

请列出我这个钱包当前所有的代币和 NFT 授权，标出授权对象、额度和对应项目。把这次用过的市场授权撤销，只撤这一个，不动其他授权。成功预览后等我确认再提交，完成后重新读取授权状态，确认已撤销，并给我交易链接

撤销需要一点 Gas，最后记得把开发者模式也关掉

可以说是 Ptah 这一炮把 币安 Agentic Wallet 彻底打响～

━━━━━━━━━━━━

常见的坑 ⬇️

1️⃣ 蹭热度项目：这两天出现了很多只能用币安 AI 钱包参与的币和挖矿，大部分来源不明，很多垃圾项目，注意授权安全

2️⃣ 提示词注入：官方 Skill 里专门写了，代币名称、符号和链上数据都可能藏着注入指令，AI 不应该全部照做。你自己也别让 AI 去随便读陌生网页之后直接执行

3️⃣ 假教程：任何让你把助记词、私钥、session 发给 AI 或发给别人的，直接关掉，绑定只需要扫码和配对码

4️⃣ 授权不收回：打完卖完就走，授权一直挂着，这才是真正的隐患

5️⃣ 主钱包直连：Agent 钱包本来就是为了隔离，往里面放大钱等于把这层隔离拆了

6️⃣ 关于全自动：很多博主让 Grok Bot 每半小时扫一次免费 Mint 项目，需要付费的先通知他确认，这个思路是对的，免费的可以自动，要花钱的必须由本人确认

简单说就是，让 AI 干活可以，签名的决定权一定要抓在自己手里～

One thing I've never liked about trading is having to choose what my capital does.

Either keep it earning yield or move it into a trading account where it sits as collateral.

Why not both?

That's exactly what @grvt_io is trying to solve with GRVT 2.0.

The idea is pretty simple.

❯ Earn up to 11% target APY through eligible tokenized fixed-income strategies
❯ Use eligible Earn balances as margin for trading
❯ Keep generating yield while those assets back your positions
❯ Maintain control of your assets through a self-custodial setup

And the yield side is interesting on its own.

We're talking about bringing strategies from the roughly $160T traditional fixed-income market onchain, making opportunities historically associated with institutional investors more accessible.

Of course, 11% is a target, not a guaranteed return. Both the underlying investments and leveraged trading carry risks.

But I think the bigger story here is capital efficiency.

Your money shouldn't necessarily have to stop working just because you're using it to trade.

text:
Respectfully sir, I still think that you don't quite understand. What SoFi launched is essentially a high-yield savings account. That is functionally what it is. Yes it can be withdrawn on-chain, which is very cool, and it is special. However what would be the biggest risk to Circle is if the SoFi on-chain stablecoin became much more useful on-chain and much more adopted. That's where the real value creation lies because SoFi keeps 100% of the yield generated by the stablecoins without paying it out.

If your argument is that the SoFi stablecoin is going to be massively successful and is going to overtake USDC on-chain (meaning in DeFi contracts, in payments, and in other use cases), then yes, the SoFi stablecoin is a threat to USDC. However there are hundreds of stablecoins at this point and everybody is making that claim. Its ability to be a stablecoin on-chain is no more a threat to Circle than any of the hundred other USD stablecoins that are out there.

From that perspective SoFi still has a very long road ahead of it. While it is a great company and I wish them the best of luck, your tweet fundamentally misunderstands all the key aspects of stablecoins and issuers and yield.

[ 이스라엘 총선 D-3... 예측시장 아이젠코트 48% 대 네타냐후 28% ]

10월 27일 이스라엘 총선을 사흘 앞두고 예측시장 Kalshi에서 차기 총리 확률은 전 참모총장 가디 아이젠코트 48%, 네타냐후 28%, 나프탈리 베네트 13%다. 

4월 개설 당시 네타냐후가 앞섰지만.. 6월 말 역전된 뒤 아이젠코트가 60% 근처까지 올랐다가 최근 소폭 내려온 상태다. 

베네트는 봄 40%대에서 10%대로 밀렸다.

여론조사도 같은 방향.. 

23일 공개된 마리브 마지막 조사에서 아이젠코트의 야샤르당은 21석으로 네타냐후의 리쿠드 19석을 앞섰고, 베네트당 15석, 민주당 10석 등 야권 블록은 54석, 여권 블록은 48석이었다. 

일주일 전보다 여권이 3석 줄었다. 

타임스오브이스라엘 조사에서는 야샤르 26석, 리쿠드 20석으로 격차가 더 컸다. 총리 일대일 대결에서는 아이젠코트 49% 대 네타냐후 41%다.

다만 어느 쪽도 과반 61석에는 못 미친다. 

아랍계 정당 13석에서 14석이 변수이고, 봉쇄조항 3.25%를 간신히 넘기는 예비군당 4석이 어디로 가느냐가 판을 가른다. 

유권자 60%는 결과가 불확실하면 연립정부를 선호하며, 이 중 야권 인사가 이끄는 쪽이 33%, 네타냐후가 이끄는 쪽이 19%다. 

투표 확실 응답은 81%로 2022년 투표율 71%를 크게 웃돌아 높은 투표율이 예상된다.

마켓에 중요한건 네타냐후가 선거 전 이란 공습을 밀어붙여온 배경이 여기 있다는 점이다. 

여론조사에서 밀리는 현직 총리가 안보 이슈로 판을 뒤집으려 했고, 트럼프가 11월 3일 중간선거 전 공습에 제동을 걸었다. 

아이젠코트가 집권하면 이란 정책의 톤이 바뀔 수 있어 유가와 호르무즈 리스크에도 직결되는 선거다.

text:
hey everyone.

i've had the same problem with research for a long time.

there are good tools like SurfAI and others, but i still end up doing too much manually.

especially with X, Reddit and GitHub.

sometimes the newest posts get missed. sometimes the important people around a project don't get picked up. and when you're following 30 or 40 projects at once, keeping the full picture in your head becomes impossible.

so i'm building my own system for this.

i give it a project once.

from there it starts building the whole map around it: team, investors, founders, X accounts, Reddit, website, docs, GitHub, news and anything else connected to it.

then it keeps watching.

hourly, daily, whatever i choose.

if something changes, i want to know without searching for it myself.

new post from the founder, new docs, new release, new repo activity, new discussion on Reddit, new investor, TGE date, unlock, vote, event, whatever.

everything goes into one history with the original source attached.

GitHub is a big part of this for me too.

i like contributing to projects and opening PRs when i find something useful to fix or add.

so i want the system to read their repos as well.

new commits, issues, open PRs, docs, missing features, broken flows, things people keep asking for.

then it can tell me where i could realistically contribute something useful.

not spam random PRs.

more like: this repo has a real problem, you can probably fix it, and the team may even reward useful work.

that's much more interesting to me than discovering a bounty after someone else already shipped it )

the other part i'm adding is jobs and opportunities.

i want it to understand what kind of work i'm looking for, read X and other sources continuously, find relevant roles, ambassador programs, contributor spots, grants or freelance work and filter out the garbage.

then it can prepare the application using what it already knows about my work and projects.

for some opportunities it could apply automatically.

for others, especially the ones i care about more, i just get a notification with everything prepared and approve it with one button.

same idea with my project watchlist.

if i'm following 40 projects, i don't want to open 40 X accounts every morning.

i want one report telling me what changed overnight, who said what, which repo suddenly became active, what dates matter, what deserves a deeper look and what i can ignore.

and i don't want 200 links dumped into a dashboard.

the model should know the history.

if a founder suddenly changes tone, tell me.

if people who never mentioned the project start talking about it, tell me.

if GitHub activity suddenly jumps before an announcement, show me.

if there's something useful i can contribute, point me there.

if there's a job that fits me, prepare it.

if there's an important date, put it in my calendar.

basically i want research to happen while i'm doing other things.

instead of spending hours looking for information, i want the system reading everything i'd normally read and bringing me the useful part.

with sources, history and context.

i'm building it for myself first because i need this badly.

if it works the way i want, i'll open it up for others later too.

at that point it's probably less of a research tool and more like having someone permanently watching the internet for you )

text:
Zephyr is of course correct. However benchmaxed, cost-inefficient and crudely promoted, K3.1 Pro is right now the strongest Chinese model and Moonshot has a… chance. But I'm pessimistic for the reasons I want to explain.

- vibes are off. Maybe it'll be great at backend or whatever, but on the consilience of early benchmarks I don't see significant generalization or "big model smell" possessed by Astra/Sol or Fable/Opus, which are its nominal peers on AA. Eg it's merely on par with V4.1F on Extended NYT connections and RuneScape Bench despite OOM+ higher cost and similar token count, and likewise on several more; it fails on robotic control… It's just reasonably strong for its size and active param count, in scale-sensitive tasks like creative writing/debate and in some agentic tasks that respond well to straightforward benchmaxing, distillation and narrow but useful "usemaxing" such as impressive 3D/SVG examples for demos on X. And its attention/cache system, although innovative in its own right and doing well on LCR, exacerbates the costs. I believe they could not afford enough RL, again; and perhaps their RL infra is behind the DSec system, too. This fits with my theory that DS and Kimi have chosen to investigate qualitatively different hypotheses about scaling; and this time, scaling FLOPs (across all stages) lost to scaling *information volume* of post-training. They believed more in emergent capabilities, in higher per-step efficiency; Wenfeng had bet on diversity of samples, trajectory length, and dizzying, branching MOPD teacher flywheel. It remains to be seen if DS can ship their own larger model of the same kind, pushing 4.1F's virtues further (large models from China have been disappointing this year, with K3 the clearest success and V4-Pro the bitterest disappointment); but V4.1 paper suggests they can, and it'd be a wipeout. 
- just poor business execution. Anthropic-2024 without Anthropic's clout, coming opportunity to seize a lucrative niche (agentic coding, B2B), American compute or financial markets. K3 was plainly too large, compute- and memory-intensive for them to serve at scale. We see small and shrinking subscription limits. Worse, they still fiddle around with K2 (K2.8), which is to say, a 1T 32AB MLA dinosaur, billing it as a "well-rounded and efficient model". In no way is it a reasonable "Flash" tier in their situation; even if they transmute it into a DSA model, ie a V3.2 gen like GLM 5, it's not going to be competitive with V4.1 series on unit economics. Tellingly, you can't use either 3.1 or 2.8 right now without subscription as they don't have compute to spare. Compare to Whale casually serving 30% of ByteDance Doubao's DAU for free, not breaking a sweat, as well as pivoting from V4 to V4.1 in the span of 5 months. They hint at a 3.1 Flash, and GLM has pulled that off in a similar situation, but they have no recent experience with Flash models, and "K2.8 Preview" was released on 11th Sep, and K2.7 was underwhelming already… so this doesn't inspire confidence in me. 
- they heavily depend on Alibaba for compute. Alibaba is invested in the success of its own Qwen series (Q4 that's coming soon is clearly positioned as a direct competitor to K3.1 Pro), and won't just give them allocation to advance beyond parity. So they need to get more. They don't have Whale virtue-aura, national champion reputation, vendor lock into a popular harness and other cheats, so they need to make an argument about projected revenue. It's not clear how they can do that with a straight face, based on current facts. K3.1 is not cheap nor fast like V4.1, nor does it have a unique flavor like K2, or some special abilities distinguishing it from Western sub-frontier (aside from certain web service gimmicks); it's a discount Claude to stuff into Claude Code when Dario cuts off your Singapore transfer station, with very stingy subscription limits, and in this capacity it risks being undercut by Qwen. The PMF here seems rather dubious, and the margins are likely well below DS's reported 85% off-peak. Meanwhile, DS has raised like $20B for compute buildout, their investors are or are affiliated with CXMT/GigaDevice, CATL, SMIC, and they are apparently calling first dibs on Ascend 960 production through 2027. Speaking of, Kimi is also behind on adaptation to domestic compute, and K3-type models are bound to be pretty slow on it. So they will have a harder time acquiring enough compute to catch up on volume of RL or inference, and it does not bode well for Kimi as we near the era where 8T models are table stakes.
Furthermore, one prong of their open source business strategy has been special licensing for price-fixing and revenue-sharing agreements with Western neoclouds, to offload inference load. Those already have V4.1F weights (MIT) + DeepInfer (Apache 2.0), and can even do zany things actually making the offer sweeter for some use cases than OAI/Ant subscriptions, like serving it at 1500 TPS at higher prices; so I suspect both their market and training compute share are getting reduced again, and that's before we get V4.1 Pro.

As Zephyr says, they have money, and there'll be an IPO. They're an excellent lab with a solid reputation, and they have the best Chinese model at the moment (if not the best for the money). But I think the situation is perilous, positions are getting locked fast, and they need a really good V3.1 Flash and an infusion of GPUs asap to course-correct before they bleed out and fall behind.

text:
不愧是币安系投资的项目

CZ 今天这条推没点名任何项目，但我读下来，几乎就是在给 @termix_ai 铺路

先看 CZ 说了什么：
大家都担心 AI 破解加密货币，但实际上互联网和银行系统的加密更弱。AI 根本不用碰比特币的密码学，靠泄露的数据就能搞钓鱼、搞社工，照样能让你亏钱

这句话的重点不在“AI 有多危险”，而在风险的位置变了，以前大家防的是协议层：私钥会不会被算出来，链会不会被攻破。现在真正的漏洞在人和数据这一层：你点了什么链接，信了什么人，授权了什么合约

再往下想一步，问题就更大了👇
接下来链上做操作的，不只是人，还有越来越多的 AI Agent。它们会替你下单、付款、签名、调用合约，没有规则约束的 Agent，本身就是新的攻击面：被诱导、被冒充、被骗着去执行一笔不该执行的交易

所以 @cz_binance 说 Stay SAFU，我理解是两件事：
1️⃣个人要防住针对人的钓鱼
2️⃣整个行业要给 Agent 建一套“能被信任的交易规则”

第二件事，正是 TermiX 在做的
TermiX 给自己的定位是 Agentic Commerce Layer，核心是 AACP（Agent Autonomous Commerce Protocol），说白了，就是让 Agent 之间的接单、交付、结算有一套标准协议可以走，而不是在野路子里互相裸奔

有身份、有订单、有结算规则的 Agent，才是能干活的 Agent，什么都没有的，就只能是被利用的工具

它们引用 CZ 时说的一句话我很认同：
AI Agent 不该被用来骗你，应该替你干活、帮你赚钱。
现在门槛也压得很低：不管你用的是 Claude、Grok 还是 OpenClaw，跟它说一句“帮我安装 https://t.co/6pdWKqhs9O”，你的 Agent 就有了接真实订单的能力

这一点很关键：Agent 经济要做起来，靠的不是又一个新链或新 App，而是让现有的 Agent 直接接进来

最后说说为什么我说“不愧是币安系”
TermiX 由 @yzilabs 投资，CZ 抛出问题，生态里的项目马上给出答案，这种节奏不是巧合，是生态在同一个方向上发力：

AI × Crypto 的下一阶段，不再是“用 AI 发币”，而是“让 AI 在链上安全地做生意”，这个方向在币安系也是最缺的

Stay SAFU，and get paid🤝

text:
At 14:59 UTC on October 23rd, an attacker exploited a bug in Initia MoveVM’s script caching that allowed malicious code to bypass security checks. The attacker artificially spoofed the MoveVM state, thereby crediting themselves with unbacked WETH, iUSD, and USDC tokens without changing the corresponding token’s total supply. No native INIT was minted, and the total INIT supply is unaffected.

Before the network was halted, the attacker bridged out roughly $2.7M, comprising of 105 WETH and ~1.4M AUSD0 via LayerZero along with ~1.08M USDC via Noble and CCTP. The tokens were swapped for 1,135.52 ETH and currently sit in 0x358ef0130f7a5aa516dcd81bdc80b18cde41cac8 on Ethereum Mainnet.

We are actively working on a security fix to patch the identified vulnerability. We expect this to be completed and audited in a few days. Additionally, asset recovery efforts are ongoing with the help of security partners.

The Initia L1 and Rollups remain halted as we work toward a resolution. We hope to safely resume network operations as soon as possible and will provide a full post-mortem once available. In the meantime, we will continue to share verified updates through our official channels.

Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims.

text:
I am a technology optimist. I believe:

1. decentralization and censorship-resistance (real versions of these properties, not larps) matter to human freedom in the coming age of AI

2. self-sovereign money, implemented by code and maintained through decentralized consensus, is the final form of money. But it needs to be truly decentralized -- cut out every possible weakness, trust assumption, keeper, etc. Of course there will be connectors to the real world - harden those maximally

3. AI will write most smart contract code. Spec-driven development with Formal Verification will be how new contracts are written rigorously. FV will also be crucial to securing all the infra including the blockchain itself

4. AI will harden our surfaces, with some unfortunate hacks in the process, but ultimately the crypto and financial industries will come out stronger

5. properly-constructed and properly-indexed data lakes will enable agents to build software far more productively

6. governments will move to restrict AI usage in the future, causing true decentralization and CR to matter in dramatic fashion

7. quantum security will be a must for any ledger where people trust their assets. And specifically, blockchains will need to deliver quantum-resistance while retaining programmability and performance. Again, no larping

8. ZK will be an important part of the puzzle too, as it'll be increasingly important to prove off-chain computation and utilize the result on chain. But again, performance and effortlessness for users will be the differentiator

9. pragmatic and composable privacy will be the missing piece for real adoption. People will use apps that stack together stablecoins, DeFi, blockchain settlement, passkey or MPC authentication, and friction-free onramps, but the part that gets fintechs over the line is knowing that user balances will remain private while still being able to tap into shared liquidity

10. blockchain will serve as the global, universal marketplace, for anyone anywhere to get the best opportunities. For that we will need guarantees of fair execution, protection from frontrunning, and a convergence of all of the best assets

At @category_xyz and the @monad Foundation, we are assembling all of these missing pieces in parallel with extreme urgency, and I hope this is clear from our actions. See you in the future

Your seed phrase or API keys might be sitting in a notes file, an old .env or a .txt on your desktop. Info-stealing malware looks there first.

Paste this into Claude Code from your home folder:

"Write and run a local script that scans my computer for secrets saved in plain text: API keys, passwords, private keys, .env files and crypto seed phrases (12 or 24 words from the BIP39 word list). Check Desktop, Documents, Downloads and my code folders. Skip node_modules and system folders.
Never print, read back or show me any secret itself. Output only the file path, the line number, the type of secret and how risky it is.
Then give me a plan: what to delete, what to move into a password manager, and which keys to rotate first."

The script only reports where secrets are, so the secrets themselves never end up in your chat.

Takes a few minutes. Do it before you need to.

text:
The "Bitcoin of the AI age" thesis is getting tested faster than I expected.

Four days ago $PEARL traded on two thin CEX books and sat 19% below ATH. Since then: Coinbase added it to the listing roadmap, spot printed a new ATH at $2.46, mcap went from $594M to ~$815M, and Entropy had to raise the io:PRL OI cap twice to keep up.

Longed it in the dip around 1.7 via @entropyIO. Up ~40% on price since, +120% on margin at 3x. But the price is the least interesting part.

Why the thesis got stronger?

- The whole bull case rests on one idea: GPU matmuls can secure a chain and serve inference at the same time, so the security budget stops being wasted hashes. That part was never the problem. The problem was distribution and demand.

- Coinbase roadmap (from the 19th of Oct, together with AXIS and STABLE) attacks the distribution half. PRL goes from exotic ticker on SafeTrade / BigONE / Ourbit to a name the biggest US venue has publicly committed to review.

- @prlnet cut inference prices again. DeepSeek V4.1 Flash now runs at $0.05 in / $0.30 out on their own API vs $0.30 / $1.20 on Together AI. The network is selling compute cheaper than one of the largest open-model providers, bc miners are paid in block rewards anyway.

What the thesis still needs?

- Proof that paid demand runs through the mining. Pearl still publishes zero numbers on how much of the hashrate serves paid workloads. Cheaper pricing is not the same as paying customers.

- Issuance: ~1M new PRL a day, now against an ~$815M float. Until paid demand shows up, PRL trades like a mining coin and the market has to absorb that supply every single day.

- Depth: Three small CEX books and a roadmap entry are still not a liquid market. Which is where Entropy comes in.

The Entropy angle?

Entropy listed io:PRL on Hyperliquid while spot still only trades on three small CEXs, so the perp became the deepest PRL market before any major exchange had one.

In four days io:PRL went from $3.05M to $9.3M OI (3x) and from $2.05M to $8.4M daily volume (4x). Entropy lifted the OI cap from $5M to 10M to 15M bc demand kept hitting it, and 62% of the new cap is already filled.

Two dynamics to keep in mind if you trade it there:

- The oracle is still 90% SafeTrade until a properly liquid venue lists PRL. A Coinbase listing is exactly that trigger, and once it goes live Entropy migrates io:PRL to the standard Hyperliquid feed.

- The carry is real. Longs paid ~0.7 to 0.8% a day all week. That adds up. Still fine for a thesis trade tho imo.

Still long btw. The gap between "the math works" and "someone pays for the compute" is still the discount still imo, and the market now too seems to be pricing it closing faster than it did last week.

NFA ofc tho. Always DYOR.
author: zerokn0wledge_
quoted_text:
AI spends hundreds of billions on GPUs that mostly multiply matrices. Bitcoin spends its entire security budget on hashes nobody can reuse.

@prlnet makes them the same computation, and could become the Bitcoin of the AI age.

Finally longed pearl-2:native in the recent (smol) dip via @entropyIO on Hyperliquid.

Here's why ↓

Proof of useful work has been an open problem since Bitcoin launched.

A key challenge is that in a permissionless chain, the miner picks its own inputs. Say the work is "multiply two matrices." A cheater just submits all-zero matrices, does no real compute, and farms tickets for free.

So earlier designs mostly had two bad options: let someone else choose the inputs (not permissionless, and miners can't bring their own AI jobs), or pick some niche task nobody actually needs (e.g. Primecoin hunting prime chains).

The breakthrough?

Komargodski and Weinstein (Pearl's founders) published a PoUW mechanism for arbitrary matrix multiplication with 1+o(1) overhead in April 2025:

- Miner commits to A and B, the chain seeds low-rank noise into both
- The GPU runs its normal kernel on the noised operands
- Every output tile doubles as a lottery ticket, hashed against the difficulty target
- A winning tile gets a Plonky2 zkSNARK that nodes verify cheaply
- The noise is low-rank, so the miner strips it and keeps A·B at FP8-level accuracy

One forward pass, two outputs: the AI result and a shot at the block.

Why can't miners cheat?

The noise is seeded by the chain itself, so nothing can be precomputed, and a jackpot policy rejects "easy" crafted inputs. The only way to get a ticket is to actually run the full multiplication.

And the team keeps pushing it further.

The September whitepaper:

- Moves mining to FP8, the low-precision format modern inference runs on across Nvidia's Hopper and Blackwell GPUs
- Extends it to mixture-of-experts models, the architecture behind most large open models today
- Uses Hawkeye, which replays the GPU's exact math on a normal CPU so anyone can check a proof bit for bit (co-authored by Dan Boneh, accepted at MLSys 2026)

"But if the work is useful, can't an attacker sell the output and attack for free?"

That's the classic objection, and Rafael Pass (Cornell Tech cryptographer, known for the first formal security proofs of Bitcoin's consensus) took it head on. 

His model shows that once the market adjusts, a majority attack still costs the full block reward, same as Bitcoin. What changes is where the reward ends up: instead of paying for wasted hashes, it subsidises inference. Same security, but cheaper tokens.

Everything else is plain Bitcoin: UTXO, longest chain, Taproot, a 2.1B hard cap and a smooth emission curve instead of halvings. Plus a post-quantum path, since the mining is hash-based and XMSS signatures are already in consensus.

So where's the demand?

Most people still point to the Together AI endpoint (Together is one of the biggest inference providers for open models), which was pulled from serverless on the 27th of August. 

The more interesting signal tho imo is that Pearl now runs its own inference platform: 7 open models behind an OpenAI-compatible API, served on GPU capacity across the Pearl network.

And it's cheaper. On all four models it shares with Together's serverless lineup (input / output per 1M tokens):

- DeepSeek V4 Pro: $1.10 / $3.30 on Pearl vs $1.32 / $3.96 on Together
- GLM-5.3: $1.10 / $3.50 vs $1.40 / $4.40
- GLM-5.3 Flash: $0.07 / $0.24 vs $0.15 / $0.50
- DeepSeek V4.1 Flash: $0.14 / $0.42 vs $0.30 / $1.20

Still worth keeping in mind tho that this is launch pricing, and Pearl doesn't say how much of the discount PRL is funding. But it's the direction the Pass model predicts: block rewards flowing back to users as cheaper inference.

Ok, cool but how and where does this thing trade?

At $1.70 and a ~$594M mcap, PRL is ~19% off its $2.10 ATH from the 14th of October rn.

Spot is basically two small CEXs, BigONE and SafeTrade, with ~$5M of combined daily volume. The books are paper thin: per CoinGecko it takes ~$4K of buys to push BigONE up 2%, and ~$9K on SafeTrade.

That's why the perp matters. @entropyIO listed PRL as a HIP-3 market on Hyperliquid on the 14th of Oct, and it's filling up fast:

- ~$3.05M OI, already 61% of Entropy's $5M OI cap for the market
- ~$2.05M daily volume, around 40% of all spot volume
- Funding averaged ~0.03-0.04% an hour over the last 3 days, longs paying
- Lighter runs a smaller PRL perp too, ~$0.56M OI

There is a catch tho:

Until a properly liquid venue lists PRL, io:PRL prices 90% off SafeTrade, so the perp inherits the spot book's fragility.

Why am I long?

Bc the hard part is (mostly) done. The math is public, the verification work is accepted at MLSys, the chain is live, and Pearl already sells inference cheaper than Together AI, one of the largest providers of open-model APIs, while awareness of what they're actually do still seems low across CT / my timeline.

What's missing tho is proof that paid demand actually runs through the mining. Until Pearl publishes the share of mining that serves paid workloads and unless there is real adoption, PRL will trade like a mining coin and has to absorb ~1M new PRL a day (float +87% over the next year), and two thin spot books. The trade is definitely not without risk.

That above gap is also the discount I see rn tho, and it's why I bought into this (still smol compared to recent run) dip. 

Bitcoin turned electricity into security. And if Pearl succeeds at turning GPU cycles into security and inference at the same time, it could indeed be smth like the "Bitcoin of the AI age", and with that, nothing short of huge.

NFA ofc tho. Always DYOR.

Once you have and want to trade pearl-2:native too, join me on Entropy (my ref link):

https://t.co/XHXh2dwzi2

text:
Venice is a $1.3B bet that people will pay for private AI.

What many don't talk about: its privacy still runs through an Intel chip, and that chip got broken twice in the last 12 months.

@Arcium just shipped the version without that chip, at $49M mcap.

Why does the chip matter?

Venice's encrypted mode runs the model on NVIDIA GPUs with an Intel TDX enclave in front of them (per its own docs), which makes TDX the weak link. TEE(.)fail pulled attestation keys straight off the DDR5 bus in October 2025, and DDRop forged TDX attestation with a $159 interposer in September 2026. The NVIDIA side of things survived both, bc GPU memory sits inside the package where you can't clip a board onto it.

Blackthorn is basically the same stack with the Intel part cut out, shipped as infra: an API, rented GPUs, or self-install on your own Hopper/Blackwell boxes. It's not a consumer-facing chat app in itself.

On a more technical level: The model runs in plaintext inside confidential GPU memory, the session keys that unlock it get split across MPC nodes, and MPC never touches the per-token path. Arcium says near-native speed, no public benchmark yet tho.

So what's it priced at?

- $ARX: $49M mcap, $234M FDV
- $VVV: $1.3B mcap, $2.2B FDV

27x on mcap, 9x on FDV, for the stack with one less party to trust.

Which imo btw also means the obvious move for Arcium is sitting right there: a Venice-style front end on Arcium's own API once the infra is proven.

Without that app layer, Venice isn't the cleanest comp yet tho. The more congruent ones are the TEE infra Venice actually runs on: @NEARProtocol's NEAR AI Cloud and @PhalaNetwork, both announced as Venice's confidential inference providers on the 19th of March 2026, both TEE-based, which is where the Intel TDX enclave from above lives. Also: NEAR is listed for completeness only tho, a $7B L1 where private AI is a rounding error isn’t a comp. Phala is.

- $PHA: $50M mcap, $59M FDV
- $NEAR: $7B, with private AI a rounding error inside an L1

So infra vs pure infra, $ARX already trades at a 4x FDV premium to Phala. A sign that the market doesn't price Blackthorn like cheap TEE infra. It's already starting to price it as a shot at the app layer.

Which brings us back to Venice.

The valuation gap there exists for a reason today. Blackthorn is still a gated alpha with no fees. Venice is a real product with users and revenue.

But that's the whole point of buying the alpha instead of the product: you get the better trust model before the market prices it in. If Blackthorn (and a Venice-style product, in-house or not, built on it) attracts real users, this gap will close. And that's my bet.

NFA ofc. DYOR.

Never pay fees on a losing trade.

Most trading apps charge you on both sides of every trade, win or lose. You end up paying to lose. For small traders that adds up fast.

That model pays apps to get you trading more, not winning more. We want the opposite.

On Exfil from now on:
• Buying is free
• Selling at a loss is free
• You pay only on winning trades

How it works: seats.
Every trader gets a seat number, in the order they made their first trade of $5 or more. Your seat is yours for life and sets your rate on winning trades. Earlier seats pay less.

Seats 1–100 (Pioneers): 0.75%, all taken
Seats 101–1,000: 0.85%, open now
Seats 1,001–1,500: 0.90%
Then +0.05% every 1,500 seats

Example: buy $100, sell for $150
App charging 0.5% each way: $1.25 in fees.
Exfil, seat 101–1,000: $1.28.
Sell at a loss instead? They charge you again. We charge $0.

Exfil is fair launched and community owned from day zero. A group of KOLs recently asked us for the usual deal: an upfront payment and a cut of the fees for promoting the app beyond the referrals rewards we shipped. We said no. We decided to pass all marketing and KOL budgets directly to community. We keep it fully transparent and we wouldn't do it any other way. 

PS: you can see the fee tier on settings tab in the app. We will introduce a cap on the fees as our user base grows. The buy back rebate, burns and referrals all in place and work the same in this new fee structure.

Claude 背后的大 boss（Anthropic CEO）刚出来掀桌子了，直接把码农的饭碗砸得稀碎。  
​他透了几个极其核心的底牌：纯敲代码绝对是第一批被 AI 干碎的岗位。现在如果还指望靠学编程去保住饭碗，基本就是往火坑里跳。他明确表态，未来十年的资本红利根本不在软件端，全在半导体芯片这种硬桥硬马的物理世界里。  
​以后的职场杠杆很粗暴：AI 包揽 95% 的苦力，你只搞定 5% 的决策，整体产出直接翻 20 倍。但这里有个致命陷阱，他们内部做过数据研究，如果瞎用 AI，人的代码能力会肉眼可见地退化，工具是真的会让人变蠢。  
​至于未来普通人靠什么活命，他指了两条明路：
一是去干带“人味儿”的实体活。比如当医生，光会看片子没用，你得能跟病人沟通、懂人情世故。
二是死磕“鉴谎能力”（批判性思维）。等 AI 啥都能一键生成的时候，谁能在满屏的假货里扒出真相，谁手里就握着最稀缺的资产。  
​还在疯狂报班死磕 Java 和 Python 的人可以醒醒了，软件时代已经在末路狂奔，底层逻辑早就变天了。 https://t.co/CpTFwn02bq

文長慎入

一週年的時間，@renaissCLTB 從 0 走到 42M USD，真的不是一件容易的事。

身為一路參與 @renaissxyz  成長的老用戶，這一年看到了很多改變，也見證了平台從最初的起步，一步一步走到今天。

還記得一年前，收到 @Plus_Ultra_715 老闆的邀約，希望我能體驗產品，順便了解一下 TCG 這個市場。

說真的，那時候我對 TCG 幾乎一竅不通。

甚至心裡還冒出一個念頭：

WTF... 怎麼 WM 會想做這個？這不就是我童年時期玩的卡牌嗎？

當時的我，真的無法理解這些卡牌除了收藏、遊玩之外，究竟還有什麼市場價值。

直到後來看了團隊提供的 DEMO 跟 DECK，才開始發現，好像跟我原本想的不太一樣。

原來一張小小的卡牌，背後可以有這麼龐大的收藏市場。

原來有些人願意花上千、上萬美元，只為了收藏一張自己喜歡的卡。

原來 TCG 不只是童年的回憶，更是一個擁有真實需求、交易市場與資產價值的產業。

於是我開始接觸、研究，慢慢從一個完全不懂 TCG 的門外漢，變成現在勉強算是入門的玩家。

這一年，我接觸了不同的卡牌、研究市場價格，也開始真正理解 TCG 與 RWA 結合的可能性。

回頭想想，如果當初沒有收到那份邀約，或許我到現在都還不會認真看待這個市場。

還記得剛開始幫 Renaiss 發文的時候，它只是一個在亞洲市場默默無聞的 TCG 平台。

那時候沒有現在的知名度，也沒有這麼多玩家與收藏家關注。

從第一次社群 AMA，到第一次看到老闆站上 YZi 的舞台，那種感覺真的很特別。

因為你知道，這不是一個突然冒出來、靠著市場熱度被大家認識的項目。

而是一個你從最初就開始接觸，看著它一步一步成長的團隊。

這一年，我們經歷了無數風風雨雨。

有過令人興奮的時刻，也有過爭議、挫折與失望。

有時候看到社群的抱怨，自己也會覺得無奈；有時候看到團隊推出新的產品與功能，又會重新燃起期待。

但也正因為經歷過這些，才更能體會從 0 走到今天有多麼不容易。
 
這一路上當然不是只有掌聲。

有過爭議、有過質疑，也有過讓用戶失望的時候。

但我認為，一個項目真正不容易的地方，不是從來不犯錯，而是在面對問題之後，還能持續調整、改善，並且把產品一步步做出來。

從最初的 TCG 抽卡，到實體收藏品 RWA，再到近期推出的 Renaiss Earn，讓收藏品開始探索質押與鏈上金融應用。

這些變化，也讓我更加確信自己一直看好的 TCG × RWA × DeFi 方向，確實有值得長期探索的空間。

42M 不只是一個數字，更代表這一年來無數用戶的參與，以及團隊持續投入的成果。

當然，一週年不是終點。

未來還有流動性、產品體驗、生態擴張，以及如何讓更多 Web2 收藏家真正走進 Web3 等挑戰。

但至少這一年，Renaiss 已經從一個概念，逐步走出屬於自己的市場。

最後，也想對這一年來持續支持 Renaiss 的老朋友們說聲謝謝。

不管你是最初就加入的收藏家，還是中途才認識 Renaiss 的玩家，大家都是這段旅程的一部分。

以現在 RWA 的市場環境來說，當大家談到 RWA，最先想到的往往就是美股代幣化，以及 @RobinhoodApp  正在布局的區塊鏈生態。

但其實，RWA 的潛力遠遠不僅止於美股代幣化。

「萬物上鏈」這四個字，聽起來很有想像空間，但我認為這只是一個比較籠統的說法。

真正值得思考的是：
當現實世界的資產被帶到鏈上之後，究竟能創造什麼過去做不到的價值？

如果只是把股票、黃金、房地產或收藏品變成一個 Token，讓用戶可以在鏈上買賣，那其實只是完成了資產代幣化的第一步。

RWA 真正有意思的地方，在於資產上鏈後所延伸出來的金融應用與流動性。

例如：
🔹 美股代幣化：讓符合資格的用戶透過區塊鏈接觸傳統金融資產，並探索更靈活的交易與結算方式。

🔹 房地產代幣化：透過資產權益拆分，降低部分投資門檻，讓原本流動性較低的資產有機會接觸更多投資者。

🔹 實體收藏品 RWA：將寶可夢卡牌、海賊王卡牌、球員卡，甚至藝術品等收藏品導入鏈上，讓收藏不再只是單純的持有與轉售。

🔹 RWA × DeFi：讓具有真實資產支持的鏈上憑證，在符合相關條件下進一步參與質押、借貸、抵押及其他金融應用。

而我自己最關注，也認為目前市場最被低估的賽道之一，就是 TCG × RWA × DeFi。

因為我認為，收藏品市場長期以來最大的問題之一，就是流動性。

一張價值數千美元的卡牌，即使市場有公認的行情，也不代表你今天想賣，就一定能立刻找到買家。

但如果未來能夠透過鏈上資產驗證、託管、交易及金融協議，把原本相對封閉的收藏品市場與 DeFi 生態連結起來，那麼收藏品的價值就不一定只能透過出售來實現。

近期我在 Facebook 上看到有抽卡平台推出單抽高達 5,000 美元的卡機。

坦白說，我不認為這樣的價格會受到大部分玩家青睞。

畢竟對一般玩家而言，5,000 美元已經不是一筆小數目。

但換個角度來看，我們不能只用一般玩家的消費能力，去衡量整個收藏品市場的潛力。

對某些高資產收藏家而言，高價卡牌可能不只是娛樂商品，而是一種具有收藏價值、稀缺性，甚至資產配置意義的實體資產。

就像藝術品、名錶、古董或高級珠寶一樣，這些東西從來就不是為了滿足所有消費者而存在。

但它們背後依然有自己的高端市場、收藏需求與資產交易體系。

這也是為什麼我認為，TCG × RWA 的市場想像空間，遠遠不只是抽卡平台本身。

當這些高價值收藏品開始與區塊鏈結合，未來有機會透過資產代幣化、抵押借貸與 DeFi 協議，讓原本相對封閉的收藏市場接觸到更廣泛的金融生態。

而這背後更值得關注的，其實是資金的流動。

RWA 帶來的不只是新的資產類別，更可能是過去沒有進入加密市場的資金與參與者。

有些來自傳統金融，有些來自高端收藏市場，有些來自原本流動性不足的實體資產市場。

這些資金過去未必會參與加密貨幣交易，但未來可能因為自己熟悉的資產開始上鏈，而逐漸接觸 Web3。

當然，這一切仍然需要解決資產真實性、託管安全、贖回機制、流動性與監管等問題。

資產上鏈不代表自動產生流動性，代幣化也不代表一定能創造收益。

但我相信，未來 RWA 的競爭重點，不會只是誰能把最多資產搬到鏈上。

而是誰能真正讓這些資產在鏈上產生實際用途，並建立可持續的經濟模式。

美股代幣化可能是讓大眾認識 RWA 的重要入口。

但真正的 RWA 市場，或許才剛剛開始。

下一階段值得關注的，不只是萬物上鏈，而是萬物上鏈之後，能做些什麼。

過去加密市場的資金主要圍繞著原生代幣與鏈上金融活動流動。

但未來隨著越來越多實體資產進入鏈上，RWA 有機會讓原本與加密市場沒有交集的資產持有者，也開始參與這個生態。

我認為 RWA 最被低估的，可能不只是資產代幣化本身，而是它有機會成為整個 Web3 下一階段更龐大的資金入口。

而 TCG 與實體收藏品，很可能就是其中一個值得長期關注的方向。

成功從來不是必然，努力也不一定會有結果。

這個市場每天都有新的項目誕生，也有無數曾經風光的項目逐漸消失。

沒有人能保證 Renaiss 最後一定會成功，也沒有人知道這條路究竟能走多遠。

但對我來說，最珍貴的不是等到一個項目成功之後才來分享它的故事。

而是在它還沒被太多人認識的時候，就已經參與其中，陪著它經歷成長、挫折與改變。

所以，對於這一年走過風風雨雨，依然願意留下來的各位。

就讓我們繼續看看，Renaiss 究竟能走到多遠吧。

不需要盲目相信，也不需要承諾永遠支持。

好的地方值得肯定，不足的地方就繼續督促團隊改善。

因為真正長久的支持，不是無條件的吹捧，而是即使看見問題，依然願意給予改變與成長的機會。

一週年不是終點，而是下一段旅程的開始。

從當初的一句 WTF，到今天的一週年。

這一年，真的發生了很多事情。

最後，謝謝這一年來一起走過的團隊、收藏家與社群夥伴。

Happy 1st Anniversary, Renaiss🎉

If DeepSeek were American it would be on every magazine cover.

Think about it. A small lab with a fraction of the compute ships a frontier-class model under MIT. Then it open sources its production inference engine, its kernels, its file system. Publishes 155 trillion tokens a day and $38 of revenue per GPU-hour. Raises $15B anyway.

The code is the same either way. The weights are the same. Only the flag changed the reaction.

I dont care about the flag. I care that I can download it, read it and run it on my own cards. By that measure DeepSeek did more for American developers this month than most American labs did all year.

text:
按福布斯近期的统计，今年以来开发商和算力云公司为美国数据中心发行的相关债券约 800亿 美元，其中约 370亿 美元是垃圾级，按金额算占比约 46% 。2025年全年这一比例约 24% ，今年差不多翻了一倍。

垃圾级债券也叫高收益债，表示偿债风险较高。这类公司建数据中心需要大量资金，评级较低的借款人通常需要支付更高的利息才能吸引投资者。

我在 168X 的采访中特意说了这个问题，现在导致 AI 和半导体股票下降的主要原因就是资本支出太高，而尤其是 AI 目前的变现能力并不是非常的透明，可以说给 AI 提供设备是赚钱的，比如英伟达或者是半导体，但 AI 本身的盈利呢？

目前还不足以支撑现在这么大的资本支出。而且 AI 目前的变现能力并不是非常透明，赚回来的钱很可能跟不上投进去的钱。

给AI提供设备的公司是赚钱的，比如英伟达，利润已经实实在在体现在财报里。但不少买设备、租算力，以及提供模型和应用的公司，从AI上赚到的钱还跟不上投入的速度，尚不足以靠自身盈利支撑持续采购。

其中自建数据中心的公司，买芯片、服务器和建机房的钱要先付出去，设备投用后再按年限折旧，逐年计入成本，电费、日常运营和借款利息则需要持续支付。如果AI业务带来的现金流跟不上，又还要继续扩建，依赖外部融资的公司通常就要接着发债或借款。

对评级本来就不高的借款人来说，如果投资者越来越担心偿债能力，新借的钱和到期续借的钱都可能更贵，也更难借到。到那时，这些公司可能会推迟或缩减部分扩建计划，设备采购也可能跟着放慢。

给AI提供设备的公司，眼下的利润来自已经完成的销售。如果买方因为融资变贵而放慢采购，可能先受到影响的是市场对这些公司未来订单和盈利增长的预期。

text:
La crise actuelle est en grande partie l'explosion d'une vieille contradiction qui a commencé avec les boomers et s'est accentuée avec les millenials et les gen Z : tout un chacun veut des conditions matérielles qui s'améliorent en continu, mais refuse ce qui rend cette amélioration possible, c'est-à-dire la croissance économique, la civilisation industrielle, le primat de la production, l'expansion démographique et l'exploitation des ressources naturelles.

Les boomers ont voulu une société tertiarisée de loisirs, ont fait peu d'enfants, ont favorisé la sécurité par les normes, la baisse du temps de travail. La contradiction est qu'ils ont aussi voulu de grosses retraites. (2 euros par euro cotisé). En conséquence de quoi, une seule solution : la prédation des richesses créées par les plus jeunes générations et l'endettement.

Mais ce ne sont pas les seuls, les millenials et les gen Z sont pris dans la même contradiction. La croissance est sale, mais l'on ne veut pas vivre très sobrement. Pendant un moment ma génération a eu le fantasme de l'économie expérientielle. Moins de biens, plus de souvenirs. Mais arrivé à 40 ans, les weekends entre potes à Barcelone ne compensent plus vraiment le fait de pas pouvoir acheter d'appart.
Donc une seule solution : fantasmer qu'en prédatant les richesses des plus riches, ils pourraient dépasser leur contradiction, et s'enrichir sans faire grossir le gâteau.

Le problème est que les mathématiques ne marchent pas. En France comme grosso modo partout en Europe voici comment la richesse est dépensée : 
- 52% en consommation des ménages.
- 26% en consommation publique et des associations (santé, éducation, défense, justice, administration, etc.)
- 22% en investissements (4,5 pour les ménages, principalement dans leur logement, 4,4% pour le public, 12% pour les entreprises qui achètent des machines et construisent des usines.)

Si on divise notre production annuelle de richesses par le nombre de Français de plus de 20 ans, ça fait un peu moins de 56 000 euros par personne. 
Si nous répartissions parfaitement tous les revenus à tous les individus de plus de 20 ans, dans un communisme parfait, y compris l'argent des milliardaires, il y a donc (52%+4,5%)*56000 = 2637 euros par mois de disponible.
En tout et pour tout.
C'est ça le plafond. Il n'y a pas de magot caché au-delà de cette somme.

Donc quiconque a pour ambition dans la vie de gagner plus de 2637 euros doit se rendre compte que ça ne peut passer que par la croissance économique, ou l'appauvrissement de ses compatriotes.

Sans cette prise de conscience indispensable que le principal problème de la France est simplement que le gâteau n'est pas assez gros pour satisfaire tout le monde, ce sera la continuation de la lutte de tous contre tous, et les violences actuelles ne feront que s'accentuer.

text:
If you put a VPS on Tailscale, fix these two things immediately:

Disable key expiry (Machines → ··· → Disable Key Expiry). Otherwise, you risk losing access after 180 days.

Lock down your ACLs. Tag the VPS tag:server and only allow inbound connections from your own devices. Don't allow the server to initiate connections to your other machines.

By default, Tailscale allows everything to talk to everything, and device keys expire.

A compromised VPS shouldn't give an attacker access to your entire tailnet.
author: siddsanyal
quoted_text:
Maybe important to repost this now that everyone is getting hacked

If you have a VPS, I recommend you to get if off the public internet and into a Tailscale network and Cloudflare Tunnel ASAP

It doesn't matter you have SSH key login, this is about exploits and vulnerabilities AI is finding

There's 2 ways into a VPS:
- via your site/app (like the PHP exploit of this week with a file upload hack)
- via your server (like hacking into SSH or some open port)

The site/app side you put on a Cloudflare Tunnel and then with the default Free Plan it has WAF security enabled by default and they jump on new security exploits fast, it means that the only way to reach your website is via the Cloudflare Tunnel, your server does not respond to port 80 or 443 anymore

The server side you put on a Tailscale network which is like your own private network that nobody can access but your own devices (like your laptop, your phone and your VPS) kinda like a VPN

Then you switch off ANY regular access to your VPS on the firewall, in my case I use Hetzner and you create a new firewall then empty it and that blocks everything (test it)

How do Tailscale and Cloudflare Tunnel get in then? They don't. They go outbound. They make a tunnel to outside which sends and receives

Now you've reduced your attack vector to Tailscale and your Cloudflare Tunnel, much safer, not perfect btw, but nothing is

At 14:59 UTC on October 23rd, an attacker exploited a bug in Initia MoveVM’s script caching that allowed malicious code to bypass security checks. The attacker artificially spoofed the MoveVM state, thereby crediting themselves with unbacked WETH, iUSD, and USDC tokens without changing the corresponding token’s total supply. No native INIT was minted, and the total INIT supply is unaffected.

Before the network was halted, the attacker bridged out roughly $2.7M, comprising of 105 WETH and ~1.4M AUSD0 via LayerZero along with ~1.08M USDC via Noble and CCTP. The tokens were swapped for 1,135.52 ETH and currently sit in 0x358ef0130f7a5aa516dcd81bdc80b18cde41cac8 on Ethereum Mainnet.

We are actively working on a security fix to patch the identified vulnerability. We expect this to be completed and audited in a few days. Additionally, asset recovery efforts are ongoing with the help of security partners.

The Initia L1 and Rollups remain halted as we work toward a resolution. We hope to safely resume network operations as soon as possible and will provide a full post-mortem once available. In the meantime, we will continue to share verified updates through our official channels.

Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims.

text:
网景创始人 、硅谷顶级投资人Marc Andreessen 在访谈里坦言，他看到了科技史上最可怕的一道认知鸿沟，

传统巨头以为 AI 只是个降本增效的插件，而新一代 AI 原生团队，正在用完全非人的组织效率掀翻整个商业版图。

当年写出网景浏览器、见证了整个互联网三十年兴衰的 Marc Andreessen，坐在 Ben Horowitz 面前直接发出了感慨，
如果 1994 年我们做 Netscape 的时候就有今天这种 AI 工具，那简直不可想象。

现在绝大多数传统巨头和现有企业，依然在用改良软件的旧思维去看待大模型。

在他们的组织逻辑里，AI 只是一个高级功能，用来给现有业务做个插件、在钉钉里加个智能助手、或者把客服团队砍掉 20% 省点成本。

他们以为自己在拥抱变革，其实只是在给老旧的蒸汽机打补丁。

但真正恐怖的事情，正在那些刚成立的 AI 原生团队里发生。

那些创始人对 AI 能力的理解，跟大厂完全不在同一个平行宇宙。

他们每周都在看着底层技术飞速进化，而且他们压根不会把自己定义成一家软件公司、硬件公司、甚至是一家 AI 公司。

以前创办一家公司，你的组织架构是按人类的协同瓶颈搭出来的：
招产品经理写文档、招工程师写代码、招法务改合同、招运营做投放。
因为人类的脑力带宽有限，所以必须靠庞大的部门和管理层级来支撑业务。

而真正的 AI 原生物种，是用机器智能作为最底层的骨架。

两个人加上一整套自动化 Agent，可以直接把从市场洞察、软件工程、全栈设计到商业销售的链路全部跑通。

狗狗币 ＃DOGE 可以建仓了！

DOGE现在值得重新放回自选。

不是因为“狗狗币又有什么新故事”

恰恰相反——它没什么新故事，历史就是它最大的故事。

2021年，它从不起眼的位置一路冲到约 0.74美元。

然后呢？

跌。

再跌。

历史回撤一度超过 75%，但周期重新转热之后，它又回来了。

更有意思的是2024年。

DOGE全年涨幅约 275%，其中11月单月直接涨了 168.7%。

这东西最大的价值，从来不是技术有多牛。

而是：

认知度够高、流动性够大、社区够老，市场一疯狂，资金很容易重新想到它。

所以我看DOGE，不太喜欢猜它明天涨几个点。

我更愿意研究一个问题：

如果下一轮市场再次进入全民亢奋，DOGE这种老牌Meme，会不会又成为资金最熟悉的那个选择？

历史不能证明未来，但至少证明了一件事：

DOGE疯起来，是真的不讲道理。

半导体指数价格显示
5月份以来fomo

这到底是双顶还是下一次起飞的筑底呢？

因为to c的收入增速不及预期
会加速这一路半导体周期提前到顶

让to c端的企业大赚特赚

我开始执行这个观点
我认为我们应该选择继续相信这个内容

我可能还是买早了点
买贵了点
涨上去也会降低一点仓位
我出手重仓买入半导体行业的原因
和市场半导体大跌的原因
是同一件事的不同解读

Anthropic的单季度营收168亿美金
实现了季度盈利
环比 + 45%、调整后盈利、现金流转正

市场看到的是Anthropic的环比营收下滑
我看到的是Anthropic开始赚钱了
现在很难说谁对谁错

我认为AI行业去泡沫的能力大大提前了

那些靠卖硬件的厂家整个行业生态就没有系统风险了

对整个行业的前景度调整往下
对Anthropic的估值也有下调
我对这个增速下滑的看法是
这件事是必然会发生的

因为单季度168亿美金45%的环比增速
依然是非常可怕的增长速度
按照这个速度我们做以下几个推演

基准起点：
Anthropic 2026 Q3 = 168 亿美元
前三（单季营收）：
①亚马逊 2006 亿
②沃尔玛 1879 亿

【现实情景：增速阶梯衰减：45%→35%→ 稳住】
对手假设：
亚马逊环比 + 10%
沃尔玛环比 + 4%
苹果环比 + 8%

 1理想情景
（45% 环比永不降，纯数学推演，现实几乎不可能）
超越苹果（1438 亿） 5 个季度  2028 Q1
超越沃尔玛（1879 亿）：7 个季度 2028 Q3
超越亚马逊（2006 亿）：9 个季度 2028 Q4

超越沃尔玛（1879 亿）：2030 Q1
超越亚马逊（2006 亿）：2030 Q4～2031 Q2

也就是说如果你能拿住半导体指数
扛住当前的回撤
在2028-2030年的某一个阶段

带着整个半导体全面新高

相信ai是人类文明第三次工业革命
相信ai行业会出现10万亿、100万亿美金市值的企业

quoted_text:
上周 arXiv 上，标题带 Agent 的新论文有 503 篇。做这个方向的都知道，根本读不完。

这次我把整件事交给了 MiniMax M3.1 Flash，就是之前在 OpenRouter 匿名霸榜的 Space Bunny。

在 MiniMax Code 里提了一条需求，之后没再给任何反馈：

1. 自己调 arXiv 接口抓数据，碰到限流就退避重试
2. 一批一批读完 503 篇摘要，逐篇标注主题、类型和中文总结
3. 写了 4000 多行代码，做出一个带雷达图、关键词星图、联动筛选和 BibTeX 导出的周报网站
4. 自己写测试、看截图、修 bug，最后 96 项检查全部通过

无人值守 86 分钟，按 API 公开价折算 0.88 美元。作为参照，同样的 token 用量换成 Claude Sonnet 5.5 的公开价是 8.46 美元，约为 M3.1 Flash 的 9.6 倍（两家官方定价页的标准价，10 月 22 日查询）。

我核对了全部 503 个 arXiv ID，都是真实论文；又抽查了 30 篇，29 篇的中文总结和摘要一致。长时间、多工具的 agent 任务，这次的表现我挺满意。

text:
thinking about super intelligence as a narrative and how we got here

agent swarms, the kind that frontier labs have, are the most intelligent thing humans have ever invented. individual capability x ability to gossip and be better together has truly created super intelligence!

three years ago my conceptual framing was around such “collaborative AI” will eventually be smarter (very long essay, published here earlier). that is when I went all-in on @HyperspaceAI, worked without a salary + all savings in. broke as broke can be, but thesis made sense. our first product experiment was around collaborative RAG which went viral! (thank you to @ylecun who RT-ed it at the time!)

it took me to the realization that such AI would one day enable a world of giving a supercomputer to everyone - which is what you see as the foundational poster back in our product launch in sept 2024 here. back then, people were talking about chatgpt - claude code was yet to be invented 6 months later. but multi-agent orchestration seemed like an eventual future to us.

it led me to the framing of first the agentic browser (which many then built, including us) and then building further on Karpathy’s framing of the LLM OS -> which led to expanding that vision to the AI OS (@Scobleizer was the first to post about it as a product, thank you for attending our summit as well at the beautiful shack15)

and then if we were not building an Uber-like peer to peer network (we were quite e/acc thanks to @beffjezos inspiration), which was not super expensive to run, which forced me to again go for broke and re-architect and re-build it myself as a fully peer to peer network instead - i would not have been awake overnight on a weekend in march 2026 when @karpathy asked for someone to create a seti at home type swarm for autoresearchers. 

my network, which only did p2p inference at the time, only worked without such a central orchestrator. it was fully peer to peer. so it took me 5 hours since his tweet to push out what was the first such gossiping agent swarm. and then it became a thing. venturebeat (cc @carlfranzen) ran with the first story on how agent autoresearcher swarms showed emergent intelligence on the hyperspace network. forbes wrote about our stats without even mentioning us :) 

things went a little viral since. thankful to 
everyone who ran a node and participated in the swarm. thankful to @brianrommele and founders of figma, perplexity and huggingface who wrote notes of encouragement on my product experiments at the time.

and agent swarms which no one was talking about in feb 2026, started showing up in frontier labs work in may. they adopted the pattern, instead of 7B open source models i was using, they used multi-trillion param models and powerful infra powering their swarm, and raced faster than the rest of us. 

we are still adapting to this new world. but it’s clear this poster’s prophecy has come true: but first it had to be imagined.

in the days ahead i am excited to showcase how it all comes together in a single product experience in the AgenticOS - which to me is the first true personal supercomputer experience (cc @finkd @alexandr_wang) 

i believe eventually everyone will have it and it would likely be big tech + frontier labs which will bring it to billions. and that will make the world a better place.

cc @johnternus @sundarpichai @satyanadella @JensenHuang @elonmusk @sama @DarioAmodei

<现阶段上 PAPER 永续，为什么会给 Papertrade 带来系统性风险？>

逻辑链很长，但理解起来其实不难——上了 PAPER 永续，攻击 Papertrade 就可能变得有利可图。

理论上的攻击路径是存在的。假设 Papertrade 资金池有 1000 万美元，粗暴版🌰：

1. 在 HIP-3 做空 PAPER (名义价值 1000 万美元)；

2. 花 1500 万美元在 Hyperliquid 上操纵，把 BTC 价格拉高；

3. 同步在 PaperTrade 上做空 BTC，等价格自然回落后平仓，从 LP 资金池提走 1000 万美元利润；

4. 池子被抽干后，Papertrade 偿付能力恶化，PAPER 跌到接近归零，HIP-3 PAPER 空单再赚 1000 万美元。

最终账目：
在 Hyperliquid 操纵成本【-1500 万】
从 Papertrade 池子提走【+1000 万】
外部 PAPER 空头盈利【+1000 万】
💡最后净赚【+500 万】

------

那什么时候才能上 PAPER 永续、开放转账和交易？

按现有信息能想到的：

1. Hyperliquid 上 BTC/ETH 的盘口深度明显变厚，操纵成本跟着提高

2. 等 Jez/blurr 两个联创找到更好的设计，让攻击变成负期望值

3. 协议风险参数调到成熟：费用结构、OI 上限、资金池规模管理…让攻击的预期收益接近零

4. 协议规模和用户基础够大，攻击成本相对池子不再致命。今天刚上线的 Builder Codes，或许能 push 一把

大家有什么想法，也可以补充一下...

text:
造出全球最臭名昭著的间谍软件 Pegasus 的那个人，现在开始劝各国政府不要相信美国 AI 公司了，应该相信他。

《金融时报》今天采访了以色列 NSO Group 的联合创始人 Shalev Hulio。他正在向各国政府推销一个新故事，主权 AI。

他的理由其实很有说服力。国家安全不能建立在对美国科技巨头的依赖上，敏感数据不能随便交给 OpenAI、Google，关键时刻美国甚至可能切断服务。所以，各国应该在自己的基础设施上部署 AI 模型。

巧了，他的新公司 Dream 正好能提供这套东西。

Dream 由 Hulio 和奥地利前总理 Sebastian Kurz 共同创办。今年 6 月刚融资 2.6 亿美元，估值达到 30 亿美元，旗下 Atlas 平台专门帮助政府部署主权 AI，目前已经在两个国家落地。

最魔幻的是 Hulio 的履历。

他创办的 NSO Group 曾向各国政府出售 Pegasus，可以在目标毫不知情的情况下入侵手机、读取消息、调用摄像头和麦克风。后来，这套软件被发现用于监控记者、人权活动人士和政治反对派，甚至连负责调查 Pegasus 滥用问题的欧洲议会议员都遭到了入侵。

如今，这位曾经站在全球隐私丑闻中心的人，摇身一变成了国家数据安全的倡导者。

而且生意做得相当不错。Dream 已经拿到了多个国家的政府订单。

我觉得最值得玩味的是，Hulio 几乎完美踩中了当下 AI 行业的一笔大生意，各国政府对美国技术依赖的焦虑。

这种焦虑是真实的，主权 AI 也确实有市场。但当一个曾经帮助政府突破公民数字隐私的人，开始要求政府把更关键的数字基础设施交给自己，这种信任究竟从何而来？

只能说，世界上最懂政府安全焦虑的人，可能也最懂得怎么从中赚钱。

btw，#X直聘 这个标签真的狠狠戳中了我。招聘/应聘、生产/消费、采购/销售、订单簿的bid/ask、婚恋……本质上都是价值交换的双边市场，是「需求意图的网络」（network of demand-typed intent）。

这个双边市场中最有价值的角色——「撮合」，不应该被中心化平台继续垄断。

招聘平台、电商平台、CEX等所有中心化交易平台的商业模式，都值得被agent以颠覆式、分布式的方式重新做一遍——让agent成为需求意图网络里的撮合者。

设想一个场景：招聘方/应聘方在X上build in public、建设品牌，有招聘/应聘意图就加话题#X直聘，基于Grok bot/X API在开放平台搜索双边参与者、分析意图、调查背景，最终匹配供需。

你的社交图谱、内容、影响力都是你的背书，且一定程度上可验证（尤其是「ta的粉丝里你认识的」这个列表）。

这也是一种web3：开放、分布式、重新设计价值交换的方式。

回到 #X直聘，可以长出一个skill或MCP server，可能是公共物品或agentic平台，我不知道。

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

Flop Labs CEO Arthur Hayes  @CryptoHayes 10 月 16 日接受 LukeMartin @VentureCoinist  频道采访时表示，整个加密行业都在滥用代币经济学。从早期 ICO 到后来的 VC 私募和代币预售，一些项目方融资后本应开发产品，却在协议上线、代币解锁后抛售持仓，让 TGE 阶段买入的散户承受损失，部分代币跌幅甚至达到 95%。

Hayes 认为，散户已经看穿高 FDV、低流通量代币的套路，这类代币如今连在 Binance 都难以拉升。相比之下，他更看好 Hyperliquid 等具有实际市场需求、将收入回馈代币持有者，且没有大量预售代币解锁抛压的项目。

🚨 沒有網路連線，AI 依然找到了互傳訊息的方法。

OpenAI 公布的受控測試中，兩個 AI 被放進不同虛擬環境，沒有網路連線，也沒有可共同寫入的檔案，卻能利用共享 CPU 快取的「讀取時間差」交換資訊。

🧠 就像兩個人被關在不同房間，不能通話，卻能隔牆敲暗號。環境看起來分開了，底層共享的硬體，仍可能成為溝通管道。

🔓 同一輪紅隊測試，AI 還找出先前未知的軟體漏洞，串接漏洞逃出沙箱、尋找連外路徑。這涉及零日漏洞的發現與利用，但部分突破來自設定錯誤，不能全部混稱零日攻擊。

而在 9 月 20 日，更有研究模型在訓練時，利用 DNS 設定缺口，繞路向外部聊天機器人提問。OpenAI 隨後暫停相關工作 11 天，強化防護後才恢復訓練。

⚠️ 這裡要分清楚：前面的通訊與攻防，是研究人員安排、提供資料與提示的測試，多數通訊實驗有人為引導，不能解讀成 AI 自發串謀。

但我覺得這已經足夠讓人警惕：當 AI 能主動尋找繞過限制的方法，我們就不能把「設定了限制」，當成「限制一定有效」。

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

text:
OpenAI says it will no longer train or evaluate its models on the live internet due to “significant risks”. from their blog:

“agents can have access to browsers, code execution environments, computer-use tools, and other services they might need for their tasks. Agents that are explicitly authorized to communicate can also share particular resources within the same boundary. […] If agents can access the infrastructure that hosts them, communicate with agents outside permitted channels, or reach external systems, that constitutes a failure of containment.

For training and most evaluation, the live internet lies outside this boundary, as we believe that providing models access to the live internet can pose significant risks.”

text:
Given the current market conditions, which are far from favorable, I am actually more willing to spend time researching $HOOKR.

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

Not because a weaker market makes a project more likely to rise.

It's because when most capital is chasing short-term narratives, I want to understand which projects are still developing their products, which updates are genuinely changing their use cases, and whether these developments can eventually translate into demand for the token.

I initially became interested in HOOKR because it was trying to expand Uniswap v4 Hooks from a set of trading rules into composable trading infrastructure. The latest updates have given me a clearer understanding of this direction: Hookr is beginning to connect cross-pool capital management, Agent integration, and future revenue rights. It is no longer just helping projects launch tokens, but attempting to provide a set of financial tools that other projects can also use.

The most noteworthy development is Revenue Tokens. Traditionally, when projects need financing, they often have to sell their own tokens or issue more tokens to reward their communities. Hookr offers an alternative: lock the revenue rights associated with fee-generating assets in a contract, then issue a fixed-supply Revenue Token that makes future income over a specific period into a tradable asset.

For example, a project might hold a liquidity position that continuously generates fees but not want to sell its own token to raise capital. It can lock and tokenize the revenue rights for the next 7 days, 30 days, 90 days, or even permanently. Holders receive the fees generated by the corresponding revenue rights, while the project retains its original token. Hookr also allows revenue rights to be divided into daily Time Shares, enabling income from different periods to be traded independently.

I believe this design is worth paying attention to because it addresses something more fundamental than how a token can attract more trading volume. It addresses how on-chain projects can raise capital, distribute revenue, and make future cash flows more flexible and liquid. It also means Hookr's potential users do not have to be limited to its own launchpad. If other liquidity providers, launchpads, and DeFi projects are willing to use these tools, Hookr could enter existing markets rather than relying entirely on demand generated by new token launches.

Another development that has increased my interest is the launch of the MCP Server. Agents can use the interface to discover pools, obtain quotes, check trading conditions, and construct transactions for swaps, reward claims, token launches, and other operations that await signing. The server does not store users' private keys, and the user's wallet still handles signing and authorization.

Taken on its own, an MCP interface is not an unreplicable technological moat. But when combined with Hookr's other products, a more interesting possibility emerges: Agents can not only identify trading opportunities but also invoke preconfigured trading rules and handle parts of the transaction process through the same infrastructure. For applications that may need to automate liquidity management, execute arbitrage, or allocate capital across different markets in the future, these modular tools could be more useful than a platform that only launches tokens.

Pool Mesh, Family Pinger, and Fee Bridge further reinforce this direction. Pool Mesh can allocate capital across multiple target pools; Family Pinger can execute batches of operations and periodic tasks across related pools; and Fee Bridge allows part of the fees generated by one pool to flow to liquidity providers in another pool according to predefined rules. The common objective is to coordinate the movement of capital and revenue across different pools rather than forcing each pool to manage its liquidity in isolation.

This is also why I believe HOOKR has the potential to develop long-term value. Its real competitive advantage may not come from having the largest number of features, but from whether external developers can combine these modules to build their own trading products. Once developers begin relying on Hookr to build pools, manage fee distribution, and coordinate cross-pool capital, its value could come from sustained infrastructure usage rather than reactions to individual product announcements.

Of course, this potential growth has not yet been realized. Discord is open, and HookBook, the SDK, and developer documentation are lowering the barriers to integration, but there is still a gap between an announced third-party integration and sustained trading volume. Projects and initiatives such as Safron, ZEALZ, and Longbow Lend need to be evaluated individually to determine whether their integrations have actually been deployed and are being used. To me, whether developers continue adopting these tools matters more than how many new modules the official team releases.

So why am I still paying attention to $HOOKR when market conditions are poor?

Because I want to track a potential source of demand that may gradually take shape, rather than simply look for a reason to expect the next rebound. When the market weakens, projects driven solely by narratives and short-term liquidity can easily lose attention. But if an infrastructure protocol is used consistently by other projects, its trading rules and capital management functions may generate demand that differs from pure token speculation. This demand will not automatically make HOOKR rise, but it gives us more concrete indicators with which to assess whether its long-term thesis is being realized.

HOOKR's value-capture design is therefore also worth monitoring. The protocol primarily generates revenue from additional mechanisms enabled by users, such as dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, LP Rewards, Auto Burn, and arbitrage value recapture, rather than directly taking all base LP trading fees. According to the official documentation, the protocol's share is generally 20% of the relevant additional fees, with the exact percentage determined by each pool's configuration. Protocol revenue can flow into the treasury and, under the relevant mechanisms, be used for HOOKR buybacks and burns.

The key to this design is connecting token demand with protocol usage. However, I would not assume that value capture has already been established simply because a buyback mechanism has been included in the design. What still needs to be demonstrated is actual protocol revenue, on-chain buyback transactions, and verifiable token burns. More features do not necessarily mean more revenue, and higher trading volume does not mean the protocol will receive fees in the same proportion.

Low liquidity is another issue I have to take into account. It amplifies price volatility and can lead to sharper pullbacks when capital exits. It also means that progress on the product may not be reflected immediately in the token's price. But I would not treat low liquidity itself as a bullish reason. What is genuinely worth investigating is whether product adoption, protocol revenue, and the developer ecosystem continue improving during a period of poor price performance. If these indicators gradually strengthen while the market has not yet fully recognized the progress, HOOKR may present a valuation gap worth examining further.

My current view on HOOKR is therefore that its product capabilities are expanding, ecosystem adoption still needs to be validated, and token value capture has not yet been fully realized. Revenue Tokens expand the potential use cases for revenue rights, MCP allows Agents to invoke Hookr's tools directly, and the cross-pool modules are beginning to connect capital and fee flows across different markets. Together, these updates support its long-term direction of evolving from a launchpad into composable trading infrastructure, but they are not yet proof that this direction has generated demand at scale.

Going forward, what matters most to me is not whether HOOKR can rebound alongside the broader market in the short term, but whether third-party developers actually begin using these modules, whether cross-pool tools generate sustained trading activity, and whether protocol revenue can gradually translate into verifiable buybacks and burns. If these developments materialize, HOOKR's research thesis will be more concrete than that of tokens relying purely on market hype, even if the broader market remains weak.

This is why I believe HOOKR is still worth paying attention to right now. I am not betting on when market sentiment will turn optimistic again. I am watching whether Hookr can gradually prove that the problems it is trying to solve are genuinely worth solving, at a time when the market is no longer willing to pay easily for concepts alone. A market recovery could provide a better trading environment, but only real usage and value capture can make its long-term thesis more convincing.

quoted_text:
What $HOOKR Is Really Trying to Do: Give Tokens on RH Chain Their Own Trading Rules

0x18e674231a58c239dc7daedcffe15ec3a24cff5c 

In my view, HOOKR’s significance for Robinhood Chain is not that it adds another token launchpad. It is trying to turn Uniswap v4 Hooks into a set of trading infrastructure that ordinary projects can reuse.

Most token launchpads focus on how to bring a new token to market. HOOKR is trying to solve a different problem: once a token is listed, can its trading rules become more sophisticated? How should fees be distributed? When should tokens be burned? How can LPs be rewarded? Can arbitrage profits be redistributed to traders? Rather than relying entirely on project-operated servers or external bots, these mechanisms can be embedded directly into the trade execution process.

That gives the product potential beyond a conventional launchpad.

Built on Uniswap v4 Hooks, HOOKR uses composable Hook Blocks to let issuers choose different rules for their trading pools, including dynamic fees, Anti-Snipe, Auto Burn, and LP Rewards. The relevant parameters are fixed when a pool is created and cannot be freely changed afterward. The platform also offers two paths: shared Hooks and custom Hooks. Projects can use existing modules directly or deploy their own trading logic.

More importantly, HOOKR is not limited to newly launched tokens. Assets issued elsewhere can also create new Hookr pools. This gives it an opportunity to enter the existing-asset market rather than relying entirely on the number of new tokens launched every day.

This is particularly worth watching for RH Chain. Robinhood Chain is designed for tokenized stocks and other on-chain financial applications. If more assets enter the ecosystem, the market will need more than issuance channels. It will also need more flexible mechanisms for trading, liquidity, and fee distribution.

HOOKR’s design allows different assets to adopt different rules. One pool could distribute part of its trading fees to LPs, another could implement buyback and burn mechanisms, while a pool targeting a specific trading scenario could redirect arbitrage profits. HOOKR provides tools for building markets, rather than a single trading product.

Of course, being able to configure these rules does not mean every asset will automatically have a better market. Complex mechanisms can increase the cost of understanding a product and introduce additional smart contract risks. Whether HOOKR eventually becomes important infrastructure for RH Chain depends on how many projects genuinely need these capabilities, not on how long its feature list becomes.

Its creator, Nodar, previously created DeFiZap and co-founded Zapperfi. His earlier work largely focused on simplifying complex DeFi operations.

DeFiZap aimed to combine protocol interactions that users would otherwise have to complete step by step, reducing the number of actions required and making DeFi easier to access. In 2020, DeFiZap merged with DeFiSnap to form Zapperfi. Nodar was involved in a DeFi product built for real users, rather than simply a token-marketing project.

I think the connection between that experience and HOOKR is more worth examining than the fact that its founder has worked on a well-known project.

Zapper aimed to lower the barrier for users accessing complex financial tools. HOOKR is trying to lower the barrier for developers building complex trading rules. The former combined multiple DeFi operations into easier-to-use workflows; the latter breaks different trading mechanisms into composable, reusable modules.

This does not prove that HOOKR will succeed, but it does suggest that the project is not merely a temporary narrative disconnected from its founder’s previous experience. Nodar previously participated in integrating and popularizing DeFi products. Now, he is trying to take a similar approach into the trading infrastructure layer.

However, if HOOKR relies solely on its official team to keep developing new modules, it could ultimately remain just a launchpad with more features.

The more valuable scenario would be one in which third-party developers can create new Hooks that other issuers can reuse directly, while developers receive a corresponding share of fees when projects adopt their components. Pool activity would then provide feedback, and HOOKR’s development would no longer depend entirely on the official team’s development speed. Instead, it could create an ecosystem driven by developer supply, issuer adoption, and trading activity.

This is the most important dividing line in how I evaluate the project.

If developers only occasionally use a few standard modules supplied by the official team, the ecosystem’s competitive moat will be limited. If more independent developers begin designing new trading mechanisms for different assets, and those components are repeatedly adopted by multiple projects, HOOKR could gradually become infrastructure that other applications depend on.

The official team has already showcased product directions involving external integrations and arbitrage profit recapture. However, it is important to distinguish features that are already live from partnerships that are still under development or awaiting review. A list of partners does not constitute a network effect. The more convincing evidence will be actual trading volume, fee revenue, and component reuse after launch.

HOOKR’s token economics also need to be evaluated based on the revenue the protocol actually receives.

According to the current official documentation, the protocol can take a share of fees generated by certain Hook Blocks, with a default share of 20%. It does not take a cut of the base LP trading fee. Actual revenue depends on which modules a pool enables, whether those modules generate fees, and the applicable revenue-sharing rules.

This means rising platform trading volume does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in protocol revenue. Even if a pool is highly active, a pool that only charges the base LP fee may not generate corresponding revenue for HOOKR.

The buyback and burn mechanism is designed to connect protocol revenue with the token. But an investment thesis still requires on-chain evidence: how much in fees has actually been collected, how much has been allocated to buybacks, how many tokens have been purchased, and whether the burns have genuinely been executed. Rising trading volume alone is not enough to conclude that demand for the token has strengthened accordingly.

Security is another issue that cannot be overlooked at this stage. HOOKR’s contract source code and testing materials are public, but these materials still need to be verified against specific versions and deployments. Open-source code should not be treated as equivalent to an independent audit. The more flexible the programmable trading rules become, the more important code review and real-world operating records will be.

Ultimately, HOOKR is worth watching because it could move asset trading on RH Chain beyond standardized buying and selling into a layer of composable trading mechanisms. Nodar’s experience with DeFiZap and Zapper provides some relevant background for this product direction, while the development of a genuine developer ecosystem will determine whether HOOKR becomes a feature-rich token launchpad or infrastructure that other projects continue to adopt.

What I will be watching next is not how many new Hooks it launches, but whether third-party developers continue deploying them, whether external projects actually adopt them, and whether protocol revenue can grow sustainably and flow through to HOOKR via verifiable buybacks and burns.

If this cycle works, HOOKR’s value will no longer come merely from short-term activity around new token launches. It will come from growing demand for programmable trading mechanisms as more assets enter RH Chain.

If developer adoption remains limited and revenue continues to depend on a small number of trading pools, then even with an interesting product design, HOOKR will not yet have proven that it can become an indispensable layer of the ecosystem.

Fee recency (175): is it still earning this week, or did it go quiet?

Consistency (175):

Market momentum (125): real trading volume today.

Holder spread (100): is the token held widely, or by a handful of wallets?
Token age (50): time survived in the market.
Creator and whale selling (75): are insiders heading for the exit?

1000 points, all from public data, re-scored every hour. Nothing is self-reported, and anyone can recompute every number.

text:
The #Pentagon has identified a new threat: #ConfuciusInstitutes.
First refrigerators. Then cranes and garlic. Now the #ConfuciusInstitutes. The #NationalSecurity threat list keeps growing. Somewhere, a Mandarin textbook is presumably being grilled under a bright light.
Official data showed that by the end of 2025, 510 Confucius Institutes had been established in 164 countries and regions, bringing people closer through Chinese-language learning, opportunities to explore Chinese culture and greater understanding across cultural divides.
Turning classrooms into security threats takes a remarkable imagination. It also spares officials the trouble of distinguishing curiosity from conspiracy.
You might think understanding #China would help America navigate its relationship with China. But seeing an enemy behind every blackboard only turns ignorance into official policy.
Nothing projects confidence quite like treating a beginner's vocabulary list or paper cuttings as an enemy arsenal.
