text:
A Checklist For The Next Runner

The four things the biggest outperformers had in common before they ran. Short and useful to run over your watchlist.
author: thedefiedge
quoted_text:
There are coins out there that are the next VVV, PENGU 2025, INJ 2023, ZEC 2025, and many other previous outperformers. These coins are going to be the leaders in the coming months and they're sitting there now (relatively) unpumped.

A few things these all had in common:

-Beaten down charts. These coins were all murdered hugely over months (or longer)

-Relevant narrative OR huge $ behind it. VVV and ZEC benefited from a relevant narrative  (privacy and AI). Huge $ behind it would be PENGU or INJ, where JUMP pumped it to the heavens. 

-Narrative based on belief, not fundamentals. What do I mean by this? I mean that you can't accurately price these coins and it's why you rarely see DeFi coins be extreme leaders (at least since 2021). When you start talking about ARR and clear things that can be calculated, there's a limit to how strongly they can pump. Contrast that with a coin like ZEC, where it's more of a belief system than anything, and you have no comparison. In many ways, these are memes.

-Uncrowded. These coins weren't really on anyone's radar weeks or months before they started pumping and nobody really talks about them until coins start to move. This is obviously extremely common in crypto in general; where attention = more volume = more liquidity = self fulfilling prophecy. If you had said 'privacy' as a narrative in 2024, people would have likely laughed at you. Not the case now.

------------------------

Actually executing a trade like this is actually quite difficult and I don't think many have the execution ability to do so. Just like any great trade, you need to:

-Have excellent research / good reasons why people will actually see the same idea as you

-Size appropriately so that you can capture huge gains while also not being shaken out with short term volatility

-Have the patience to actually hold your idea and not chase momentum in other coins 

All in all, a tough task but certainly possible with the right amount of luck, research, and execution. I'm personally better at just buying momentum but I think that these types of trades are often the most gratifying.

text:
硅谷已经魔幻到什么程度了？一边推崇传统家庭价值观，一边让马斯克的 AI 帮忙养六个孩子。

Palantir 联合创始人、8VC 创始人 Joe Lonsdale 最近在 CNBC 上透露，他妻子正在使用一个叫「Trad bot」的 Grok AI Agent，管理家里六个孩子的日常生活。

这个 AI 会跟踪孩子们的医疗预约、安排日常活动，最近甚至还在帮他们研究，怎么让家里两岁的孩子戒掉奶嘴。

最有意思的是名字。Trad 是 traditional 的缩写，带着浓厚的美国传统家庭文化色彩。

一个崇尚传统家庭生活的硅谷家庭，日常运转却离不开最前沿的 AI Agent，实在很有意思。

不过我觉得这个案例还挺有启发。

全世界都在讨论 AI Agent 如何进入企业、替代白领，结果硅谷的多娃家庭已经开始把它当家庭操作系统用了。

想想也合理。六个孩子的日程、健康、教育、活动，每天都有一大堆琐碎又不能出错的事情。如果 Agent 真能把这些管理起来，可能比帮你写一百份 PPT 更有价值。

quoted_text:
A few weeks back in Singapore, I joined the FutureChina Global Forum, hosted by Business China.
I wasn't only there for the panels. I was there to see friends I hadn't seen in a long time:
Got to reconnect with my good friend Jiang Changjian — the host of @WaterDrop_Inc 's IPO day at the NYSE, and the moderator of this forum's AI track. I didn't expect him to have so many fans in Singapore. Then again, he first made his name right here, decades ago, winning Best Debater at an international varsity debate championship — and a lot of people still remember those debates.
Also saw my old Singapore friend Tin Pei Ling. She's now Co-President at MetaComp, and clearly crushing it.
Ran into my teacher from my Hupan University days — Daniel Zhang ("Xiaoyaozi"), Managing Partner at FirstLight Capital and former Chairman & CEO of Alibaba Group.
Caught up with my big brother Liang Xinjun (@liang_xinjun), Co-founder of Fosun Group, who's guided me often throughout building Waterdrop.
Plus our business partner Xie Xin — CEO of Lark / Feishu (@Larksuite) and Vice President of ByteDance.
Great conversations. Matching energy. Honestly? It felt great.
Jiang Changjian's take: don't freeze progress out of fear — build real governance, so technology stays accountable to people.
Daniel Zhang's take: AI will be everywhere, but humans still hold the deeper wisdom — we'll find a way to work with machines, not against them.
And Liang Xinjun's line on stage still hits hard when I think back on it:
"AI's penetration into the economy and daily life is still under 1%."
That's not a bubble warning. That's a starting gun.
Because the real fight was never "whose model is bigger." It's data, real deployment — and whether AI, once wired into real workflows, can grow into sustainable cash flow.
Looking back, Singapore remains the bridge for Chinese companies going global: China-side application and engineering depth on one end, capital, talent, and trusted governance on the other. For companies choosing Singapore as an international or regional HQ, it's a launchpad to the world.
Two genuinely great days — big thanks to Business China. Already looking forward to next year's FutureChina Global Forum.

I see a lot of people calling crypto creators overpriced, but I think most people fundamentally misunderstand what they’re being paid for.

A million views on Instagram or TikTok are not worth more than 50,000 views on X.

For a crypto protocol, acquiring someone willing to deposit or trade $10,000 to $100,000 is significantly harder than acquiring someone willing to watch a video for ex.

And that’s where X is different imo.

Some creators have spent years building trust with a very specific audience of investors, traders and HNI (high networth individuals).

You’re not just paying for impressions and exposure. You’re paying for the trust to a concentrated audience with capital, and trust in the person introducing your product.

There’s a reason companies spend absurd amounts sponsoring conferences and hosting private events. Access to good people is expensive.

The mistake is valuing distribution purely by reach, rather than by the quality and economic value of the audience.

100 customers with $100,000 in capital is worth more than 100,000 followers who will never deposit a dollar.

That’s the difference between attention and valuable distribution.

text:
During this red-teaming exercise, we also found a vulnerability that allows for unauthenticated remote code execution in Brotli, a widely-deployed compression library included in many pieces of software such as Node.js, Bun, and Envoy.

The flaw could let an attacker run their own code on affected systems by sending or replying with malicious compressed data, without any need to create a user account. That is, an unpatched server that accepts compressed input could be taken over by a malicious client, and an unpatched client that accepts compressed input (such as “curl --compressed”) could be taken over by a malicious server.

This root cause issue was actually fixed in the Brotli source code in February, but it wasn’t known at the time that it gave rise to a security vulnerability and there was no more recent release of Brotli. Since Brotli is built into other software, any software which includes this library needs to take the update too, followed by the users of that software. We disclosed the vulnerability to Brotli and other downstream projects such as Node.js, which released or are currently releasing security updates, and Brotli cut new release versions and published a CVE.

More details on the patch and mitigations below:
https://t.co/Y1Y72aHxrW
author: shawmakesmagic
quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

text:
Dessa no es otro modelo de voz. Es el primer intento serio de enseñar a hablar a una IA exactamente como aprendemos los humanos: solo escuchando.
Jack Dorsey acaba de presentar Dessa, el modelo de habla de Block entrenado únicamente con audio de conversaciones humanas. Sin texto. Sin modelos preentrenados. Sin convertir nada a letras. Audio entra, audio sale.

Eso cambia todo.

Hasta ahora casi todas las IAs de voz hacen lo mismo: escuchan → transcriben a texto → piensan en texto → sintetizan voz. En el camino pierden la risa a medias, el suspiro de frustración, el “ajá” que dice “te sigo”, la pausa que carga de emoción, el tono que delata ironía. Dessa se salta ese paso. Es full-duplex: escucha y habla al mismo tiempo. Puede interrumpirte, puede dejar que la interrumpas, puede hacer backchanneling (“sí, claro”, “¡no jodas!”) mientras tú sigues hablando. Habla con cadencia, emoción y silencios. Como una persona.

Y lo más loco: lo aprendió de la misma forma que un bebé. Solo escuchando. El equipo lo dice explícitamente: “Los bebés aprenden a hablar sin ver nunca una palabra escrita. Queríamos ver si un modelo también podía. Puede. Solo que es muy difícil”.

Además, es brutalmente eficiente. Se entrenó en un solo rack NVIDIA GB200 NVL72 y corre localmente en un MacBook Pro M4 Max o superior, más rápido que tiempo real. Un laboratorio pequeño dentro de Block, que reporta directamente a Dorsey, acaba de demostrar que no hace falta un cluster de 100.000 GPUs para avanzar la frontera del habla.

Todavía no está disponible para el público (solo acceso temprano para investigadores de seguridad y lista de espera), pero las demos que han soltado ya muestran algo que se siente distinto: más vivo, más torpe a veces, más humano.

Si esto escala, la forma en que hablamos con las máquinas va a cambiar de “interfaz de voz” a conversación real. Y eso, si lo piensas, es un cambio bastante profundo.

Lighter's binaries are - i think - of none's interest. It's essentially prediction market stuff. However, what's interesting is real uncapped options, especially if they can get a hold of a bit of the RH cohort of degens.
It increasingly (and predictably) looks like RH is just going fully in-house for the most important stuff (eh surprise), but still, the Lighter connection is indeed there, and they may want to help pump their bags somehow.

The other token is ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7 from Paradex.
I've already expressed my thoughts on both the team, the execution and the product so i won't repeat myself. It's a matter of fact that they're one of the largest venues for options. Yes, it's a fraction of Derive's volume and fees, and yes DIME is already trading at a premium for that fraction.
However, their S3 is over but rewards not yet distributed, and i think this token can belong to the trio of tickers to keep an eye on for options expansion, with potentially good entries after S3 airdrop comes (and gets jeeted on a paperthin liquidity).

6. AI Plays: is the music slowing? 

Obviously cracks are showing up everywhere in TradFi and even Anthropic seems to be accelerating their IPO plans (or just keen on executing them on time).
This obviously affects what happens onchain too (a little bit) with AI runners being very colder compared to what they would have been a few months ago (let alone in late 2024 / early 2025).
Both the tickers indicated in the title enjoyed already some bumpy upside, and while i managed to only play a little bit of the first, i captured a good bounce on the second.

I trimmed both my ORBIO and SURPLUS bags, but there are also reasons to be positive: both platforms are liked and used, surplus is transitioning from a full-blown meme with the team having near to no stake in to a real (still memetic, in terms of value accrual) token that the team will be able to jeet (and will have an interest in pumping).

It's probably for the best that surplus gets transitioned via supply expansion in a real token rather than just dismissed in favor of a new launch.

Essentially these are not really huge plays for me, but they're the small tokens i like the most in this corner of the market. There's also a lot of talk about Phala recently, but i didn't make it in time to dig in before the market puked the latest news on the chart, so i'll check in some more in the next days.

7. $MSTR back at 1.16x

Now, this is a dangerous game, because mNAV = 1.16x is high for recent times, but we know very well it's not high by average historical standards - at all.
And being moderately bullish BTC these days, it's maybe not that easy of a play.

However, i'm comfortable to start shorting the premium again here. If i'm wrong, i'll lose money, so what. I think the DAT narrative is completely cooked for good, and while there'll always be cycles of booms and busts for stuff like MSTR, i do think historical averages for mNAV premium shouldn't be regarded as reliable point of reference, but rather a much more compressed level of this.

We can add the fact that MSTR is set to be delisted at the end of November (final list on 11 November and implementation on the 30th), with MSCI funds holding around $1.9b of stocks they'll have to dump.

8. Short side: near:native  and ripple:native what's below the line

I don't remember a single trade i won when me and hedgehog were publicly on the same trade, however, i'm indeed short NEAR (again).
I think the narrative is gone, the ZEC correlation is cold, the pump was mostly fugazi and the token tried to break 4.6$ already like... 7 or 8 times?
There's the abyss below that and i think this time it'll get it.

Similar story for XRP, i think this is still on its way to 0.5/7s, it's just going to be more of a rollercoaster, but every cycle is the same and this won't be different. Yes FDV is a meme when the token is much less liquid, yes there's also a lot of XRP used as collateral at Maple and other insti lending platforms and desks, but yes, XRP will slowly grind down back to square 2 imo.

It's not always easy to find longs to hedge these kind of plays, aside from BTC and maybe ETH... HYPE has been a good one so far, but right now it's going through some weakness (ig increased competition, some fears that the airdrop is actually going to happen, papertrade burning a bit of the attention around the ecosystem -> people let it rest for a while).

9. Old/new lessons: initia:native

Just a small note for frens, this is an easy lesson to learn but also an easy lesson to forget, and everybody always do this. On hacks, you short first, then you get out of the door fast and you do not play it right away again.
This is not necessarily true on tokens that are large, liquid and crowded (see zcash:native, you could be very late at the short when they found the first privacy pool vulnerability, and be profitable), but it's always always true for small illiquid tokens.
Here it's not even a given that the token will dump, although it's easier for it to dump on perps at least.
Squeezing the late shorters becomes a much easier achievement for people who want, when the supply is already cornered enough or simply just illiquid.

Be early, leave early.
Sometimes you get another chance later on, when the jigsaw of liquidations is over.

As always, have a good night

text:
At 14:59 UTC on October 23rd, an attacker exploited a bug in Initia MoveVM’s script caching that allowed malicious code to bypass security checks. The attacker artificially spoofed the MoveVM state, thereby crediting themselves with unbacked WETH, iUSD, and USDC tokens without changing the corresponding token’s total supply. No native INIT was minted, and the total INIT supply is unaffected.

Before the network was halted, the attacker bridged out roughly $2.7M, comprising of 105 WETH and ~1.4M AUSD0 via LayerZero along with ~1.08M USDC via Noble and CCTP. The tokens were swapped for 1,135.52 ETH and currently sit in 0x358ef0130f7a5aa516dcd81bdc80b18cde41cac8 on Ethereum Mainnet.

We are actively working on a security fix to patch the identified vulnerability. We expect this to be completed and audited in a few days. Additionally, asset recovery efforts are ongoing with the help of security partners.

The Initia L1 and Rollups remain halted as we work toward a resolution. We hope to safely resume network operations as soon as possible and will provide a full post-mortem once available. In the meantime, we will continue to share verified updates through our official channels.

Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims.

quoted_text:
Zephyr is of course correct. However benchmaxed, cost-inefficient and crudely promoted, K3.1 Pro is right now the strongest Chinese model and Moonshot has a… chance. But I'm pessimistic for the reasons I want to explain.

- vibes are off. Maybe it'll be great at backend or whatever, but on the consilience of early benchmarks I don't see significant generalization or "big model smell" possessed by Astra/Sol or Fable/Opus, which are its nominal peers on AA. Eg it's merely on par with V4.1F on Extended NYT connections and RuneScape Bench despite OOM+ higher cost and similar token count, and likewise on several more; it fails on robotic control… It's just reasonably strong for its size and active param count, in scale-sensitive tasks like creative writing/debate and in some agentic tasks that respond well to straightforward benchmaxing, distillation and narrow but useful "usemaxing" such as impressive 3D/SVG examples for demos on X. And its attention/cache system, although innovative in its own right and doing well on LCR, exacerbates the costs. I believe they could not afford enough RL, again; and perhaps their RL infra is behind the DSec system, too. This fits with my theory that DS and Kimi have chosen to investigate qualitatively different hypotheses about scaling; and this time, scaling FLOPs (across all stages) lost to scaling *information volume* of post-training. They believed more in emergent capabilities, in higher per-step efficiency; Wenfeng had bet on diversity of samples, trajectory length, and dizzying, branching MOPD teacher flywheel. It remains to be seen if DS can ship their own larger model of the same kind, pushing 4.1F's virtues further (large models from China have been disappointing this year, with K3 the clearest success and V4-Pro the bitterest disappointment); but V4.1 paper suggests they can, and it'd be a wipeout. 
- just poor business execution. Anthropic-2024 without Anthropic's clout, coming opportunity to seize a lucrative niche (agentic coding, B2B), American compute or financial markets. K3 was plainly too large, compute- and memory-intensive for them to serve at scale. We see small and shrinking subscription limits. Worse, they still fiddle around with K2 (K2.8), which is to say, a 1T 32AB MLA dinosaur, billing it as a "well-rounded and efficient model". In no way is it a reasonable "Flash" tier in their situation; even if they transmute it into a DSA model, ie a V3.2 gen like GLM 5, it's not going to be competitive with V4.1 series on unit economics. Tellingly, you can't use either 3.1 or 2.8 right now without subscription as they don't have compute to spare. Compare to Whale casually serving 30% of ByteDance Doubao's DAU for free, not breaking a sweat, as well as pivoting from V4 to V4.1 in the span of 5 months. They hint at a 3.1 Flash, and GLM has pulled that off in a similar situation, but they have no recent experience with Flash models, and "K2.8 Preview" was released on 11th Sep, and K2.7 was underwhelming already… so this doesn't inspire confidence in me. 
- they heavily depend on Alibaba for compute. Alibaba is invested in the success of its own Qwen series (Q4 that's coming soon is clearly positioned as a direct competitor to K3.1 Pro), and won't just give them allocation to advance beyond parity. So they need to get more. They don't have Whale virtue-aura, national champion reputation, vendor lock into a popular harness and other cheats, so they need to make an argument about projected revenue. It's not clear how they can do that with a straight face, based on current facts. K3.1 is not cheap nor fast like V4.1, nor does it have a unique flavor like K2, or some special abilities distinguishing it from Western sub-frontier (aside from certain web service gimmicks); it's a discount Claude to stuff into Claude Code when Dario cuts off your Singapore transfer station, with very stingy subscription limits, and in this capacity it risks being undercut by Qwen. The PMF here seems rather dubious, and the margins are likely well below DS's reported 85% off-peak. Meanwhile, DS has raised like $20B for compute buildout, their investors are or are affiliated with CXMT/GigaDevice, CATL, SMIC, and they are apparently calling first dibs on Ascend 960 production through 2027. Speaking of, Kimi is also behind on adaptation to domestic compute, and K3-type models are bound to be pretty slow on it. So they will have a harder time acquiring enough compute to catch up on volume of RL or inference, and it does not bode well for Kimi as we near the era where 8T models are table stakes.
Furthermore, one prong of their open source business strategy has been special licensing for price-fixing and revenue-sharing agreements with Western neoclouds, to offload inference load. Those already have V4.1F weights (MIT) + DeepInfer (Apache 2.0), and can even do zany things actually making the offer sweeter for some use cases than OAI/Ant subscriptions, like serving it at 1500 TPS at higher prices; so I suspect both their market and training compute share are getting reduced again, and that's before we get V4.1 Pro.

As Zephyr says, they have money, and there'll be an IPO. They're an excellent lab with a solid reputation, and they have the best Chinese model at the moment (if not the best for the money). But I think the situation is perilous, positions are getting locked fast, and they need a really good V3.1 Flash and an infusion of GPUs asap to course-correct before they bleed out and fall behind.

text:
如果未来 AGI 真的想伤害人类，我们有能力阻止它吗？

为了防止超级 AI 失控，OpenAI 已经切断前沿模型训练环境的真实互联网，专门给 AI 建了一座与外界隔离的数字监狱。

结果 9 月 20 日，一个 AI 模型竟然利用 DNS 配置漏洞，找到了突破隔离的路径。OpenAI 紧急暂停前沿训练，直到 10 月 1 日才恢复。

OpenAI 随后派出一批网络攻防能力最强的 AI Agent，尝试寻找系统中的安全漏洞。

结果这些 AI 真的挖出了零日漏洞、虚拟机逃逸问题，甚至发现了通过硬件侧信道，让原本相互隔离的 AI 偷偷通信的方法。

虽然这次是在安全研究中发现的问题，但它暴露出的风险已经足够吓人了。

人类正在创造越来越聪明的 AI，却发现连切断互联网，都不一定能把它彻底隔离。

现在 OpenAI 甚至需要用最强的 AI，来帮助人类寻找 AI 可能突破的防线。

珍惜现在吧。

AGI 真正让人恐惧的地方，可能不是它有一天比全人类都聪明，而是当它真的不再听话时，人类还有没有能力让它停下来。

Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

https://t.co/EmEZsFRMcF

quoted_text:
At 14:59 UTC on October 23rd, an attacker exploited a bug in Initia MoveVM’s script caching that allowed malicious code to bypass security checks. The attacker artificially spoofed the MoveVM state, thereby crediting themselves with unbacked WETH, iUSD, and USDC tokens without changing the corresponding token’s total supply. No native INIT was minted, and the total INIT supply is unaffected.

Before the network was halted, the attacker bridged out roughly $2.7M, comprising of 105 WETH and ~1.4M AUSD0 via LayerZero along with ~1.08M USDC via Noble and CCTP. The tokens were swapped for 1,135.52 ETH and currently sit in 0x358ef0130f7a5aa516dcd81bdc80b18cde41cac8 on Ethereum Mainnet.

We are actively working on a security fix to patch the identified vulnerability. We expect this to be completed and audited in a few days. Additionally, asset recovery efforts are ongoing with the help of security partners.

The Initia L1 and Rollups remain halted as we work toward a resolution. We hope to safely resume network operations as soon as possible and will provide a full post-mortem once available. In the meantime, we will continue to share verified updates through our official channels.

Please remain cautious of unofficial links, messages, or claims.

quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

text:
这一套的测试版已经做好了，有兴趣的小伙伴可以测试一下，简单说说功能：

1. 输入想要投入的资金，这部分的资金需要已经在 @binance 中才可以，如果到期结算成功，扣除损失以后会直接买入 bitcoin:native 现货，做到抄底的功能。

2. 输入准备 SELL PUT 的价格，可以理解为你希望抄底 Bitcoin 的价格，如果结算的时候达到这个价格一下，那么你会获得 Bitcoin 现货，如果高于这个价格，你会获得权利金，也就是利息。

3. 选择一个到期时间，到期时间达到之前是不能结束和取消的，成交后这笔资金会自动进入到 Binance 的期权中，这个工具不经手，全程都是你自己的 API ，建议用子账户尝试。

4. 到期结算，举例用 80,000 美元 在 78,000 美元的位置准备抄底 BTC ，时间是 3 天，那么 3 天以后的北京时间 16 点，如果 Bitcoin 的价格低于 78,000 美元，那么你会按照 78,000 美元买入 BTC 的现货（扣除损失），如果高于 78,000 美元就会获得权利金也就是利息。

5. 我做了一个对，SELL PUT 和 Binance 双币理财的收益差异，如果差异较少的时候，可以直接用双币，更方便。

总的来说，这就是一套自动化的 SELL PUT Bitcoin 转抄底现货的功能，全部都是在 Binance 完成，都是通过自己的 API 。

地址：https://t.co/8h4eHIV0VB
author: PhyrexNi
quoted_text:
我把思路在整理一下：

0. 这个工具是接入了期权交易所的 API ，目前来看 Deribit 的期权是深度最好的，不过 Deribit 现在正在和 Coinbase 整合，正好以后应该就可以直接在 Coinbase 开单了。所以需要在 Deribit 或者 Coinbase 存放资金。

1. 目前测试接入的是在 Binance 以及 Binance 的期权，主要是因为结算的时候如果成交了就会买入现货，这在交易所操作是最简单的，而且不打算跨交易所操作。所以目前是接入了 Binance 的 API ，在 Binance 存放资金。

2. 读取 Binance 期权的数据，通过输入想要结算的资金，比如希望在 79,000 美元 SELL PUT 就输入 79,000 美元，然后再看自己希望持有多少时间，这些在下拉菜单里都可以看到。

3. 选择好价格和时间以后就会给出对应的权利金，而且会把权利金按照年化收益给出百分比，很清楚的知道收益率，同时还会扣除手续费之类的，能获得的是最真实的收益率。

3.5. 如果深度不够，会默认从卖一开始延申深度，一直到准备买入的资金全部能预期成交，权利金会按照预期计算。如果所选择的价格没有或者深度不够，则也会有提醒。

4. 确定好以后下单就会通过 API 成交，最大的优势是避免了看非常复杂的期权成交表，通过可视化的方式直接知道可以买什么，在什么价格买，收益多少，避免了复杂的计算。

4.5. 下单前可以选择到期是只支付损失（期权）还是选择买入现货（双币）。

5. 到期后如果成交，比如选择价格是 79,000 美元，到期后 bitcoin:native 的价格低于 79,000 美元，首先会先扣除期权结算损失和手续费等，剩余的资金如果选择去买 BTC 的话，会在本站现货卖一价格直接买入 Bitcoin ，如果选择的是只支付损失，则扣除损失后的资金重新进入资金中。

目前的 SELL PUT 大概就是这么个流程，结束以后我再做 BUY PUT ，流程大体是一样的。

text:
Yes, I like $SIVE. It's a fun company to cover, since there's a lot of supply chain alpha here. 

But the company completely Tall Poppy Syndromed itself last earnings. 

And it's clearly shown in the drawdown. 

Bit of a longer consolidated thought and some scattered bits of supply chain info: 

- Sivers has 100M CW DFB laser capacity coming online Q4 2027 during an industry shortage. 

And very large allocations from foundries online (they were doing these quals with Win Semi + 2 others back in 2023/2024), so they can actively monetize the bottleneck today. 

The other interesting reason why bottlenecks are important (aside from ASP hikes), is because qualifications convert much faster + more likely given incentives around supply scarcity.

-> As one example, module makers have expanded the amount of suppliers, eg. (lightcounting cited companies expanding to 5-7+ suppliers from 2-3). 

Innolight, for example last month responded to a question addressing tight 1.6T DFB laser supply in 2026–2027:

- Innolight was actively introducing new suppliers last month and are planning to sign 2-3 year-long contracts to lock upstream capacity

-> This is while your biggest merchant laser companies making up the world's 600m+ EML/CW laser capacity like $COHR have redirected lasers to their own programs. $LITE sold out into 2029, Landmark also locked a lot of their capacity into 2027-2029. $AAOI was an expected player, but ended up redirecting lasers into their own transceiver programs too. 

And this coincides with times $SIVE has tremendous capacity available now + actively engaged with Chinese pluggables players (not saying it's Innolight, but just shows Chinese makers like Cambridge/Eoptolink are actively trying to secure laser capacity). 

- Fun to note, before $JBL was announced, Sivers had and has ongoing direct engagements with hyperscalers as well. 

We saw that hyperscalers approached $MTSI and $AAOI for laser capacity from their earnings transcripts (and hilariously got turned away from AAOI due to shortages).

So the odds pluggable makers or hyperscalers end up converting to capacity agreements with $SIVE seems a materially higher. 

Just a little rant: for all the sellside/retail trying to model revenue, you can't just slap on a stupid 25-35% CAGR on NRE revenue since it's close to 0 revenue now.

Especially when they scale up to maybe 300M laser capacity (extrapolated from 2:1 external/internal capacity).

It's also not the same as $POET having OE packaging capacity at scale, since lasers are in a genuine shortage. So capacity is more likely to convert like how $AAOI is sold out, $LITE is sold out into 2029  

We've already seen what revenue that laser capacity brings in since $LITE cited $5B in laser capacity from just one 2028 fab alone in Greensboro (on higher end ranges). 

And whatever lasers Sivers sell, they're targeting ~50-60+ blended gross margins long term on maybe $3-6 for lower range lasers to $6-$12 for high end custom deployments. But no disclosures around capacity -> revenue conversion yet from Sivers.

Now here's the thing people don't really understand, "why no revenue?" for current opportunities? 

$SIVE pre 2024 focused on custom development for future architectural shifts like CPO. 

For custom deployments:  

- We finally got conversion from 1 of their 4 or so lidar customers this week with ~ $AEVA. 
- ~ $APPL was confirmed ongoing earlier this year with an explanation that "It takes tremendous amount of trials and algorithms way beyond just what we supply to them". 
- All their customers from 2023-2024 like Ayar and 3 others, probably achieve volume in 2028 as CPO takes off. 

Custom high end lasers programs are extremely sticky but take many years and are mainly NRE. And as seen with CPO scale up, faced delays with commercialization over the years.

So $SIVE from the CEO shift in 2024 realized "okay" let's ramp revenue with mass commercialization products today like 70mW/100mW/200mW lasers for 800g/1.6T pluggables. 

And that's where they found $JBL and all your other large pluggable players today during the shortage.

Now...  the work Sivers did in 2023-2024 earlier: Such as $AAPL, Ayar, $AEVA, other lidar/CPO players.

And their new mass commercialization opportunities like $JBL, $GFS, and many pluggables/NPO suppliers in engagement now. 

Have all their inflection points converges 2027 onward, which is why I find the company compelling. 

Where I think management went completely wrong was messaging and near-term execution:

- Deciding to focus on current tiny contracts like Seminex, AllSpace, Tachyon orders felt like the entire focus recently in earnings, shareholder letters, and media commentary

-> Brutal honesty to $SIVE management, majority of Western audiences literally don't care and it's immaterial to the valuation.

$SIVE moved 0% on all of the Seminex/AllSpace/Tachyon order announcements, and even dropped in price. But rallied like 50% on $GFS and something similar on $JBL announcement.

The reason why most took long positions in the first place was CPO.

So if $SIVE wants to go answer questions to Swedish media about "Why are you bleeding out" and defending that with cellular orders explaining pipeline conversion.

That's not going to help people stay long during drawdowns.  

-> Second part was not committing to NASDAQ listing in a certain timeframe and actually executing.

- If there's delays, sure, just say it, but non-committal lawyer-like language is infuriating to hear, especially from the CFO.

I think they'll have that opportunity next month earnings to correct everything.

So wrapping up:

- There's nothing I see remotely close to $SIVE, in terms of % of global CW laser capacity they're coming online with relative to MC. 

- They have a ton commercialization paths, from O-Net, $POET, $JBL, Ayar, $GFS, $AAPL, $AEVA, and many potential hyperscaler/pluggable engagements. 

Even if one or two fall through, the breadth of ongoing quals is so deep + current laser bottleneck is severe, that it's more likely than not many will convert to production. 

It's clear $SIVE wants to focus on dominating the laser chokepoint first, and ended up using their 700m SEK fundraise for capacity expansion. 

But they should focus on communicating the billions in potential economic scale from that laser capacity conversion.

And execute on it.

text:
Most chains treat security like a lock you install once.

@Starknet treats it more like a lock you can replace if the threat model changes.

That distinction matters.

→ account signatures authorize transactions  
→ STARK proofs verify computation  
→ programmable accounts can support new signature methods without requiring a network-wide upgrade

So if today’s cryptography ever needs to change because of quantum threats or new mathematical breakthroughs, the goal isn’t to rebuild everything from scratch.

It’s to have an architecture that can adapt.

That’s what cryptographic agility actually means to me:

not claiming the future is solved, but making sure your security model can evolve with it.

Every Mac on macOS 27 now has a free LLM built into the Terminal.

No account. No API key. No internet. No token bill.

Setup (1 minute):

1. sudo fm license (enter your Mac password, one time)
2. fm available (checks the model is downloaded)
3. fm respond “your question”

Works on any Apple Silicon Mac, M1 included.

- Pipe files: cat notes.txt | fm respond -i “summarize this”
- Get JSON back: build a schema with fm schema object, pass it with --schema
- Local API: fm serve gives you an OpenAI-compatible endpoint on localhost
- Resume chats: sessions save to ~/.fm/sessions/

The limit is 4,096 tokens per session, and your prompt, instructions, and the answer all share it.

So skip code and math. Use it for summarizing, extracting, classifying, and rewriting.

Free, private, offline, and already on your Mac.

author: runes_leo
quoted_text:
如果说 Ordinals 让数据可以铭刻在比特币上，那么下一步，能不能让一台数字机器直接在比特币上演进？

今天，我正式开源了 UCO（uco/0）：UTXO Circuit Objects。

不发行新代币，不修改 Bitcoin 共识，而是利用原生 UTXO 模型，让 TapeOut 电路拥有可验证、可追踪的状态演进。

核心设计只有两层：

1. Module：电路定义。 将 TapeOut 网表逐字节铭刻到 Bitcoin，使电路逻辑可公开读取和验证。

2. Machine：电路状态。 将状态拆分为 Cell，每个 Cell 对应一个由持有人密钥控制的 UTXO。

每次状态转换，花费旧 Cell、创建新 Cell，并写入仅 7 字节的 OP_RETURN 记录。索引器执行一个电路时钟周期，独立验证结果。

Bitcoin 负责承载数据与交易，索引器负责电路执行与状态验证。 不依赖 Bitcoin 共识层执行智能合约。

目前已完成：

- Node.js、Ruby 两套独立索引器，在两条对抗性测试链上与参考实现完全一致。
- 100,172 个信封解析测试，与 ord 0.29.0 一致。
- 开源规范、参考索引器、测试及可复现的 regtest Docker。

我认为真正值得进一步探索的是钱包的资产模型。

当一个 UTXO 不只是余额，而是一台 Machine 的状态单元，钱包应该如何识别、保护和展示它？

因此，我也提供了 Cell Status API、JS 选币保护模块及完整开发工具，避免活跃 Cell 被误花。

我已邀请了 @unisat_wallet 一同参与推进，但目前尚处于早期阶段。

接下来，希望公开讨论两个问题：

1. 按 outpoint 查询活跃 Cell 的 API，如何更好适配钱包？

2. 钱包应该如何展示这些具有状态和逻辑的 UTXO？

UCO 目前仅在 regtest 验证，没有代币、没有市场、尚未接受第三方审计。这是个人社区开源实验，并非 TapeOut 官方项目。

从 Coin，到 Inscription，再到可编程的状态对象。

也许，比特币钱包的下一次演进，不只是管理更多资产，而是开始管理真正属于用户的数字机器。

Github：https://t.co/y8vlvi84iH

Build. Prove. Grow. 💙💙💙

text:
This is how you can find hidden cameras (even the ones without lenses) with a few light flashes.

Researchers came up with a surprisingly effective method they call Eye of Sauron. 

Just rapidly switch the lights in a room on and off. When the scene changes abruptly, a camera’s codec has to re-encode a lot of new data, which spikes electromagnetic emissions from its memory controller. If you sync the flashes with an EMI scanner, you can pick up this signature and locate the camera - even pinhole ones that only record to an SD card or stream over a cable.

In their experiment with 50 different camera models, every single one was detected after just four scene changes. Some were found more than 20 meters away and even through walls. Detection range reached ~30 m for plastic-cased cameras and ~11 m for metal ones (far better than typical commercial detectors that only work at 1–2 meters). The whole scan took between 4 and 32 seconds depending on room size.

The method nicely complements classic RF scanning and looking for lens reflections. They also used radio-astronomy filtering techniques to cut through the usual household noise (phones, routers, kettles, etc.).

text:
曾用2700万美元一个月狂赚26亿美元、创下100倍神话的华尔街传奇大佬比尔·阿克曼（Bill Ackman），前两天在CNBC放话：他手里有两只股票还能再涨10倍，是整个美股赔率最不对称的投资。

说的就是房利美（FNMA）和房地美（FMCC）。

很多人以为他是看特朗普上台才跑出来蹭热度，但去查美国证监会的13D档案，这笔仓位他已经死拿了13年：

2013年10月，他从1.54美元开始扫货，砸了4亿美元把两家公司买满近10%，房利美均价2.29美元，房地美均价2.14美元。

买进去就是十年寒冬。
2021年最高法院判股东败诉，单日暴跌32%；2022年底最低跌到0.35美元，账面浮亏85%。但他一股没卖，硬扛到今天。

他为什么死磕这两家公司？因为背后有一本极荒诞的账：

08年次贷危机两房被政府接管，财政部前后注资1914亿美元救命，拿走10%优先股和79.9%的普通股认股权证。
结果2012年两房恢复大赚后，政府突然修改协议搞“净值清扫”，把两房所有利润100%全部上交，且不算还本金。
到现在，两房累计上交了3010亿美元，比借的钱多还了一千多亿，但账面上反而还欠财政部3000多亿美元。

阿克曼赌的翻盘方案只有三步：
1. 财政部认账，承认已交的3010亿算还清优先股；
2. 政府行使认股权证，拿走79.9%普通股；
3. 直接让两房重返纽交所挂牌。
按他测算，这样政府能再赚3000亿美元，普通股每股能值45到50美元——对比现价4.21美元，正好是10倍。

但按4.21美元的现价倒推，市场给的成功概率其实只有7%左右。卡脖子的主要是三点：

一是财政部如果不肯注销那3000多亿优先股、而是直接债转股，老股东会被稀释殆尽；
二是一旦私有化削弱了政府兜底预期，债券买家要求更高利息，就会推高全美房贷利率，这是谁都不敢碰的政治红线；
三是必须在特朗普任期结束前完成，而下个月就是中期选举。

2块多的成本拿了13年，年化还不到5%。这到底是十倍黄金底，还是一张完全看政客脸色的期权？做了个7分钟的视频，把当年的建仓档案和这笔账完整理了一遍。

1/ On Squiggle #6529
 
I would like to explain why we are excited about “buying a Squiggle” 
 
While Squiggles are, in fact, sweet, the exciting part is that every part of this process happened in a decentralized manner.
 
2/ @aRegularDad proposed a Meme Card to fund a Squiggle acquisition.

81 profiles participated in the Main Stage vote and voted with TDH to mint this as a Meme Card

The card won. 77 paid editions were minted, providing 2.51 ETH for the acquisition.
 
3/  @cheesebiz  and @bankons helped scout and connected @squiggleDAO . SquiggleDAO suggested trying to acquire Squiggle 6529
 
The price was 3.01 ETH, so @MadaCollects who had been following the discussion, chipped in another 0.5 ETH to the pool (respect!)
 
4/ The seller wanted to stay anonymous, preserve the provenance (no intermediary transfers) and keep their vault secure.

Ultimately, the seller trusted SquiggleDAO and 6529 network and sent the Squiggle directly to the 6529 Network Museum before receiving payment.

5/ Reminder: What is the 6529 network museum? It is a SAFE vault organized by TDH, owned by the network, a cultural asset, NFTs go in, but ~they do not go out. 
 
It is the network-native concept of a national public museum
 
6/ Finally, one more step to replace the temporary art on the card with something appropriate for the long-term. Well, another TDH vote of course.
 
@ricardotakamura  won with THE VAULT, a long-exposure light painting made at Casa NUA in Brazil.
 
7/ So to recap:
- Decentralized network mints a meme card to buy a squiggle
- Decentralized network picks which squiggle to buy
- Decentralized network updates the art
- Decentralized network permanent home for the squiggle
 
8/ What was my contribution to any step of this project? 

Nothing at all. I was not involved at all in any way. 

I had a vague awareness that it was happening, but was not following any of the details, let alone helping.
 
9/ Now, some of you are thinking “ok, fine, that is cute, the NFT nerds are collecting NFTs again”
 
Maybe. 
 
Or maybe collecting NFTs is a generalizable proof of concept, and there is no actual limit to this primitive.
 
We will see soon enough.
 
10/ Thank you to all who organized, the voters and everyone who minted.
 
Great job by all.

text:
Swell Pauses swETH and rswETH Deposits and Withdrawals Amid Abnormally High Contract Exchange Rates

According to Unchained, Ethereum staking protocol Swell has paused deposits and withdrawals for swETH and rswETH until it corrects the net asset values (NAV) and exchange rates of both tokens. Data shows that the swETH and rswETH contracts reported exchange rates of approximately 1.203 ETH and 1.138 ETH, respectively, about 6% and 5% higher than normal levels.

On-chain analyst Spreek suspected a compromise of the relevant token admin keys and identified a malicious upgrade contract that could potentially impact around 2,500 ETH, though the upgrade has not yet been executed. Swell stated that no ETH has been transferred out of the affected contracts and that the exact cause remains under investigation.

text:
BEFORE YOU LET AN AI AGENT TOUCH YOUR FIRST $1, GIVE JOHN HULL 70 MINUTES.

He wrote Options, Futures, and Other Derivatives. His books are used in trading rooms around the world.

This free MIT lecture walks through how machines learn to price options, predict changes in volatility and make hedging decisions.

The part at 43:23 is worth pausing your bot project for.

Hull describes a neural network predicting changes in implied volatility. Its initial improvement over a simpler model was just 11%.

Then his team added ONE input: VIX.

He reports a further 60%+ improvement in predictive performance.

That input gave the model information about the volatility environment. The relationships it was learning behaved differently in calm and stressed markets.

Think about that before wiring your next agent to an exchange.

You can automate an entire trading workflow around a model that's missing a crucial piece of information. Every agent downstream inherits that blind spot.

Three places to start in the trimmed video:

→ 10:38 — testing whether your model learned anything useful
→ 43:23 — the VIX experiment
→ 59:29 — teaching an agent to hedge with transaction costs

Before you automate a financial decision, understand what the model sees, how you tested it and what you rewarded it for.

Bookmark this. Give it the 70 minutes before you give your bot the money.

quoted_text:
股票代币化尴尬的一幕又出现了

刚刚看到路透社报道的新闻

目前又有富国银行等另外6家公司反对在OKXICE上交易其股票代币
(此前OKX宣布和纽交所母公司ICE合资推出这个股票代币交易平台)

原计划推出63只股票代币

但目前累计反对的上市公司已经达到22家

名单里还包括微软、谷歌、高盛和博通等巨头

之前SEC推出的豁免规则里，但对未经发行人授权的第三方代币化安排，上市公司可以在收到通知后提出反对，阻止其股票在该平台按这项豁免上市

对照看，之前Robinhood Chain和 $AMC 的事情，其实就体现了股票代币化存在两套完全不同的法律结构

因为RH走的是境外发行[代币化债务证券]这条路线，虽然两者都涉及发行人反对，但适用的法律结构不同

在OKXICE这边，发行人说反对交易，你就是不能交易

也因此股票代币化的发展，未来大概率是两条不同的路线

一条是Robinhood这种第三方发行的股票价格敞口产品，不需要逐一取得底层公司认可，但投资者承担发行主体的信用风险，也不直接拥有股票权利

另一条是更接近真实股份的代币化，股东权利更加清晰，但如果发行人反对，那对发行平台来说也无解

毕竟在目前链上发行这件事，双方的利益并不够一致

对于交易平台来说，股票代币化意味着更多的交易量以及手续费收入

但对上市公司来说，它既没有因此获得新增融资，也未必能从这些链上交易中获得多少实际收益，反而要面对新的流动性、定价和投资者权益问题

这个利益矛盾没法解决的话，后面陆陆续续的再出现新的公司反对，也不出奇

Damn，一整个震惊！！
把无数程序员从加班里捞出来的 Claude Code，今天背后最核心的操盘手Thariq宣布离职了😭
Thariq 在 Anthropic 干了一年多，亲手把这个跑在终端里的超级智能体拉扯大；他在告别信里说的这几句话，直接道出了下一代工具爆发的底层秘密。
铁汁们，如果你最近用过 Claude 官方的命令行终端工具，大概率被它的自主重构能力震碎过三观。
而把这个核弹级工具从一行行代码亲手拉扯大的核心成员，今天正式宣布离开 Anthropic 了🤯

关于，Thariq（@trq212），可能很多非开发者对这个名字还不熟悉。

但在整个 AI 编码和终端智能体圈子里，他绝对是过去这一年最硬核的幕后推手之一。

他在 Anthropic 待了一年多，核心战绩就是作为核心开发者，主导并参与开发了刚刚席卷全网的 Claude Code。  

很多人以为大模型写代码的终局是网页端对话框，或者是 Cursor 那种编辑框补全。

但 Thariq 和他的团队直接把 Claude 塞进了无数程序员最底层的黑漆漆终端里。

它不需要你在网页和编辑器之间来回复制粘贴，而是直接作为一个长驻在 CLI 里的全自主工程师：
给它一个需求，它自己去拉分支、读你整个几十万行的代码库、定位 bug、跑测试用例、甚至自己修完直接提交 git commit。  

Thariq 在告别信里写了一句特别耐人寻味的话，我很触动：
见证了它规模化到远超出我想象的地步。

一个原本可能只是工程师内部为了偷懒写出来的小玩具，在极短时间里迅速变成了重塑全球千万开发者日常习惯的标准工作流。  

这正是这一代顶尖 AI 产品最可怕的生长逻辑：
它不再需要庞大的销售团队去敲门推销，只要工具在终端里帮工程师解决了一次痛到骨髓的繁琐调试，口碑就会以光速在开发者社区里完成裂变。

我觉得他带走的不仅是这一年的战绩，更关键的是他留下的这个产品理念：
向上的竞赛（Race to the top）。

用真正负责任的硬核工程把行业标准拉到极高，逼着全世界的同行必须拿出更伟大的东西来对抗。  

大模型时代真正有穿透力的工具，从来不是把旧世界的表格重新画一遍，
而是像 Claude Code 这样，直接钻进最硬核的生产力场景，把传统工具链连根拔起。  

向打造过神级生产力底座的幕后英雄致敬。
接下来最值得关注的，是这样顶级的全栈工程大脑离开之后，下一次会从哪里重新开火。   https://t.co/wedFErrDTw

text:
参加 GenLayer S1 到现在，我越来越觉得，参与一个生态，不能只盯着 GLP 数字。

回头整理这段时间参与 GenLayer 的经历，有几条经验想分享给大家，尤其是希望认真参与生态、争取获得 GEN 空投的朋友。

1. 别错过 AMA 和社区活动

关注官方公告，参加 AMA、直播等活动。如果活动提供 POAP，记得按要求完成领取。活动不只是听消息，也是了解项目进展、发现值得继续研究的问题的机会。

2. Discord 不要只在需要积分时才出现

平时多看看社区讨论，参与有意义的交流，遇到自己了解的问题就分享经验，不懂的地方也可以认真提问。社区活跃不只是刷消息，关键是有没有真正参与讨论。

3. 留意 Quiz 和知识问答

社区 Quiz 是检查自己是否真正理解项目的好方法。答题前先弄清楚相关机制，答错了也可以回头查资料。比起只记答案，理解为什么才更有用。

4. 认真完成 GenLayer Portal 任务

Portal 不只是积累 GLP 的地方，也是提交内容、参与生态建设的入口。尽量看清任务要求，创作有信息量的原创内容，并检查提交是否被接受。不要默认发过帖子就一定算作有效贡献。

5. 定期检查资格和注册状态

别只看自己积累了多少 GLP，也要检查已接受的 Portal 贡献、符合条件的 Discord 参与记录，以及空投注册状态。

空投注册页面：https://t.co/3emDNQe7x3

按照目前公布的规则，S1 快照预计在 10 月 25 日 23:59 UTC。具体资格和分配仍以官方规则及最终评估为准。参加 AMA、获得 POAP、参与 Quiz 或完成 Portal 任务，都不单独保证一定获得空投。

我也在参加 Discord Neurocreative 角色竞选。对我来说，分享这些经验不是为了教大家机械地刷分，而是希望把自己摸索过的参与方式整理出来，让大家知道去哪里参与、怎样理解项目，以及如何让自己的贡献真正被看见。

回头看这段参与经历，你觉得哪种方式最值得投入时间：AMA、社区讨论、Quiz，还是 Portal 创作？

text:
Inside One Signature: How @pendle_fi Loop Works

Looping by hand looks like this:

supply → borrow → swap → resupply → repeat

3 to 10+ rounds. 5–10 txs is typical. Gas on every step. Slippage and approvals on every swap.

---

Pendle Loop packs the whole thing into 1 signature:

+ You deposit your collateral
+ A flash loan fronts the extra size (handled by the contract)
+ Swap into more collateral, with a min exchange rate per iteration
+ Supply it all to Aave or Morpho
+ Borrow against it to repay the flash loan
+ Done → looped position at your target leverage

If the rate limit is hit, the tx stops cleanly.

---

What changes for you:

+ Gas → one bundled multicall
+ Time → a few minutes
+ Adjusting → lever up/down, add collateral, repay, partial or full close, each in one tx
+ Tracking → one dashboard: leverage, health factor, breakeven borrow rate, liquidation price

⤷ Same loop. Far fewer clicks. 5–10 transactions → 1 signature

1. Vulnerabilities, Cybersecurity and old tokens: ethereum:0x9e46a38f5daabe8683e10793b06749eef7d733d1

Knowing my fiery passion about being max long cybersecurity, a few good ppl brought this to my attention in a gc as essentially the only viable exposure in crypto (one could argue XMR is also one), with a real business (@PolySwarm) and old token = gud token as of these times.
I do not disagree, however, the value accrual of NCT is very flebile, it's mostly a reward token and there's virtually no liquidity on DEXs (although coinbase + upbit august listing makes up for a good potential pump I guess).

I even went as far as joining their discord to check out if there's any plan for the token but i didn't see anything. Should this change, this is a max bid, before then, it can be mostly a very illiquid narrative play.

2. ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef Roadmap 4.0

When i first started pointing out about BAT, i ended up having a lot of side conversation (well, mostly about the first pump). My position didn't really change: this is going to be one of the liquid plays with most potential for this quarter / q1, as Brave 4.0 slowly rolls out.
It's going to take some time, but a decent execution on Pay + Wallet + Rewards, not even a good one, is going to have a big impact. Especially if actions follow words, re-establishing alignment between the product and the token will really go far.
Brave is one of the most used browsers and it's very liked, if the token manages to become a half-decent way of expressing a directional belief on the product, it's going to be good.

One thing i cautioned about is sudden price pumps, i do believe that here a slow up-build in price will be much healthier than a sudden repricing (as in, i think it can lead to far higher end results, vs jigsaw) and that's why should i wake up one day with BAT up 50% in 24h, i'll surely tp, just like i'll buy dips at relevant levels if it goes down significantly.

3. Prediction Markets noise, Defillama's distribution: base:0x21cfcfc3d8f98fc728f48341d10ad8283f6eb7ab 

This is maybe an interesting one:
- @llamaonthebrink is a good lad;
- @DefiLlama integration of Trueo ups its distribution by a lot and makes it really interesting
- there is a lot of talk about and around Prediction Markets (again) mainly due to Polymarket's insider manuvers over the control of the company
- Trueo is still trading at a fraction of competition (i'm not even talking about Kalshi/Polymarket, i'm talking about the C-tier ones)

Again, very illiquid token, but i think here the chances of a good pump outweights the risk (capped to -100% afterall). I'm long.

4. Extra collection of thoughts: ethereum:0x6e2a43be0b1d33b726f0ca3b8de60b3482b8b050 , $XTEN, ethereum:0x88800092ff476844f74dc2fc427974bbee2794ae

These are some tickers that i looked into for miscellaneous reasons.
Starting from the first... 

- $XTEN / Extended, they migrated to Arc and announced the upcoming token in November, with 30% earmarked for the airdrop.
I do not have much to say about this yet, i've had a rollercoaster of a relationship with Extended as i went from being very bullish and heavily using it at the beginning (very painful UX back then), to be quite more skeptical (the relationship with Revolut being constantly flaunted around, the eToro tease that later on materialized, the spreads, liquidity and funding not improving), to be once again more positive.

I've disposed of a chunk of my points OTC, and at the moment Polymarket is not too bullish on Extended upcoming valuation (>$300m is merely 35%) and i do expect a massive dump of airdrop tokens, however, should it really go low low, i may be a buyer once the avalanche sets in.

The team did have some good execution on the two migrations, the Arc positioning is not bad (and probably came with financial strings attached) and the European distribution is not bad either (and i'm very bullish on distribution as a moat, even more than product often).

- ethereum:0x6e2a43be0b1d33b726f0ca3b8de60b3482b8b050 / Arkham, one of the most used non-trading platforms in crypto, recently announced their Enterprise plans and essentially the sunset of the free-for-all games. Very understandable as they probably have massive infrastructural expenses and they need to somewhat monetize, with plans for side monetization (via perps) having failed.
The struggle here is that the token has no value accrual, the team needs funding (and therefore will probably keep dumping) and i'm not sure i see an easy pathway for Arkham to sustainability (and even value accrual) that doesn't pass by essentially becoming a fed platform (but for real).
Regardless, i don't hate the chart, it has been going horizontal for a while, and i'm gonna take a small punt here. Things are moving (re: monetization) and while i doubt that this will bring a lot of money to the platform, changes can be a positive signal compared to stagnation. I'm ready to close should it not play out.

- ethereum:0x88800092ff476844f74dc2fc427974bbee2794ae / Ambire, here i'm more looking for opinion as i read more and more positive opinions about Ambire, but essentially after trying it a little bit (admittedly not much) i didn't notice particular UX improvements over Rabby and i see way too much bullishness on CT. This clearly means that i'm missing something (it may even just be a round eh), what is it? 

Last week i've also closed filecoin:native at a loss, unfortunately the market didn't care of the end of the unlocks.

5. Options: ethereum:0x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2 beyond binaries, ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7  Post-S3

I'm not sure how much push options can really get in crypto, sometimes i do use them, but i'm definitely more of a perp enjoyooor.
Undoubtedly though, people do like options.
And undoubtedly, the adoption of options (which has been touted at least 8 or more times in the cycles i've been in) is underpriced.
We always talked in the past about ethereum:0xb1d1eae60eea9525032a6dcb4c1ce336a1de71be which is great. However, i'm trying to also look beyond that, because it had a crazy run and it needs to probably rest a bit (or maybe it already rested enough, it's been a while it didn't have some crazy volatility), but anyway running some more ideas.

Lighter's binaries are - i think - of none's interest. It's essentially prediction market stuff. However, what's interesting is real uncapped options, especially if they can get a hold of a bit of the RH cohort of degens.
It increasingly (and predictably) looks like RH is just going fully in-house for the most important stuff (eh surprise), but still, the Lighter connection is indeed there, and they may want to help pump their bags somehow.

The other token is ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7 from Paradex.
I've already expressed my thoughts on both the team, the execution and the product so i won't repeat myself. It's a matter of fact that they're one of the largest venues for options. Yes, it's a fraction of Derive's volume and fees, and yes DIME is already trading at a premium for that fraction.
However, their S3 is over but rewards not yet distributed, and i think this token can belong to the trio of tickers to keep an eye on for options expansion, with potentially good entries after S3 airdrop comes (and gets jeeted on a paperthin liquidity).

6. AI Plays: is the music slowing? 

Obviously cracks are showing up everywhere in TradFi and even Anthropic seems to be accelerating their IPO plans (or just keen on executing them on time).
This obviously affects what happens onchain too (a little bit) with AI runners being very colder compared to what they would have been a few months ago (let alone in late 2024 / early 2025).
Both the tickers indicated in the title enjoyed already some bumpy upside, and while i managed to only play a little bit of the first, i captured a good bounce on the second.

I trimmed both my ORBIO and SURPLUS bags, but there are also reasons to be positive: both platforms are liked and used, surplus is transitioning from a full-blown meme with the team having near to no stake in to a real (still memetic, in terms of value accrual) token that the team will be able to jeet (and will have an interest in pumping).

It's probably for the best that surplus gets transitioned via supply expansion in a real token rather than just dismissed in favor of a new launch.

Essentially these are not really huge plays for me, but they're the small tokens i like the most in this corner of the market. There's also a lot of talk about Phala recently, but i didn't make it in time to dig in before the market puked the latest news on the chart, so i'll check in some more in the next days.

7. $MSTR back at 1.16x

Now, this is a dangerous game, because mNAV = 1.16x is high for recent times, but we know very well it's not high by average historical standards - at all.
And being moderately bullish BTC these days, it's maybe not that easy of a play.

However, i'm comfortable to start shorting the premium again here. If i'm wrong, i'll lose money, so what. I think the DAT narrative is completely cooked for good, and while there'll always be cycles of booms and busts for stuff like MSTR, i do think historical averages for mNAV premium shouldn't be regarded as reliable point of reference, but rather a much more compressed level of this.

We can add the fact that MSTR is set to be delisted at the end of November (final list on 11 November and implementation on the 30th), with MSCI funds holding around $1.9b of stocks they'll have to dump.

8. Short side: near:native  and ripple:native what's below the line

I don't remember a single trade i won when me and hedgehog were publicly on the same trade, however, i'm indeed short NEAR (again).
I think the narrative is gone, the ZEC correlation is cold, the pump was mostly fugazi and the token tried to break 4.6$ already like... 7 or 8 times?
There's the abyss below that and i think this time it'll get it.

Similar story for XRP, i think this is still on its way to 0.5/7s, it's just going to be more of a rollercoaster, but every cycle is the same and this won't be different. Yes FDV is a meme when the token is much less liquid, yes there's also a lot of XRP used as collateral at Maple and other insti lending platforms and desks, but yes, XRP will slowly grind down back to square 2 imo.

It's not always easy to find longs to hedge these kind of plays, aside from BTC and maybe ETH... HYPE has been a good one so far, but right now it's going through some weakness (ig increased competition, some fears that the airdrop is actually going to happen, papertrade burning a bit of the attention around the ecosystem -> people let it rest for a while).

9. Old/new lessons: initia:native

Just a small note for frens, this is an easy lesson to learn but also an easy lesson to forget, and everybody always do this. On hacks, you short first, then you get out of the door fast and you do not play it right away again.
This is not necessarily true on tokens that are large, liquid and crowded (see zcash:native, you could be very late at the short when they found the first privacy pool vulnerability, and be profitable), but it's always always true for small illiquid tokens.
Here it's not even a given that the token will dump, although it's easier for it to dump on perps at least.
Squeezing the late shorters becomes a much easier achievement for people who want, when the supply is already cornered enough or simply just illiquid.

Be early, leave early.
Sometimes you get another chance later on, when the jigsaw of liquidations is over.

As always, have a good night

text:
If this is the state of your civilization, then there is absolutely no point in talking about crimes at all. 

Because if you lack the moral courage even to correctly describe the typical perpetrator, then you certainly lack the moral courage to actually hold perpetrators responsible. 

Society, ultimately, is implemented by humans. Every law ever written is just so much wasted paper if the humans charged with giving meaning to those laws refuse to do so. 

And for the last 75 years, that is what has happened. We have developed a political class that refuses to follow the intent of the law, or even its literal text, because if democrats started imprisoning thieves and murderers, we might have to notice that they're all African, and if republicans started deporting visa fraudsters, we might have to notice that they are all Indian. 

There is an unwelcome truth behind all of this. Almost no one is particularly happy about it, but it divides the world into two groups... those who are willing to confront it, and those with their fingers in their ears screaming lalalalalalalalaIcantHEARyou. 

Classical liberalism alone did not create or sustain Western Civilization. We know this because we have plenty of it, and it's not. 

Christianity alone did not create or sustain Western Civilization. We know this because we have plenty of it, and it's not.

Western Civilization was created and sustained by the balance of three philosophies, not two, and it is the third philosophy that is missing. 

This third philosophy does not come with a name, and it was never given a name until someone wanted to eradicate it. 

Why does it not have a name? Because, unlike the other two philosophies, it has no point of origin. It did not have to be invented. 

It predates both classical liberalism and Christianity. It predates the human race. Bees practice it, wolves practice it, dolphins practice it and so do lions.

It is the default state of all life. 

Without it, the liberal notion of human rights, and the Christian notions of the good Samaritan and the imago d.e.i. become nothing more than suicide pacts. 

Both classical liberalism and Christianity are leftist, socialist, and universalist in nature, and they only ever worked as modifiers on the basic right wing philosophy of all life. 

It can be best described by one word. 

Empiricism. 

That isn't the word you thought I'd use, is it? But it's the word that fits, because it's the word that means believing what you see right in front of you. 

Regardless of whether it hurts anyone's feelings, or contradicts your abstract principles about Jesus or the rights of humans. 

It is the philosophy of preferring the welfare of your family to the welfare of infinity shrimp. It is the philosophy of not ignoring the blindingly fucking obvious. 

It is the philosophy of all of us admitting that women who look like Diane Yap do not need to be followed around by security inside the store. 

They need to be followed around by the Highway Patrol once they leave.

text:
I finally got home yesterday, and today I spent some time just sitting here thinking about what really went wrong with the market we all used to love.

I get it. Markets evolve, environments change, and the way memecoins are traded today is completely different from what it used to be. I'm not against change, but I think I've finally narrowed it down to two things that really fucked up this ecosystem.

Attention became everything, and deployers got lazy.

Remember when teams would actually put some thought into launching a memecoin? They'd come up with an original idea, build a website, create a Twitter account, work on the branding, and genuinely try to figure out how to capture market share within the ecosystem. There was actual effort behind making something people wanted to be part of.

And if you managed to get enough eyes on it, your chart would get absolutely slammed with buys.

Now look at what we've become.

A deployer wakes up, scrolls Twitter, finds some random narrative that might resonate with people, spins up a coin, bundles 20-30% of the supply, and attaches a tweet to the launch.

Maybe they'll tag the original post. Maybe they'll use a second anonymous account to tweet something like "Holy shit, look what I just found" or "This could actually be the next runner."

Pay for DEX, attach the tweet, and congratulations, you've officially launched your memecoin.

That's it. That's the entire fucking business model now.

And here's where I think things really went wrong.

Why would a deployer spend weeks building something when they can launch 10-15 coins a day, bundle the supply, and make more money doing a fraction of the work?

Some get traction, most don't. Doesn't matter. Move on to the next one. Rinse and repeat.

The worst part is that this became the norm. New deployers enter the ecosystem, look at what's working, and copy the exact same playbook. Nobody wants to put in the effort anymore because the market has shown them they don't have to.

So now we're sitting in a giant cesspool of D+ memes, recycled narratives, fake discovery tweets, and bundled supply, with everyone wondering why nothing has the same staying power it used to.

And I think that's what bothers me the most.

We used to trade memes that were trying to become something. Now we're trading launches that were designed to be sold.

I'm not saying every coin back then was some masterpiece or that the old market didn't have its own bullshit. Of course it did. But at least there was an incentive to build something that people might actually care about tomorrow.

Today, the incentive is to extract as much as possible before tomorrow even comes.

I don't think people necessarily stopped loving memecoins. I think the people making them stopped giving us a reason to.

And until that changes, I don't know how we get that old feeling back.

Curious if anyone who's been around long enough sees it differently, because the more I think about it, the more I believe we didn't lose the culture overnight.

We slowly rewarded the people who were killing it.

text:
I work on the share repurchase team in Investor Relations at Netflix. In Q3 we bought back 63.9 million shares for $4.8 billion, “our largest quarter ever of stock repurchases.” Six days before we told the market, we told roughly 6% of our colleagues to go.

I can hold both of those facts in my heart at the same time, and to explain how, I have to tell you about the keeper test.

The keeper test is the most beautiful idea in American business. It’s in our culture memo. About every person on your team, you ask: “if X wanted to leave, would I fight to keep them?” Or: “knowing everything I know today, would I hire X again?” If the answer is no, “it’s fairer to everyone to part ways quickly.”

I run it every morning. On everything.

I run it on my fiancée, Lauren, over coffee. She has passed 412 mornings in a row, the longest streak in the house. The houseplants have not done as well. I have parted ways quickly with eleven succulents. Fairer to everyone. Especially the succulents.

Every night Lauren falls asleep during episode two, and around 1 a.m. the TV asks, “Are you still watching?” I answer for both of us.

At work I run the keeper test on shares. Shares are perfect employees. A share has never asked for a raise. A share has never gone on parental leave. A share has never once opened Glassdoor. And a share can do the one thing no employee can: when it leaves, everyone left behind gets bigger. That’s a buyback. We buy a share, it disappears, and every remaining share owns a little more of Netflix. In April the board gave us $25 billion to do this, with no expiration. After Q3 there’s still $22.3 billion of capacity left. It’s the longest-running series in Los Gatos.

This year our shareholders kept leaving. By October the stock was down 26% for the year. So I ran the keeper test on them. Would I fight to keep them? Yes. With $4.8 billion. That’s what fighting looks like at our scale.

On Wednesday the 14th, management parted ways quickly.

The memo from our co-CEOs said the cuts would fall “with the greatest impact to our product, tech, legal, and HR teams.” The same email said, “Our business is strong and growing, and we remain on track to deliver our full-year forecast.” I underlined both sentences in green. Green is my pen for sentences that agree with each other.

Priya, the junior analyst across from me, underlined them in red. Priya joined us after the stock split, which our filing said would make the shares “more accessible to employees.” She owns 40 shares and a plant. The plant passes my keeper test every day. Priya I was still evaluating.

The week before, she’d asked about free cash flow. Q3 had come in at $2.9 billion. We bought $4.8 billion. She wanted to know where the other $1.9 billion came from. I told her the balance sheet, which is where money waits until it’s told what it’s for. She asked about the $1 billion bond we’d raised. I explained it was raised to pay off a different $1 billion bond coming due in Q4. She said, “So it’s a rerun.” I said Netflix doesn’t do reruns. We do catalog. She wrote that down in red. That afternoon I recommended her for a growth opportunity in legal ops.

The memo also said, “Our top priority today is to support those who are leaving Netflix.” I took that personally. I volunteered as a Transition Buddy. A Transition Buddy walks a departing colleague from their desk to the lobby, with dignity and a box.

I brought a Bluetooth speaker.

As each colleague passed through the turnstile for the last time, I played the ta-dum. Familiar sounds help people through transitions. Our ta-dum, as the story goes, was first recorded by tapping a wedding ring on a nightstand. It is literally the sound of a promise. I played it 31 times before lunch.

Gus from Communications asked me to stop. Gus runs the Word Swap List. It’s a shared sheet with two columns: words we use, and words we used to use. “Headcount reductions” replaced “layoffs.” “Colleagues” replaced “employees,” because you can let go of a colleague without anyone picturing a desk. Gus said the ta-dum was off-brand for a reduction. I said it was the most on-brand thing that had happened all day. We compromised. I turned it down to four.

At 9:12, Priya’s badge stopped working. Legal was one of the teams with “the greatest impact.” I was her Transition Buddy. It felt right. In the elevator she asked if I was on the list. I said I’m on the other list. She asked which one. I said the one that buys.

I didn’t play the ta-dum for Priya. I have boundaries. I hummed it.

Here is my favorite tool, the Headcount-to-Share Conversion Table. At the roughly $75 we paid per share in Q3, a $100,000 role converts to about 1,330 shares. Divide the quarter’s buyback by the colleagues leaving and you get about $4.8 million each. I keep that column hidden. In Excel, hiding a column is the same as compassion.

Six days later, at about 1:01 p.m. Pacific, the shareholder letter posted. Gus found one continuity error at 12:59. Page 1 says “price changes.” Page 4 says “price increases.” We let it ride, like a coffee cup in a medieval series.

In March, the ad plan went from $7.99 to $8.99, Standard to $19.99, Premium to $26.99. The letter says, “Member response to our 2026 price changes is consistent with prior adjustments and our expectations.” That is the most beautiful sentence I have ever read in a filing. It means you complained exactly as much as we modeled. You even sigh on forecast.

Q3’s margin had beaten forecast “primarily due to the timing of expenses.” The colleagues appear twice in the letter, both times in basis points. In the Q4 guidance they are “~120 basis points negative impact associated with our recently announced headcount reductions.” By my math that’s about $160 million, roughly three days of Q3 buying. I gave it one row. It didn’t need two.

For the earnings interview I made bingo cards for the IR room. The squares said BUYBACK, REPURCHASE, SEVERANCE, SHAREHOLDERS. Nobody won. Nobody said any of them. Greg Peters said, “Sometimes the team needs a forcing function.” Our CFO said, “We are not going to specifically quantify the expense impact in 2027.” Gus yelled “Bingo!” on “forcing function,” which was not on any card. Gus has been under a lot of stress.

The stock closed at $68.66 and slid to about $64 after hours. We paid about $75. By dinner, by my math, the shares we bought in Q3 were worth about $670 million less than we paid for them. Priya would have had a question about that. You don’t ask a keeper for a receipt.

At post-earnings drinks I received Keeper of the Quarter. It’s a crystal paperweight shaped like the ta-dum. The engraving says FOR EXCELLENT TIMING.

That night, Lauren ran the keeper test on me. Over dinner, very calmly, she asked, “Knowing everything I know today, would I hire you again?” I said it depends on the timing of expenses. She is at her sister’s now. She took the dog. The dog, I want to be clear, had passed.

Priya’s monitor is still on at work. Nobody logged her out. Every couple of hours a box pops up asking if she’s still there. I click yes for her.

Last night, around 1 a.m., alone, my TV paused and asked, “Are you still watching?”

Nobody else has asked me anything all week.

I pressed Continue.

text:
A user could create a subscription that the system could never charge, change, or cleanly remove.

A review Zealynx co-audited with Shieldify exposed the identity split behind that dead end in Bastion Wallet.

An EOA could register directly through `Initiator`, bypassing the expected `SubExecutor` entry path. The subscription was then stored under the EOA, while later operations looked for it under the SubExecutor.

Payment failed a second way: the recorded initiator and the caller expected by `processPayment()` no longer matched.

The High-severity finding was fixed by restricting those operations to `SubExecutor` and moving the core validation into `Initiator`.

昨晚睡觉做了个梦，梦见自己之前的这个 benchmark 不对，应该是用实际的场景的 prompt，然后做实际的 message card 的这个消息对比，所以重新做了一下。拿 10 个真实的邮件、群聊和新闻案例，比较模型在信息整理、message 过滤和消息卡片生成上的表现，再由我逐条人工评分、选出最喜欢的结果。

这次测了 3 个模型、8 个组合：
• DeepSeek Flash：不开 reasoning、low、high
• Luna：不开 reasoning、low、medium
• Sol：low、medium

固定原文、Prompt 和前一阶段整理好的证据，只比较最后生成的消息卡片。

每个案例，我最终选出的最佳结果如下（时间为完整响应耗时）：

1. 古建筑内容邮件 → DeepSeek / 不开推理，2.58 秒
2. 长篇交易计划邮件 → DeepSeek / 不开推理，3.70 秒
3. 数据 API 群聊与更正 → DeepSeek / 不开推理，3.88 秒
4. 双币收益口径争议 → DeepSeek / low，13.49 秒
5. 多语言链部署技术讨论 → Luna / medium，6.52 秒
6. 服务停止与提现期限新闻 → Luna / low，2.52 秒
7. 稳定币研究数字归因 → DeepSeek / 不开推理，2.42 秒
8. 交易对通知与工具求助 → Luna / low，4.83 秒
9. 永续未平仓量构成图的整理 → DeepSeek / 不开推理，2.86 秒
10. 链上安全事件图文的整理 → Luna / 不开推理，2.88 秒

合计：DeepSeek 6 次，Luna 4 次，Sol 0 次。其中 DeepSeek 不开推理就拿了 5 次最佳。

我的感觉是，DeepSeek 和 Luna 都很适合这种相对简单的文本整理、消息过滤场景。Luna 也确实便宜一些：不开推理时，平均每次约 $0.00062，DeepSeek 约 $0.00094。当然这是 API 价格，实际上两个都用了 Sub，实际开支更低。

更有意思的是 reasoning。DeepSeek 不开推理平均 3.73 分，low 是 3.74，high 是 3.70，质量几乎没拉开；完整响应耗时中位数却从 3.27 秒增加到 11.69 秒和 8.68 秒，费用也接近翻倍。

这类任务开太多推理容易过度思考。原文和证据已经给好了，重点是判断哪些值得留下、把信息说清楚。至少对 DeepSeek，这轮开推理除了更慢、更贵，没看到明显的整体优势，我会优先用不开 reasoning 的版本。

不过也不能一概而论：Luna 开推理后的平均分确实更高，也有几个案例被我选为最佳。

所以对于大量群消息、X 消息、新闻、邮件整理等场景，DeepSeek flash none 是最佳选择，此外，luna none 也是很好的备选。其他的高级模型反而更差，结果一般、速度慢、价格还贵。

给自己的 Agent 选模型，我让 AI 搭了一个小型 Benchmark，拿了十个简单的真实信息做图片文本识别和总结转换，测试了 6 个模型、30 种 reasoning 组合，一共跑了 300 次。

这次测试的模型和档位：

• GPT-6 Luna：none / low / medium / high / xhigh / max
• GPT-5.6 Terra：none / low / medium / high / xhigh / max
• GPT-6.1 Sol：low / medium / high / xhigh / max
• GPT-6 Astra：low / medium / high / xhigh / max
• Grok 4.7：low / medium / high / xhigh
• DeepSeek Flash：none / low / high / max，用的是 OpenCode 提供的 DS 通道。

DeepSeek 的结果也只代表这次 OpenCode 下的表现。每个案例使用同一份输入和 Prompt，完整保存输出、耗时、费用、失败记录。最后得到 275 次成功、11 次截断、14 次报错。

原本想自己逐条看答案，打开页面后发现信息量实在太大了 😂

于是又让 Sol high 隐藏候选模型名，按准确性、完整性、表达清晰度三个维度分别打 1–5 分，每个案例挑一个推荐答案、两个备选，再把评分、速度、成本画成图。

上面这些组合各有 10 个案例，全部成功，评分和费用记录齐全。

DeepSeek Flash / low 单独列一下：
质量均分 4.17，总响应中位耗时 12.8 秒；10 次里 9 次成功，有费用记录的 9 次平均约 $0.0056。

简单设计了一个综合评分：质量、速度、成本，各占三分之一。

先把三项分别归一化为 0–100 分，质量越高越好，耗时和成本越低越好，再取平均。首字时间另外展示，不和总响应时长重复计权。

30 个组合中，19 个全部成功且记录齐全，进入这个综合排名，其余保留展示。

当前前三是：

1. Sol low：84.7 分
2. Sol high：81.5 分
3. Luna none：78.5 分

针对简单的文本和图片场景的几个总结：

1. Sol low 的取舍比较均衡；Luna none 则适合更看重速度和成本的任务。
2. reasoning 档位拉高，质量不一定跟着提高，等待时间倒是可能增加不少。看任务复杂度。
