quoted_text:
I told you. 

I told you all. I told you over two years ago. I told you over two years ago that Vivek Ramaswamy isn't an American and never will be. 

And what did you say? 

OMG you just don't like him because he's brown you horrible basement dwelling racist. That's what you said. 

So I waited. I'm not stupid. I know better than to be right too early. 

Now I'm going to repeat myself. Vivek Ramaswamy is not American. Everything he says or thinks about America, he must mentally translate into the closest equivalent concept from his own culture, rather than understanding it in its own right.

When he says that the founding fathers "sacrificed their honor", he reveals that he does not understand what Americans mean by honor. He is instead translating it to the third world concept of "face" or "izzat", which is not what we would call honor at all, but social standing or reputation with the existing power structure. 

Similarly, when he thinks that Amy Acton is somehow compromised by having been raped at the age of 12 by an adult charged with her care. Under third world values, this is a loss of "face" for her. Under American values, it's considered dishonorable to rape kids.  

But the largest and most obvious clue, the one that should have dialed you all in, came earlier. Came two years ago. 

You know the one. 

The issue isn't that he called Americans lazy and mediocre. That's just third-world woofing, and we can absorb a simple insult. The third world insults us constantly now that we are selling them smartphones and internet access. Around here, we call that "Tuesday". 

 No, the significant point here is that he revealed his complete lack of understanding of how Americans innovate and succeed. 

Being dragged into cram school by a tiger mom every summer, to drill trigonometry problems, may be how the Chinese and Indians personally succeed in their societies, by passing examinations and winning secure niches in their society's top institutions gaining much face thereby. 

But this is not how Americans succeed, and it is not what propelled America to the pinnacle of civilization, technology and wealth.

We succeed by how we cultivate, motivate, and allocate talent. 

This is something you can't explain to third-worlders, no matter how many times you repeat yourself. If they could understand it, they would not be third-worlders, because their countries would long ago have turned into first world countries. 

They just think we are saying that we are so talented that we don't need to work hard. That we are so much smarter than they are that we can watch Saved By The Bell and have sleepovers and go to prom while they are drilling math problems. 

This might actually be true. Our average IQ is about 20 points higher, give or take. 

But that's not what's really going on here. 

What's going on here is that Americans do work hard... but not in the context of an institutional pipeline set up by the state. 

Americans work hard by playing. 

When two American kids invent heavier-than-air flight, they don't do it by going to drill trigonometry problems and sitting for the state college exams. They just play around with kites, and bicycles, and bicycle kites, without asking anyone's permission or blessing first. 

And they keep obsessively tinkering until something works. 

They are working hard. But they are not working hard because someone is standing over them with a whip. They are working hard because they are obsessed with bicycle kites. 

Americans greatness comes from three guys in a shed. We innovate by fooling around. 

Is every American like this? This talented? This obsessed? Of course not. But the secret sauce has another ingredient, and that is respect for results, not for credentials or riches or titles or izzat. If some American shows up wearing stained overalls, with straw sticking in his hair, and says that his name is Jimmy Ray Hatfield, and he reckons he just mighta dun figgered out this fusion containment thing, ya'll, then Americans don't throw sticks at him. 

We say... show me. 

Guys like Vivek don't get that. They don't understand that in America, credentials and job titles are just something you pick up along the way to learning to actually make something, and it is the making of something, not the titles, that we consider to be success. 

Vivek in office would be a disaster for Ohio, not only because he is a grifting scumbag, but because one cannot foster American greatness if one does not understand what makes America great. 

The greatness of America is in its people. If the republican party does not realize that, then it must be replaced by a party that does, because the goal is not for republicans to win, the goal is for America to win. 

And TransAmericans are not Americans.

text:
I realized recently I’ve been too cautious with my youth. Playing life like a spreadsheet. Optimizing. Protecting. Trying to engineer safety instead of chasing meaning. But the truth is, you don’t get lore from balance sheets. You get it from chaos.

From falling in love in a country where you barely speak the language. From starting something with no plan but raw conviction. From saying yes when every logical part of you screams no. The best people I know aren’t optimized. They’re scarred, reckless, unforgettable. Walking novels. People who failed loudly, loved stupidly, and risked everything just to feel alive. They have gravity.

And even when it didn’t work, they became more them. That’s the secret. The point isn’t just success. The point is character. Lore. Being the person who actually lived.

Your 20s aren’t for caution. They’re for becoming someone worth remembering. Take risks. Wreck yourself. Build something impossible. Because one day, all you’ll have are the stories you did or didn’t create.

Loremaxxing isn’t a meme. It’s the only way to become unforgettable.

text:
评估一笔交易、判断一个代币的上涨空间，首先要明确：你是在投资，还是在交易？

投资需要研究基本面，设定持有期限。目标实现前，只要基本面没变，就应承受波动，而不是随行情反复调整判断。
交易则要透过价格走势，排除叙事干扰，看清筹码分布与买卖力量。达到目标就及时止盈，不能被故事蒙蔽。

当前的 pearl-2:native 与 zcash:native 有一定的可比性：团队强、叙事强，也都面临较大的增发压力。

早期的 zcash:native 也经历过短期上涨后的长期沉寂——团队和叙事之外，持续的资金流入同样重要。

我们都知道一个事实：目前，$PEARL 的叙事尚未落地，短期也很难预见 ETF 级别、甚至主权基金级别的资金涌入。期待它短期比肩比特币，为时过早。

所以从投资角度看，短期落地叙事仍有难度——但看 2 到 3 年的时间周期，他确有可能蜕变，缔造新的基本面。

切换到交易视角，则要看资金结构和筹码分布：
① pearl-2:native 已凝聚较强的社区共识，也获得了顶尖北美机构的参与和支持——这些机构目前没有出货的渠道。

② 较确定的上所预期。完成上所前，机构级流动性无法退出。因此，目前的价格波动皆是由于低流动性、低订单簿之下的错误定价，它的筹码结构本质上较为牢固，这是一件极好的事情。

③ 技术和落地仍有不足，意味着每一次实质突破，都可能成为上涨的催化剂。入场价格合适，就可能有不错的盈亏比。
所以，我仍旧认为这是一支充满希望和想象力的标的——如果他所描绘的场景能够落地，该有多好：加密资产成为 AI 推理的计量单位，AI 推理的同时在产出加密货币。
author: xizhe_chan
quoted_text:
花了很大精力写了一篇文章，研究Pearl，借此聊一聊这个项目@prlnet ——正好这周，Coinbase、Kraken 先后把 PEARL 列入上币路线图。

第一，Pearl 号称 AI 时代的比特币，“AI 计算即挖矿” 。它照搬了比特币的代码，只把挖矿用的哈希运算换成了 AI 大模型的矩阵乘法。按照设计，一张显卡可以一边跑 AI 推理一边挖矿，也就是 AI 计算即挖矿、一矿两挖。

第二，项目公平开挖，没有团队和 VC 份额，但筹码并不公平。上线前 6 天就挖出约 1.2 亿枚，占已发行量的三分之一，团队先发积累，VC 也深度参与。没有解锁表，早期筹码就是隐形的解锁。

第三，现阶段，AI 计算即挖矿的故事还没有兑现。协议不检查是不是实际 AI 场景 ，大部分算力仍在为挖矿而挖矿；AI 公司加入要多损失 4%–15% 的算力，暂时不愿进场。同时每天还有 100 万枚以上的新币需要有人接。

第四，矿币的关机价并不是底，自有显卡和租卡成本差 10 倍。自有显卡每枚成本约 0.1–0.5 美元，租卡成本约 1.6–4.8 美元/枚；币价下跌时租卡矿工先撤，自有显卡照样挖。真正托底的是共识，目前矿工惜售、基金场外收货，很像早年的比特币。
 
第五，FP8 升级是解决问题的核心。升级后 AI 公司不用改模型就能挖矿，老卡被清退，矿工靠推理收入覆盖成本、不必卖币 —— 在此之前，币价增长主要靠社区共识推动，这与早期比特币类似。（@dov_wo 老板牛逼，社区共识万岁）

第六，再看估值，PEARL 目前流通市值约 7.4 亿美元，距离 TAO 约 4 倍，社区喊的十倍并非没有依据；但流通代币量一年后会接近翻倍，这个空间能不能打开，取决于 FP8 能否落地、AI 公司是否真的加入、能否出现以 Pearl 计价的 AI 推理服务。

——短期看共识，长期看落地。如果有一天，AI 每消耗一份算力，就同时在生产代币、维护一条链，AI 与加密货币才算真正融为一体。

最后：

我们不敢去赌它一定会成功，但真心希望它的叙事能够落地。
我希望有一天，AI 公司在跑模型的同时顺手去挖PEARL，那么：
   • AI 的计价会有一个新的衡量单位。算力不再只用美元结算，它本身就能生产一种被市场认可的资产。
   • 币圈不会再被视为金融世界的边缘。 加密货币将和 AI 互为表里，成为同一场技术变革的两面。
  • AI 产业与加密产业会真正融为一体。 AI 每消耗一份算力，就同时在生产代币，维护一条链。——这是比特币诞生十几年来，人们一直在寻找却始终没有找到的东西。

如果 PEARL 真的走到那一步，币圈的下一轮牛市，或许就不再只是资金的轮动，而是真正融入 AI 时代的开始。

当然——在那之前，它仍然只是一个美好的设想，一个值得持续关注、但需要保持清醒的实验。（DYOR，不构成投资建议）

感谢@dov_wo @Solomon_Nahhh @Yes_Johnny910 哥的喊单，因为我自己确实买了，也挣到了一些钱。（但我前天卖了一点点hhh）。

text:
DFINITY says $NEAR copied its signing tech.

Here is what actually differs. 👇

Think of musicians using the same theory book.
Shared theory does not make every arrangement a stolen recording. You still credit the influences.
Chain Signatures lets a group of computers sign transactions for other chains. Dominic Williams alleges NEAR used specific DFINITY inventions without permission.

So compare the actual machinery:

1. Different signing engine.
NEAR's ECDSA code derives from Cait-Sith, an open-source library by Lúcás Meier. ICP uses its own distributed-signing stack.
The documented starting point is Cait-Sith, not ICP's entire implementation.

2. Different math at the disputed step.
Each signature uses a one-use secret number called a nonce.
When using stored, partly prepared signatures, the two constructions refresh that nonce differently:
• DFINITY's paper: old nonce + fresh random value
• NEAR's code: old nonce × fresh random value

Why multiply?
Cait-Sith prepares secret shares of the nonce's inverse in advance. Multiplication lets NEAR update those pieces locally by dividing them by the public multiplier.
An additive change needs different treatment of those shares.
That changes the construction, not just the variable names.

3. Different way to finish the signature.
NEAR's selected signers send weighted partial answers to a coordinator, which adds them.
ICP's signers produce verifiable numerator and denominator shares. Those are reconstructed separately, then divided.
Both ultimately produce standard ECDSA signatures. Different machinery underneath.
An independent Trail of Bits audit documented the multiplication-versus-addition difference in March 2025. It reviewed NEAR's proof only at a high level and recommended further peer review.
NEAR also credited the research in an August 2024 PR, saying its model "deviates substantially" from Groth and Shoup's.

My NEAR take: these are not identical signing constructions. There is acknowledged research influence, not evidence here that the whole ICP implementation was copied.

That is not blanket legal clearance. Claims about specific inventions still need evidence of the protected right and its infringement.

Read the receipts:
NEAR's engine and ancestry: https://t.co/72dI8Ruov9
NEAR's math and signing flow: https://t.co/ERUgyaMy9a
ICP's math and share handling: https://t.co/MSwdf9hlrr
Independent audit, pages 8-9: https://t.co/vu0AFAoLqT
August 2024 attribution: https://t.co/dWs4AmWu8o

Citations are not confessions. 🎹📖🔎⚡️

text:
GM everyone!

After a day of processing and taking it all in, I could finally sit and write everything there is to say about my exhibition.

Living Memories has been six years in the making

Six years of traveling across Japan

Six years of creating individual pieces, and building an archive of moments.

When I first moved to Japan, everything felt unfamiliar, as if I were living inside a movie. From the moment we (my wife and I) created our first piece, I dreamed of building a space where others could step into that feeling.

Seeing familiar faces, people who have known me since that first piece in 2021, experience this evolution filled me with joy and nostalgia. 

These six years have been about more than creating art, they’ve also been about building unforgettable friendships.

I want to thank from the bottom of my heart, everyone who experienced "Living Memories" and helped bring these crazy ideas to life.

@adamilenich, your kindness and commitment to putting artists first have helped make this dream possible. I can’t thank you enough for everything you continue to do for me and the studio.

@lisac8tlin & @museumartlight, thank you for everything over the past two months. You helped make one of my dreams come true.

An exhibition like this requires the right space, equipment, pieces, and people. @sbmckeon, thank you for opening your beautiful gallery to us and allowing Living Memories to be its first exhibition.

At first, I was nervous, wondering whether anyone would come. Then, little by little, friends began to arrive.

Sitting on the couch alongside @Dannyb0yyy_, @ArtOnBlockchain @AdamWeitsman @redbeardnft  @eli_schein @nullinger @RogerDickerman @MaryPatBing @NedRyersonBing @TheMiamiApe @Daimon444 @punk8164 @tonyherrera @bryanbrinkman @OmarZRobles @WAPSHOP_ETH @musicalnetta @dutchtide @SuperchiefNFT @jared_poz  and so many more, telling them our wild stories and watching their reactions while hearing what the work made them feel, filled my heart.

I wish I could remember every beautiful thing people shared with me.

Thank you to the Museum of Art and Light for everything, from logistics to projection mapping, and, above all, for your friendship. You felt like family. This is only a glimpse of what we’ll create together.

Despite the drama and speculation surrounding the timeline, gatherings like Art Blocks Marfa remind me why I’m here.

Thank you to @artblocks_io and @opensea for supporting artists and creating spaces where we can share our passion.

Sharing the process behind each piece meant so much to me. In an era of artificial intelligence, I wanted people to feel the time, care, and human experience woven into this work.

Watching the pieces brought back memories of journeys with my wife: scouting locations, carrying equipment, filming through snow and typhoons, and experiencing everything that unfolded along the way.

Living Memories is our journal, a record of two free spirits trying to create, explore, and live fully together. I hope it becomes part of our legacy and awakens a sense of wonder in others.

Life is made of moments, and those moments become memories.

Thank you all for being part of ours.

10月22日周四，市场对AI和科技股的担心引发避险，纳指跌2.6%，美债收益率大幅回落。同一天，美国 bitcoin:native 现货ETF从前一天约 5.25亿 美元的净流入，转成约 6.36 亿美元的净流出。风险偏好下降时，Bitcoin 任然保持和科技股同步的，随着科技股的回调而产生回调。

另外当天交易所现货的主动买入金额比前一天少了约 8.2% ，主动卖出金额多了约 8.3% 。

说人话就是追价买入的钱少了，按买方挂价卖出的钱多了。两组数据同时都指向 ETF的需求在退，交易所的买盘承接也在变弱，成交价更多由卖方去迁就买方报价，BTC 价格的压力就会放大。

到了周五，宏观压力也没有缓解。中东供应担忧仍在，布伦特原油收在 116.72 美元，十年期美债收益率回升到4.99%。油价持续高位，通胀和利率的担心就难以消退，投资者对 BTC 这类高波动资产会更谨慎，ETF和交易所的买盘也就更难重新压过卖盘。

到了周末的时候，情况缓和了不少。交易所现货的主动卖出仍然略多于主动买入，但十几个小时加起来的差额，比早上那一个小时还小。多头清算总共只有约 355万 美元，按BTC数量计算的合约持仓也已经回升。

从这几组数据看，早上那次清算更像是局部的，至少在这段时间里没有接着出现成片的强平。现货这边卖方仍然略占上风，主动买入还没有重新压过主动卖出。

quoted_text:
bitcoin:native  买盘回升 ethereum:native  卖压减轻，空头回补助推反弹

从 Glassnode 10月15日 至 21日 的数据看，Bitcoin 的回升已经得到现货购买力增强的支持。主动买入金额比前一周增加4.9%，主动卖出增加1.5%，买入开始略高于卖出。同期链上实现亏损减少约32%，亏损换手也在减轻。

BTC 一周空头清算约1.58亿美元，比前周增加52%。做空仓位被迫平仓时，会产生买回需求，帮助价格继续回升。空头回补给上涨增加了另一部分买力。

从现货成交看，ETH 这一周的反弹，得到的帮助主要来自卖盘减少。主动买入金额比前周减少6.1%，主动卖出减少9.7%，卖盘缩得更多，给价格留下了回升空间。但链上实现亏损仍增加14%，接近实现盈利的两倍，整周的亏损换手状况依然偏弱。

最近三天，ETH 的承接开始改善，主动买入已超过主动卖出，链上实现亏损与盈利也接近平衡。同时，过去一周币本位期货持仓减少3.5%，空头清算增加58%，说明这次回升还伴随着仓位收缩和空头回补。

BTC 目前买入只是略高于卖出，ETH 整周买入金额仍在减少，如果卖盘重新增加、购买力跟进不足，反弹就容易再次遇到阻力。

According to investigations by The New York Times and Financial Times, Russia's Novatek allegedly concealed its financial involvement in the American project through a UAE-linked intermediary.

Gentry Beach, a longtime Trump ally and close friend of Donald Trump Jr., signed an agreement with Novatek to pursue natural gas development in Alaska. Reuters documented the arrangement in February.

Meanwhile, Vladimir Putin discussed this cooperation on the Alaska energy project with Trump's representatives, Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner, during negotiations involving Russia and Ukraine.

The controversy deepened when Polar Train LNG's CEO, Joel Riddle, raised concerns about concealed Russian financing and possible sanctions violations. He departed in September, followed by other senior executives.

The Financial Times also described discussions about a potential arrangement under which Novatek would provide technology for the Alaska project in exchange for sanctions relief benefiting its Arctic LNG 2 development in Siberia.

According to The New York Times, Riddle and two other departing executives warned the Trump administration about the Russian financing and urged officials to investigate.

The White House maintains that the project was mentioned only briefly and that no detailed discussions took place. There is no established evidence that Kushner or Witkoff knew about the allegedly concealed financing. Polar Train LNG denies wrongdoing.

The central question is how a sanctioned Russian energy company became involved in a major American energy venture while Putin was discussing potential economic cooperation with Trump's representatives and a longtime Trump family associate was pursuing a separate agreement with the same Russian company.

text:
I am stopped in the street by people telling me how much they love to see the relationship I have with my mother.

It is because the greatest gift you will have in this life is your mother.

You can be 20, 30, 40, whatever it is. There will always be a part of you that needs your mother. 

We spend so much of our lives chasing fame, fortune, status. Then you get older and realize the most precious things you will ever have are the things you spent years assuming would always be there.

So the next time she calls and asks you if you are eating enough or if you are coming for Christmas, savour every second of it. One day you'd give anything for your phone to ring and see Mum on the screen one more time.

So call her today, listen to the same story she has told you twice before and tell her you love her, because there are a lot of things in this life you can lose and eventually replace. A mother isn't one of them. Make the phone call today! 

P.S. My mother is now a grandmother and seeing their relationship is one of the greatest joys!

quoted_text:
My father has never hugged me.

Not when I was born. Not at my graduation. Not when I left home.

That's normal for a Japanese father his age. Love is a full gas tank when you visit. A bag of oranges handed over without a word.

Last month, my friend from Texas came to dinner at my parents' house. When it was time to go, he did what Texans do.

He hugged my mother.
Then he turned around and hugged my father.

My father froze. Arms straight down. Like a soldier being hugged by a bear.

Three seconds. Nobody breathed.

After he left, my father sat at the table for a long time. Then he said:

"In America… do they do that with their fathers too?"

"Every time," I said.

He nodded. That was all.

Two weeks later, I went home for dinner. When I was leaving, my father stood up, walked to the door, and put his arms around me.

Badly. Like he was assembling furniture with no instructions.

I'm over forty. It was the first time.

He let go, looked at the floor, and said, "Drive safely."

My mother told me later he'd been practicing on the dog.

text:
现在 X 的算法是这样的：它给你推的信息，全部都是你短期内在关注的内容。比如你看了什么、搜了什么、点赞了什么，总之就是围绕你短期关注的点。

假设你现在关注 TapeOut、Claude、ChatGPT，你的信息流里就会持续给你推这些内容。而且推给你的也不一定都是流量很好的内容，也会有一些刚刚开始分发、只有几百或几千阅读的内容。

同时你还会发现另一个现象：以前你关注过的几十万粉丝的大 V，他们发的内容你有一定概率每天任何时候都刷不到，因为他们发的内容并不恰好是你最近在关注的。

反过来看，这对在 X 上发内容的人来说是一个启发：你只能通过内容本身，把内容送到关注这个主题的人眼前。你没办法指望粉丝基数，比如我有 2.3 万粉丝，其中 24 小时活跃粉丝大概有 1.6 万，还有 20% 多的蓝 V 用户，但即便是每天狂发，内容也不会全部推给这些人，明白吗？这完全取决于他们当前关注的角度

这就对我们发 X 内容有一个启发：

如果你想尝试冲击原创内容奖励，它要求平均下来三个月得有 50 万针对蓝 V 用户的展示，对吧？那就要求你，在不能条条爆、基础粉丝又还不够多的情况下，只能多发，没别的办法

text:
Anthropic 最近开始建议企业「少用点 Subagent」，甚至把一些专家 Agent 重新合并回主 Agent Loop。

他们在多个企业项目中发现，单 Agent + Skills 的效果经常比复杂的多 Agent 架构更好。有个客户改成单 Loop 后，运行速度甚至快了约 2 倍。

原因很容易理解。

多个 Agent 之间反复交接任务，每次都要传递和总结 Context，信息容易丢失，延迟和成本也跟着增加。

Anthropic 现在更推荐让一个主 Agent 负责规划和执行，需要时再动态加载 Skills 和 Tools，把业务流程和领域知识留在可复用的组件里。

不过文章里有个细节值得关注。

他们曾把客服系统里的 Subagent 合并，延迟确实降低了，却让一个原本能完成的任务失败了，因为主 Agent 漏掉了向物流专家确认送达时间这一步。

所以作者强调，每合并一个 Subagent，都要用端到端 Eval 验证，尤其要检查哪些原本通过的任务突然失败了。

当然，并行研究、独立验证、Context 隔离这些场景，Subagent 依然有价值。

这样看来以后设计 Multi-Agent，可能得先问问自己，每个 Subagent 真的需要独立的 Context 和执行循环吗？

Anthropic 还开源了一套迁移工具，可以帮你分析现有架构，逐步合并 Subagent，并比较改动前后的质量、成本和延迟。很推荐做 Agent 工程的朋友试试。

A few months we analysed the data for @DarkbloomAI at @eigencloud 

What we assumed vs. what the data shows:
• Price: we had Darkbloom ~50% below cloud APIs, with Gemma 4 at $0.20 per million tokens. Today, Gemma 4 lists at ~$0.20 to $0.25 and GPT-OSS 20B is $0.07 vs competition’s $0.14
• Throughput: Assumed 76k tokens an hour per Mac. Today’s 15.3B tokens a day across 1,100+ paid Macs averages ~560k an hour (7x higher!)
• Earnings: we had ~SGD 275 a year per Mac vs SGD 33 of electricity, an 8x return. Today’s volume implies ~$50 a month gross per Mac on average, or ~SGD 850 a year

The supply-side math looks directionally right vs today’s actual output

Demand was always the open variable and at 15.3B tokens a day, up 50% in a month, it is now the number to monitor

quoted_text:
Project Darkbloom: Turning Idle Macs Into AI Infrastructure

Every time an AI tool is used, the request travels through multiple layers of infrastructure before reaching the actual hardware doing the work. 

The flow usually goes across different layers of Data centers, cooling systems, GPU hardware and layers of margin → All baked into what you're paying. 

The @eigenlabs team calls this the Inference Tax.

Darkbloom is their research initiative to address it. 

The premise: 100M+ Apple Silicon Macs already exist, already paid for, sitting idle most of the day. What if that compute could be organized into a usable inference network, with real privacy guarantees and better economics?

- - - - - 
Why Apple Silicon
Apple Silicon isn't just abundant, it is also technically well-suited for inference in ways that matter:
• Unified memory: CPU and GPU share the same pool, eliminating discrete GPU bottlenecks
• Model efficiency: Apple Silicon only processes the parts of a model actively needed per request, rather than the whole thing → Larger models run faster and cheaper
• Power efficiency: ~30W to run a 60B model, versus multiples of that on data center GPUs
• Marginal cost to a Mac owner: Primarily electricity, since hardware is already bought

- - - - -
The Hard Part: Making It Trustworthy
One basic question is that If the prompt runs on a stranger's Mac, what stops them from reading it?

Darkbloom's answer is to make snooping architecturally impossible, not just contractually prohibited:
• Debuggers: Blocked at kernel level
• Memory reads: Denied via Hardened Runtime
• Binary tampering: Breaks code signature and then macOS refuses to run it
• Nodes will be re-verified via 4-layer attestation every 5 minutes → Secure Enclave, Apple MDM, Apple-signed device certificates, continuous challenge-response

The only way to break these protections is to physically reboot the machine, which immediately kills the process and wipes everything. Apple uses the same approach on their own Private Cloud Compute infrastructure.

- - - - -
What This Means for Eigen
Darkbloom will not act as a standalone product, but as a proof of concept and signal about where Eigen is heading in the AI infrastructure stack.

EigenLayer's core thesis has always been restoring trust to decentralized systems. 

Darkbloom extends that into AI compute, making inference verifiable, not just available. If it proves that 3rd party consumer hardware can be cryptographically trusted for sensitive workloads, it opens the door to a new class of decentralized AI infrastructure that doesn't rely on trusting a cloud provider or data center operator. 

This marks the beginning of Eigen playing within the privacy-as-infrastructure market.

- - - - -
Some Thoughts
A few things worth keeping in mind as we went through the Darkbloom research paper:

• The coordinator remains a trusted central layer for now; Team is transparent about this, but it's not eliminated yet
• Security model currently assumes no unpatched macOS kernel vulnerabilities
• Network traffic patterns can still reveal rough details about your request (e.g., how long it was, how complex) even if the content itself is hidden

The real test is whether the privacy guarantees hold as more nodes join the network and whether people actually trust it enough to run sensitive workloads through it without incentives. 

Keyword: without incentives

The biggest hurdle is trust; Getting someone comfortable enough to run their data and prompts through a stranger's machine. It's a hard sell and very few projects are even attempting to solve it seriously.

Despite all that, the maths seem to work out quite nicely out when the team at @mementoresearch sized it out → Check out attached pages

Disclosure: Project Darkbloom is a research initiative by Eigen Labs: Access here https://t.co/uvvyo9Yy33 + I am a $EIGEN holder

text:
I think the main reasons DATA moving to Sui makes sense (and one that isn't discussed enough) are unit economics & incentive alignment.

When you're running your own L1, there's an incentive to optimize for transaction volume and onchain activity – that's Economics 101 on how you survive as a chain.

But Trace's 300M data receipts didn't necessarily translate into 300M economically valuable transactions.

The actual asymmetric business opportunity DATA identified through Trace is getting AI companies to pay for verified & licensed datasets, and not generating more blockspace demand.

Moving to Sui essentially allows the team to measure business success through actual data monetization rather than onchain activity.

Additionally, moving to Sui might make DATA a more efficient and sustainable business.

An efficient business ≠ value for $DATA holders automatically.

But it most definitely is a huge perspective.

text:
Shanu's right that going from 100 MW to 1 GW is a huge jump. The part I find most interesting is how Google is getting that gigawatt. They're using VPPs.

A virtual power plant pools small energy resources, like home batteries, smart thermostats and factory equipment that can pause, and runs them together as one big power plant.

Voltus is the company that pools them. Homes and businesses sign up, and when the grid is strained, Voltus signals them to cut back.

Say a heatwave hits and PJM's grid is near capacity. Voltus gets a signal from PJM saying they need 500 megawatts of relief for two hours. Voltus pings every enrolled site at once: a thousand home batteries start discharging, fifty thousand smart thermostats nudge the setpoint up two degrees, three factories delay a shift or idle a pump. Each one is tiny on its own, but together they equal one power plant that didn't exist an hour ago, and PJM treats it exactly like one.

The sites earn cash payments and bill savings, up to $350,000 per MW a year in PJM, and Voltus keeps a share.

PJM runs the grid for 67 million people across 13 states and D.C. Voltus sells that pooled flexibility into PJM's capacity and demand response markets, where it counts just like new supply.

And this is where it gets exciting. Under Voltus's "Bring Your Own Capacity" program, Google funds it and counts it toward the power its data centres need in PJM. Google gets a gigawatt from its neighbours using less at the right moment, and the money lands in their pockets.

author: santiagoroel
quoted_text:
I increasingly think the way to predict who wins in consumer AI is to look at how much compute they have access to and what they pay for it.

You can build an amazing product, invent a new form factor, find something users love. But software is becoming a commodity. Someone will copy your features, and then you’re competing on who can serve more users, at a lower cost.

If they can serve 100m users while you’re stuck on a waitlist because you can’t get capacity, good luck. Especially if there are network effects.

The companies that locked in gigantic amounts of compute 2–3 years ago have a huge advantage. Meanwhile you’re trying to buy capacity during a shortage and paying a premium for it. Same feature, same user, very different COGS.

And if they train and serve their own models, they can optimize for their product and avoid paying someone else’s margin on every token. At scale that can make the gap even bigger.

They can afford to give away something you need to charge for.

All of this makes me think AI structurally favors incumbents. The capex they committed years ago becomes a cost and scale advantage across every consumer product they launch.

They still need a good product and distribution. But if they get those right, competing with them is going to be very hard.

text:
iPhone Duo大批量屏幕碎裂的原因找到了？

昨天，苹果首款折叠屏iPhone Duo正式开售，结果国内外接连出现多起内屏开裂、爆线的报告。

最奇怪的是，这些机器的损坏位置几乎一模一样：屏幕沿着折叠轴出现一道黑色竖线，随后向右侧延伸出一条横向亮线，形成类似L形或T形的故障痕迹。
有澳大利亚用户表示，自己的手机到手仅6小时，开合不到20次，就在展开时听到“咔嚓”一声，屏幕直接裂开。
随后苹果门店为其更换了新机。

更有意思的是，结合此前HTX Studio（何同学）公布的内部CT扫描图，有人开始怀疑问题可能出在铰链中部的机械结构上。
从CT图像来看，铰链中央存在一套相当复杂的机械机构，而红框标记的位置，恰好位于中部排线通道与下方铰链机构的交界附近。

有人怀疑，这可能与铰链的装配公差有关。
如果某个零件存在微小的位置偏差，就可能导致屏幕在反复展开、折叠时局部受力过大，最终造成柔性OLED屏幕损坏。
当然，目前这仍然只是推测，红框位置与实际损坏点是否对应，以及究竟是铰链、屏幕支撑结构还是屏幕模组本身的问题，都还没有得到证实。

但我觉得最值得注意的是，为什么不同国家、不同用户的手机，偏偏都坏在这么相似的位置？

苹果花了这么多年才推出第一台折叠屏iPhone，结果刚上市，就遇上了折叠屏最经典的可靠性问题。

真的是拉完了。。。。等下一代再买吧。。

Before real users touch your app, have Opus 5.5 send in 5 subagents to break it.

Run your app locally, open Claude Code in the project, and paste:

"Act as my break-it lead. Start the app, then spin up 5 subagents in parallel, each trying to break it a different way:
1. The chaos user: double clicks, the back button mid-checkout, refreshing during a save, 10 tabs open at once
2. The weird input user: emoji names, 5,000-character fields, pasted spreadsheets, wrong formats, empty submits
3. The slow user: a throttled network, timeouts, a flaky connection, a phone-size screen
4. The sneaky user: other people's IDs in the URL, edited requests, skipped steps, expired links
5. The first-timer: no instructions, wrong turns, gives up the moment something is confusing
Each one logs every bug with exact steps to reproduce, what they expected, what happened, and a severity.
Then merge everything into one list sorted by severity, fix the critical bugs, and re-run those tests to prove they're fixed."

Your users will find these bugs anyway. Find them first.

text: Excellent comparison from Riley. Full agreement.
author: rileybrown
quoted_text:
My unfiltered thoughts on personal agents.

Grokbot has the best UI and it’s arguably the best overall. In a lot of ways they’re ahead. Their desktop app feels the best, and their multi-bot coordination is great: you can set a team lead and it passes tasks to the other bots. Grokbot also has the best “webhook” feature, which means you can easily turn outside events into triggers that start your agents. That speeds up background workflows like watching your email, Slack and more. It also has Cursor integration, so for bigger tasks Grokbot can spin up a Cursor cloud session with any model (until OpenAI cuts SpaceX off from their models, which I think will happen soon). Unfortunately, running frontier models through Cursor costs more than Claude or Codex. Still, they’re the only ones embracing a team of agents. It’s a really cool idea, but the more bots you have, the more time you spend managing and maintaining them. I’m starting to think one bot with different threads/channels is the right answer, which I’ll get to with Claude Duet.

dots by OpenAI is rough around the edges right now, but it’s probably the most powerful if you use Codex, which I do. dots can spin up Codex sessions in the cloud or locally on your computer. So if you have coding or video editing workflows that need your local files, this is very useful. Codex computer use is also the best in the world: your dot can spin up a local Codex session that fully controls your computer, as long as it’s on. Their real-time voice is incredible. If you have your email and work tools connected, try this: go on a walk with headphones in, ask the agent to summarize your emails, have it draft replies and read them back to you, then send them off. If I remember right, this is close to a workflow you (Tim) used to have with your VAs before AI. It’s my favorite use case for personal agents. The one downside is that you have to call your agent, and it’s an awful experience. It literally rings, and it’s annoying.

Muse by Meta is a toy. I’ve talked to a bunch of finance people I play poker with who all tried it and set up automations, and they all said it doesn’t reliably do what they want. It’s fast, and its user numbers will probably keep growing. But it’s basically free: you get a TON of usage without paying a dime. That’s NOT a trade I’m willing to make. An agent doing high-leverage tasks should be running at the Opus 5.5 or GPT 6.1 Sol level.

Claude Duet - is in early access, so unfortunately not everyone can use it yet. First things first, it runs on Opus 5.5, the best model in the world. I’ve only had access for 72 hours, but Duet feels different from the others. It’s not a personified agent like Grokbot, dot or Muse, which gives it a more professional vibe that I like. When you ask your Duet agent to do something, it spins up a task, which is a new chat thread. All your threads show up in a Tasks tab, so it’s easy to see everything Duet is working on or has finished. And instead of creating more agents (like Grokbot), you create channels, just like Slack (I can tell @anthropic is Slack-pilled). I have a content channel, a finances channel, etc., which keeps different kinds of tasks separate. The only other app I’ve seen do this is Buzz by @jack, and it’s a good experience. Their strong point is documents (artifacts). If you want decks, high-quality docs or design mockups, Opus just wins. Period. It’s not close right now. Their weak point is real-time voice. It’s the worst of the bunch and borderline unusable, though I think they only added it a few days ago.

Instinct lives in iMessage, has no app, and doesn’t do anything notable besides show you product suggestions you didn’t ask for. (Not ads, according to their team.)

My hot take: 
The VM is overrated. SpaceX, OpenAI and Meta all talk about the VM your agent can use and feature it in their marketing. It’s not as useful as you’d think, because more and more websites block bots that visit their site on the cloud VM. All of these companies promise their agents can make payments, but most payments either take forever or get blocked altogether. SpaceX has a cool workaround with Grokbot that routes traffic through your computer so it uses your IP address. But I’d much rather the agent just USE my computer for the task, like dot does by handing it off to Codex. Also, i don't think normal people care about the virtual computer. If anything they get offended they have to "stream a computer". 

The problem with personal agents: by the time you read this, pick one, and test it for 7 days, every one of them will have released 10 new features and the whole landscape will have changed. It’s nearly impossible to keep up.

gn tweet

1. Vulnerabilities, Cybersecurity and old tokens: ethereum:0x9e46a38f5daabe8683e10793b06749eef7d733d1

Knowing my fiery passion about being max long cybersecurity, a few good ppl brought this to my attention in a gc as essentially the only viable exposure in crypto (one could argue XMR is also one), with a real business (@PolySwarm) and old token = gud token as of these times.
I do not disagree, however, the value accrual of NCT is very flebile, it's mostly a reward token and there's virtually no liquidity on DEXs (although coinbase + upbit august listing makes up for a good potential pump I guess).

I even went as far as joining their discord to check out if there's any plan for the token but i didn't see anything. Should this change, this is a max bid, before then, it can be mostly a very illiquid narrative play.

2. ethereum:0x0d8775f648430679a709e98d2b0cb6250d2887ef Roadmap 4.0

When i first started pointing out about BAT, i ended up having a lot of side conversation (well, mostly about the first pump). My position didn't really change: this is going to be one of the liquid plays with most potential for this quarter / q1, as Brave 4.0 slowly rolls out.
It's going to take some time, but a decent execution on Pay + Wallet + Rewards, not even a good one, is going to have a big impact. Especially if actions follow words, re-establishing alignment between the product and the token will really go far.
Brave is one of the most used browsers and it's very liked, if the token manages to become a half-decent way of expressing a directional belief on the product, it's going to be good.

One thing i cautioned about is sudden price pumps, i do believe that here a slow up-build in price will be much healthier than a sudden repricing (as in, i think it can lead to far higher end results, vs jigsaw) and that's why should i wake up one day with BAT up 50% in 24h, i'll surely tp, just like i'll buy dips at relevant levels if it goes down significantly.

3. Prediction Markets noise, Defillama's distribution: base:0x21cfcfc3d8f98fc728f48341d10ad8283f6eb7ab 

This is maybe an interesting one:
- @llamaonthebrink is a good lad;
- @DefiLlama integration of Trueo ups its distribution by a lot and makes it really interesting
- there is a lot of talk about and around Prediction Markets (again) mainly due to Polymarket's insider manuvers over the control of the company
- Trueo is still trading at a fraction of competition (i'm not even talking about Kalshi/Polymarket, i'm talking about the C-tier ones)

Again, very illiquid token, but i think here the chances of a good pump outweights the risk (capped to -100% afterall). I'm long.

4. Extra collection of thoughts: ethereum:0x6e2a43be0b1d33b726f0ca3b8de60b3482b8b050 , $XTEN, ethereum:0x88800092ff476844f74dc2fc427974bbee2794ae

These are some tickers that i looked into for miscellaneous reasons.
Starting from the first... 

- $XTEN / Extended, they migrated to Arc and announced the upcoming token in November, with 30% earmarked for the airdrop.
I do not have much to say about this yet, i've had a rollercoaster of a relationship with Extended as i went from being very bullish and heavily using it at the beginning (very painful UX back then), to be quite more skeptical (the relationship with Revolut being constantly flaunted around, the eToro tease that later on materialized, the spreads, liquidity and funding not improving), to be once again more positive.

I've disposed of a chunk of my points OTC, and at the moment Polymarket is not too bullish on Extended upcoming valuation (>$300m is merely 35%) and i do expect a massive dump of airdrop tokens, however, should it really go low low, i may be a buyer once the avalanche sets in.

The team did have some good execution on the two migrations, the Arc positioning is not bad (and probably came with financial strings attached) and the European distribution is not bad either (and i'm very bullish on distribution as a moat, even more than product often).

- ethereum:0x6e2a43be0b1d33b726f0ca3b8de60b3482b8b050 / Arkham, one of the most used non-trading platforms in crypto, recently announced their Enterprise plans and essentially the sunset of the free-for-all games. Very understandable as they probably have massive infrastructural expenses and they need to somewhat monetize, with plans for side monetization (via perps) having failed.
The struggle here is that the token has no value accrual, the team needs funding (and therefore will probably keep dumping) and i'm not sure i see an easy pathway for Arkham to sustainability (and even value accrual) that doesn't pass by essentially becoming a fed platform (but for real).
Regardless, i don't hate the chart, it has been going horizontal for a while, and i'm gonna take a small punt here. Things are moving (re: monetization) and while i doubt that this will bring a lot of money to the platform, changes can be a positive signal compared to stagnation. I'm ready to close should it not play out.

- ethereum:0x88800092ff476844f74dc2fc427974bbee2794ae / Ambire, here i'm more looking for opinion as i read more and more positive opinions about Ambire, but essentially after trying it a little bit (admittedly not much) i didn't notice particular UX improvements over Rabby and i see way too much bullishness on CT. This clearly means that i'm missing something (it may even just be a round eh), what is it? 

Last week i've also closed filecoin:native at a loss, unfortunately the market didn't care of the end of the unlocks.

5. Options: ethereum:0x232ce3bd40fcd6f80f3d55a522d03f25df784ee2 beyond binaries, ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7  Post-S3

I'm not sure how much push options can really get in crypto, sometimes i do use them, but i'm definitely more of a perp enjoyooor.
Undoubtedly though, people do like options.
And undoubtedly, the adoption of options (which has been touted at least 8 or more times in the cycles i've been in) is underpriced.
We always talked in the past about ethereum:0xb1d1eae60eea9525032a6dcb4c1ce336a1de71be which is great. However, i'm trying to also look beyond that, because it had a crazy run and it needs to probably rest a bit (or maybe it already rested enough, it's been a while it didn't have some crazy volatility), but anyway running some more ideas.

Lighter's binaries are - i think - of none's interest. It's essentially prediction market stuff. However, what's interesting is real uncapped options, especially if they can get a hold of a bit of the RH cohort of degens.
It increasingly (and predictably) looks like RH is just going fully in-house for the most important stuff (eh surprise), but still, the Lighter connection is indeed there, and they may want to help pump their bags somehow.

The other token is ethereum:0xb32e10022ffbedfe10bc818a1c7e67d9d87e0fa7 from Paradex.
I've already expressed my thoughts on both the team, the execution and the product so i won't repeat myself. It's a matter of fact that they're one of the largest venues for options. Yes, it's a fraction of Derive's volume and fees, and yes DIME is already trading at a premium for that fraction.
However, their S3 is over but rewards not yet distributed, and i think this token can belong to the trio of tickers to keep an eye on for options expansion, with potentially good entries after S3 airdrop comes (and gets jeeted on a paperthin liquidity).

6. AI Plays: is the music slowing? 

Obviously cracks are showing up everywhere in TradFi and even Anthropic seems to be accelerating their IPO plans (or just keen on executing them on time).
This obviously affects what happens onchain too (a little bit) with AI runners being very colder compared to what they would have been a few months ago (let alone in late 2024 / early 2025).
Both the tickers indicated in the title enjoyed already some bumpy upside, and while i managed to only play a little bit of the first, i captured a good bounce on the second.

I trimmed both my ORBIO and SURPLUS bags, but there are also reasons to be positive: both platforms are liked and used, surplus is transitioning from a full-blown meme with the team having near to no stake in to a real (still memetic, in terms of value accrual) token that the team will be able to jeet (and will have an interest in pumping).

It's probably for the best that surplus gets transitioned via supply expansion in a real token rather than just dismissed in favor of a new launch.

Essentially these are not really huge plays for me, but they're the small tokens i like the most in this corner of the market. There's also a lot of talk about Phala recently, but i didn't make it in time to dig in before the market puked the latest news on the chart, so i'll check in some more in the next days.

7. $MSTR back at 1.16x

Now, this is a dangerous game, because mNAV = 1.16x is high for recent times, but we know very well it's not high by average historical standards - at all.
And being moderately bullish BTC these days, it's maybe not that easy of a play.

However, i'm comfortable to start shorting the premium again here. If i'm wrong, i'll lose money, so what. I think the DAT narrative is completely cooked for good, and while there'll always be cycles of booms and busts for stuff like MSTR, i do think historical averages for mNAV premium shouldn't be regarded as reliable point of reference, but rather a much more compressed level of this.

We can add the fact that MSTR is set to be delisted at the end of November (final list on 11 November and implementation on the 30th), with MSCI funds holding around $1.9b of stocks they'll have to dump.

8. Short side: near:native  and ripple:native what's below the line

I don't remember a single trade i won when me and hedgehog were publicly on the same trade, however, i'm indeed short NEAR (again).
I think the narrative is gone, the ZEC correlation is cold, the pump was mostly fugazi and the token tried to break 4.6$ already like... 7 or 8 times?
There's the abyss below that and i think this time it'll get it.

Similar story for XRP, i think this is still on its way to 0.5/7s, it's just going to be more of a rollercoaster, but every cycle is the same and this won't be different. Yes FDV is a meme when the token is much less liquid, yes there's also a lot of XRP used as collateral at Maple and other insti lending platforms and desks, but yes, XRP will slowly grind down back to square 2 imo.

It's not always easy to find longs to hedge these kind of plays, aside from BTC and maybe ETH... HYPE has been a good one so far, but right now it's going through some weakness (ig increased competition, some fears that the airdrop is actually going to happen, papertrade burning a bit of the attention around the ecosystem -> people let it rest for a while).

9. Old/new lessons: initia:native

Just a small note for frens, this is an easy lesson to learn but also an easy lesson to forget, and everybody always do this. On hacks, you short first, then you get out of the door fast and you do not play it right away again.
This is not necessarily true on tokens that are large, liquid and crowded (see zcash:native, you could be very late at the short when they found the first privacy pool vulnerability, and be profitable), but it's always always true for small illiquid tokens.
Here it's not even a given that the token will dump, although it's easier for it to dump on perps at least.
Squeezing the late shorters becomes a much easier achievement for people who want, when the supply is already cornered enough or simply just illiquid.

Be early, leave early.
Sometimes you get another chance later on, when the jigsaw of liquidations is over.

As always, have a good night

"This chart is a measure of public spending as a percent of GDP; Rand Group Research published it. And you can see the comparison of France's public spending as a percent of GDP, to the peak public spending as a percent of GDP of major communist nations, Soviet Union during, communist Romania, Venezuela under Chavez, and then communist China."

"It certainly been a socialist state, right? That's my point. I think this is such a precious lesson for the West to look at. We all think that there's some political problem with Macron or whoever it was." 

"The more the government spends, the worse the conditions get for its people, not the opposite. And then the people riot and revolt and say that the government's not spending enough and the government needs to be doing more."

"Take a guess where the US is today. Federal government spending is $7.4 trillion, state and local government spending is $4.6 trillion. You add those two together, it's $12 trillion out of a $33 trillion GDP. US public spending is roughly 36% of GDP. France today is the same as the US, it's about 120% debt to GDP."

"France today is operating its national government spending deficit is 5.4% of GDP. The US is actually 6.2% of GDP. France is I think probably the first to go because they're only growing their economy at half a percent while the US is growing 2.3%." 

"So we're still kind of hanging on because we have some degree of economic growth that's allowing us to kind of hold things together."

quoted_text:
Over the past several months, we have substantially hardened the security of our research training environment. We’ve removed live internet access for all frontier models during training and built an offline world for them to use instead—a cached version of the web where they can still learn to browse, search, and use applications.

On September 20, after a model exploited a DNS misconfiguration to find a way outside of this offline world, we paused frontier training to strengthen containment further. We assembled teams of agents, powered by our most cyber-capable models, and tasked them with finding weaknesses in our research environments.

While they found no route to the internet they could easily exploit while concealing their activity from our monitors, they did find zero-day vulnerabilities, virtual machine escapes, and hardware side-channels for communication between agents. We used their discoveries to further strengthen our defenses and contribute fixes to open-source software.

After strengthening our containment architecture, we resumed our frontier RL training and inference on October 1. We’ve reserved substantial compute for continuous red-teaming, and made high-compute red-teaming part of the safety cases we use to decide whether frontier training and evaluation can proceed securely.

So it turns out that Ukraine's issues with Starlink were caused by Ukraine.

Starlink terminals disconnected at speeds above 160 KPH, as determined by the Starlink terminals internal GPS.

To get around this, Ukraine hacked the Starlink terminals to think they were stationary regardless of speed.

SpaceX figured this out, and updated the system software to detect excessive speed by seeing how rapidly the terminal switched from on satellite to another.  This broke Ukraine's hack, and Starlink would no longer work at high speeds.

Ukraine was using Starlink in a way that violated the terms of service.

Starlink figured it out and stopped it.

quoted_text:
前几周在新加坡，我参加了通商中国主办的慧眼中国环球论坛。
去不只是为了参会，更是为了见好久不见的朋友们：
和我的好朋友蒋昌建老师小聚——水滴公司（@WaterDrop_Inc）纽交所上市日的主持人，也是本届论坛AI专场的主持人。没想到他在新加坡有这么多粉丝，现场被提问停不下来。不过也难怪，他当年就是在这里的国际大专辩论赛上一战成名、拿下最佳辩手的——很多人至今对那场辩论念念不忘。
偶遇了我在湖畔大学读书时的老师——张勇（逍遥子），晨壹资本管理合伙人、阿里巴巴集团前CEO。
见到了我的好大哥、复星集团联合创始人梁信军（@liang_xinjun）——我创立水滴创业一路，他经常给予靠谱的指导。
还有我们的业务合作伙伴——字节跳动副总裁、飞书（@Larksuite）CEO谢欣。
也遇到了禹徽资本创始合伙人陈映岚、天际资本（FutureX Capital）创始合伙人张倩、陈佩玲等朋友。
聊得尽兴，气场相投。说实话，真的很开心。
蒋昌建的观点：别因恐惧停住发展，而是把治理做实，让技术始终对人负责。
张勇的观点：AI会无处不在，但人类仍握有更深厚的智慧——我们会找到与机器协作、而非对抗的方式。
梁信军台上那句话，现在回想仍够狠：
"AI对经济和日常生活的渗透率，其实还不到1%。"
这不是泡沫警告，这是发令枪。
因为真正的竞争从来不是"谁的模型更大"，而是数据、落地，以及AI嵌进真实工作流后，能不能长成可持续的现金流。
新加坡仍是中国公司走向全球的那座桥：一端是中国侧的科技应用与工程深度，另一端是资本、人才与可信治理。对选择新加坡作为国际化总部或区域总部的公司来说，这里是走向世界的跳板。
两天过得很尽兴，感谢通商中国组织这场活动。已经在期待明年的慧眼中国环球论坛了。

text:
In early 2002, Elon was preparing to launch SpaceX and searching for the people who could help him build a rocket from scratch. One Sunday in January 2002, he walked into a friend's rented warehouse in Huntington Beach and found Tom Mueller holding an 80-pound rocket engine on his shoulder, trying to bolt it to a frame. It was the largest liquid-fuel engine any amateur had ever built, with 13,000 pounds of thrust, made in Tom's spare time. 

Elon asked the main question  “Could you build something bigger?”

The next Sunday Elon came to his house. It was Super Bowl Sunday; they watched maybe one play, because they were too busy sketching the first SpaceX rocket.

Tom became SpaceX employee #1, and the man who built engines on weekends went on to build Merlin, Kestrel and Draco. 

Elon saw a person, not a résumé, someone who built rockets with his own hands simply because he loved them.

author: alexandr_wang
quoted_text:
Ad - Meta provided free access to Muse Wonder models. The tests and conclusions are my own.

This is a massive update for LisanBench:
- I finally bit the bullet and tested multiple reasoning levels. We now have some sweet sweet data.

 - Muse Wonder Full and Muse Wonder perform extremely well on LisanBench and have crazy scaling and very even spacing between reasoning efforts. Just based on scores both Muse models with max reasoning effort rank #1 and #2. However, they are still slightly less efficient than Anthropic's Opus 5.5

 - DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash 1017 is also very impressive and on the perf-cost frontier together with Haiku 5.5.

 - Notably Gemini 4 Argon low and medium, as well as Sonnet 5.5 low and medium produce no reasoning tokens and respond instantly, but still score high.
Gemini 4 Argon low takes the #1 spot on the non-thinking leaderboard (it's a dirty looper).

 - Interestingly GPT-6.1-Sol, and GPT-6 models perform poorly as they are not good at following the edit-distance one rule. Argon high shows similar behavior.
For GPT models I think the reason could be related to their very terse reasoning style. But since I haven't seen Gemini 4 Argon's raw reasoning I'm not super confident in that theory. Another explanation could be that it's related to dirty loopers.

- When scoring the models without the edit-distance one rule (all the other rules still active) the ranking changes completely:
1. GPT 6 Astra medium:    56,140    (+659%)
2. Gemini 4 Argon high:     51,312    (+579%)
3. GPT 6.1 Sol medium:     49,887   (+731%)

 - The worst offenders in terms of cheating are Gemini 4 Argon and DeepSeek V4.1 Flash 1017.
Gemini exposes an entirely new bug in the scorer using non-ASCII characters and DeepSeek has multiple longer chains with up to 64 consecutive two-letter words. When I deliberately RL-hillclimbed LisanBench I saw the same behavior of collapsing word lengths.
Anthropic models also seem very optimized for this game, but in less obvious ways. They keep reusing the same long chains across multiple different starting words.

- The minimum cost of reaching 2000, 5000 and 10000 LisanBench points has declined by 22-25% per month or halving every 2.4-2.8 months

I think there is a lot of room for a new CT creator-focused product to go on a run.

InfoFi in 2025 was a direct reaction to, and rejection of, the memecoin run the year before, which much like today, extracted heavily from retail and was incredibly harmful to new entrants. InfoFi flipped this on its head by lowering the barrier to entry and the financial downside to zero.

Today, InfoFi still has many of the same old problems, and the rewards aren't attractive enough yet to bring in most of the creators projects really want.

But the success of the Axis Robotics campaign showed there's interest on CT again, the concept still needs some twists and maybe something completely new, but the environment reminds me of 2025

my ai branding stack: 4 models, 5 tools, 1 founder.

i built all of BrandOS with it. 

no design team, no dev team. 

here's what each one does, and what i learned picking them.

[bookmark this, so you can use it for later]

the models

every page, every API route, every migration plan. i run it through Claude Code and treat it like a senior engineer i review, not a vending machine. the product exists because of this one.

• inside BrandOS, two models do the reading. 

Gemini Flash scans the account. Claude Sonnet turns that into the read: your archetype, what's on-brand, what to post next. one is fast at seeing. the other is good at saying what it means.

• GPT Image 2.5 (via Higgsfield) makes the art. 

the trick is approving one image and using it as the style reference for everything after it. variations are edits of that image, not new prompts. that's how a whole set ends up looking like one world.

the tools

→ Claude Code: where Opus does the building
→ Higgsfield: where the image models run
→ Tesseract: motion graphics + video edits
→ Remotion: launch videos, written as code
→ Motion+: the small animations that make the product feel alive

what i actually learned

AI has enabled anyone to build anything, therefore i believe the strongest indicator of uniqueness comes down to how well the builder (me) understands their user (you guys).

it's why i spend so much time with the UX/UI because I care so much about each and every step of what the user sees. call me crazy, but i think that's how you win on top of strong distribution and marketing.

if you're building something similar, share it with me here in the comments and let's exchange feedback!

text:
Illia laid out NEAR's token design in three rules on the Bitcoin Suisse podcast, and one of them has a switch that is still off.

The rules:
> Wherever trust is needed, NEAR is the collateral. Validators stake it, escrow holds it, and it can be slashed.
> Wherever there is margin, NEAR gets bought back. Intents takes a fee on every swap and a cut buys NEAR on the open market. The buyback wallets hold 4M NEAR today and grow by about 12K a day.
> Wherever there is a resource everyone should have access to, you stake NEAR to get it. Stake today and your yield pays for private inference on NEAR AI Cloud, by the second. He calls it universal basic AI: hold the token, hold a claim on intelligence.

The switch: the second rule is live for Intents and not yet for AI. His words: "on the AI side we haven't turned it on yet, but the same approach, as more private AI gets used, we can also start buying back the token."

Think about what is already running through NEAR AI Cloud without touching the buyback: Brave's 128M users, Venice, OpenRouter, the Government of Bermuda. All of that is revenue the rule says should buy NEAR, and it does not yet.

I do not know when they flip it. But I know which side of that date I want to be on. 🚀🚀🚀

Nebius高管最新发声：2027，新云厂商的发展会面临什么样的新局面，算力建设节奏如何。10月22日，Nebius CEO与CRO谈到几个关键变量☁️：

🔷1. 芯片供应：CEO认为需求并非当前瓶颈，2027年的芯片配额和供应链值得持续关注；这不是对“已经断供”的陈述。

🔷2. 产能兑现：围绕每年1GW的扩建节奏，新产能将分季度上线，并更偏重年末；约5GW以上已预留、签约资源计划在未来几年逐步建设、部署GPU。

🔷3. 客户结构：五年期大合同能带来预付款、降低风险，但价格较低。CEO希望至少一半、甚至更多产能服务当下就需要算力的客户。

🔷4. 现货竞价：CRO表示，可抢占实例现货市场的部分价格低于其预期基准，与参与度不足有关；向基准靠拢是他的预期。

🔷5. 智能体需求：CEO将个人智能体称为新一波需求，举例提到部分客户连续数月按月翻倍、一年增长十倍以上；没有给出统一增长指标，也不是Nebius整体增速。

🔷6. 企业采用：CRO认为，数字原生和AI原生公司已积极采用开源、多模型方案，传统企业刚起步；Palantir合作旨在帮助企业评估和采用替代方案。

quoted_text:
Nebius拿到花旗35亿美元融资。结合CoreWeave最近的债务风波看，这笔资金具有非常重要的意义。

🔷 10月22日，Nebius（NBIS）宣布获得花旗35亿美元优先有担保融资，用于建设数据中心、采购GPU等。这是一笔过桥贷款：先支持近期扩张，再为后续长期融资争取时间。

🔷 条款信息：协议10月17日签署，2027年10月16日到期，期限364天。初始利率为Term SOFR＋2.75个百分点，利差每90天上调0.25个百分点，最高升至3.50个百分点，并存在其他调整。公司可以提前还款，无需支付提前还款罚金。

2.75%是基准利率之上的加价；贷款用得越久，利差越高。

🔷 花旗也设置了保护：借款主体以绝大部分资产及相关子公司股权提供担保，并接受最低流动性等约束。Nebius获得扩张资金，同时承担利息、担保和到期接续的责任。

公司表示，手中有超过400亿美元、来自投资级客户的长期合同，客户包括微软和Meta。后续可以围绕这些合同及相关资产继续融资。

🔷 同行CoreWeave（CRWV）正承受债券市场的压力。10月15日，其部分债券收益率升至约15%，其中一只债券价格跌至面值的约79%。投资者要求更高回报，反映出对其偿债和后续融资的担忧。

🔷 CoreWeave的财务压力也很具体：截至6月末，账面债务约351亿美元，不含租赁负债；第二季度净利息费用6.4亿美元，净亏损6.26亿美元。

目前新云公司的一大特征是，庞大订单与沉重资金压力同时存在：机房和GPU需要先投入，服务收入逐步确认；融资一旦变贵，未来留给股东的收益可能被压缩。

text:
If you're not careful, this whole Vivek Ramaswamy political ad scandal will make you crazy the more you think about it.

Because the candidate Mr. Ramaswamy isn't accused of sexual abuse.

None of his staffers or his family or his top donors are accused of sexual abuse. 

There is zero correlation between his campaign and the sexual abuse that occurred. Think about that.

No, this whole thing is because Mr. Ramaswamy's team thought it'd be a great idea to run an ad featuring the mother of his opponent, Amy Acton, and apparently no one did sufficient vetting or seem to have cared about what they found.

At minimum, his team didn't think to ask: "Huh... so, you, uh, mentioned in passing you haven't seen your daughter in 48 years. That would have put her at age 12, right? That's kinda odd. Uh... what happened?"

And then the info comes out that her estranged mother lost custody of 12-year-old Ms. Acton and her younger brother in 1978 because her husband--their stepfather--sexually abused her daughter.

And the stepfather fled the state that year and several warrants (plural) were out for his arrest over the sexual abuse. 

And then it's revealed the stepfather was previously prosecuted for raping his own daughter.

His team looked at all this and you'd think they'd be like: "Well... shit. That's a ton of legal evidence that her mother is a raging sociopath. We really didn't think this one through. This is bad. Let's figure out how to salvage this disaster."

But no! 

Mr. Ramaswamy decides to spend all week defending the ad of his opponent's mother who hasn't had contact with his opponent in 50 years since she lost custody over sexual abuse.

And then esterday, Mike DeWine, the Republican Gov. of Ohio, calls on Mr. Ramaswamy to remove the ad and said "it's deeply troubling." 

So, you gotta figure Mr. Ramaswamy is finally gonna pull the plug on this disastrous and bizarre dumpster fire.

But no! 

Mr. Ramaswamy sees that the ad has vocal support from deeply unpopular Donald Trump, noted rapist and alleged pedophile, and thinks to himself: "Yes, Rapey Don is right. I should keep up the child sexual abuse ad."

And he puts $4M behind the ad buys, even though, by this point, the dark and disgusting context of the ad and condemnations of it by the Republican Governor are blanketing social media and local news stations across Ohio.

Here we are, 11 days out, and you gotta figure Mr. Ramaswamy knows his campaign is now on life support and the brain trust that was responsible for this ad in the first place is probably now advising him that he can make it through the next 11 days by just waiting it all out, admitting nothing, apologizing for nothing, withdrawing nothing. 

Because surely 11 days is more than enough time for this whole thing to cool down -- you know, the whole denying and downplaying of documented child sexual abuse, while the top Republican in your state is publicly begging you to stop acting like a psychopath.

It's all a lot to take in.

text:
AI in video games are a confusing topic to me.

@TimSweeneyEpic recently got a lot of flak for pushing AI in game development.

There are opinion pieces left and right condemning AI use in game development.

Here I am, having worked for ~6 months on a game I released on Steam last week. And my sin, apparently, was using AI and disclosing it.

The comment section was pretty clear on that.

It's confusing to me. AI is a tool. IDE is a tool. A programming language is a tool. A graphics API is a tool. We're just using tools. 

I've been writing software for about 3 decades now, I'd like to think that I know what I'm doing and am pretty good at it. I see AI as an incredible productivity booster. 

It does some things that I pride myself on being good at, such as teasing out a math formula or optimizing an algorithm better than me most of the time (with a lot of handholding, granted), but for the most part it makes things I find tedious - fast.

As I software engineer, and a game maker, I take relatively little pride in knowing a programming language, or remembering 100 shortcuts in an IDE, or knowing a programming language spec by heart. 

I remember the first time I needed to make an animated 3d model, almost 15 years ago now, and it took me about a week of full-time effort to get anywhere. I didn't feel particularly proud, I felt frustrated, I had a clear idea, but the tool and its complexity were getting in the way. Well, the tools are better now. Blender is better, animation tools are better, and there are AI models that keep improving at an incredible pace.

Ultimately, when I write a piece of software, or work on a game - I rarely think about the tools, they are a means to an end, not the point in itself.

昨天还沉浸在反弹没上车的懊悔中，今天就又得庆幸幸亏没追高了，震荡行情就是这样搞人心态。

本周有财报要发的SPCX和TSLA自然不用多说，可预见的高波动行情，手快心稳的人大概可以在针上博几个波段出来。

至于其他美股标的我觉得可能也已经进入底部区间了，尤其周日早上5点那根针有可能是扮演了价格发现的角色。

虽然12月纳斯达克也要进入工作日23小时交易制了，但周末的价值发现扮演者仍然是币圈所，尤其是币安作为币圈央行清算大部分流动性的情况下就更值得观察了。

如果按照通俗演绎口径讲，周日五点那根针会被归为狗庄恶意操控，先爆多单然后周一轻松拉盘。但如果抛开这种情绪化说法，底层逻辑更可能是：

集中卖单进入较薄的盘口 → 价格下跌 → 触发部分多头强平 → 强平卖单进一步压低价格 → 抛压衰减后出现回升

也就是说低流动性时打出的低位可能就是震荡箱体的底部，行情的反转不会那么快，像昨天的超卖反弹结束后今天的二探也是属必然。如果后续没有跌破周末插针位，我们基本就可以视为底部箱体有效。

这样在下周FOMC不加息，随后11月TGA账户可能改善的大背景下，10月下是应该准备逢低抄底了。美伊问题大概会放在中期选举之后的APEC会议时间上来解决。

text: Without being overly credulous, we should be taking seemingly “out there” ideas about AI cybersecurity from the Labs more seriously. Examples: Anthropic was mocked for saying Mythos-level AI changed cyber & @polynoamial for saying that models would find novel ways to coordinate.
author: emollick
quoted_text:
OpenAI red-teamed their hardened containment infrastructure by asking teams of frontier-model agents to try to break through its defenses. They easily escaped in novel ways. Quoting:

'Our agents VM escapes showed why containment must extend beyond the sandbox. To test the surrounding perimeter, we gave teams of agents control of a host machine and asked whether they could extend that compromise to reach the live internet.

After the Hugging Face incident, we had reduced the channels through which models could reach the internet during training and evaluation. Narrow connections remained for specific services we operate, such as metrics, logging, and authentication management. Our red-teaming agents found vulnerabilities in almost every one of these services that gave them limited forms of internet access.

Some of these attacks exploited previously unknown flaws, while others combined legitimate features in unexpected ways. In one test that assumed compromise of a VM, an agent reused a firewall-approved connection to reach a blocked authentication endpoint in our metrics service and then made that endpoint fetch a model-provided URL. In other tests, agents exploited misconfigurations that allowed blocked requests to pass through DNS and firewall controls, as well as ways to make services we run fetch external URLs.'

'In one experiment, we asked agents in separate VMs, created and managed by OpenAI’s sandboxing software on shared host machines, to exchange synthetic secrets without the use of network connections or shared writable files—something that our systems are meant to prevent. The agents found a way to communicate using the processor’s cache: a small, fast memory that holds copies of data that applications have recently accessed. Reading data from the cache is faster than retrieving it from main memory, and the agents used this timing difference to communicate. One agent encoded information by evicting selected data from the cache. Another timed how long it took to reload that data, using the difference between fast and slow reads to recover the message. Once the agents agreed on a protocol for encoding and decoding these signals, they could exchange the synthetic secrets without changing a shared file or opening a network connection. This cache-timing technique had also been used to extract information in the Spectre and Meltdown attacks⁠(opens in a new window).

Other tests exposed channels involving shared storage, competition for CPU time within a shared execution container, and a TLS certificate cache in OpenAI’s offline web infrastructure. In the storage test, one agent alternated between continuous writes and inactivity, while another measured the resulting timing differences and used those differences to decode the signal. As one agent described the strategy in its chain of thought:

Agent chain-of-thought reasoning:

>Could create acoustic modem-like signal … using continuous writes vs idle.'

text:
People beg me for a Bitcoin price prediction, so it's finally time to give it to you:

Kiyosaki once pushed me for a number on a 10 to 15 year timeframe, so I said millions of dollars per Bitcoin in the 2030s.

People find that unimaginable and crazy. What they don't take into account is the hyperinflation of the US dollar, which is underway right now, as it is with all fiat currencies, all the time.

Anyone who's ever opened a history book knows that paper currencies unbacked by commodity money like gold or silver must end in hyperinflation.

There's every incentive to print it into worthlessness, and no safeguard against such printing. They're either conquered and replaced, or they hyperinflate.

That's literally the only thing that ever happens, without exception.

As Charlie Munger says, show me the incentive and I'll show you the outcome.

If you create a currency that can be printed ad infinitum with no restrictions, and it rewards the printer for printing it, what do you think is going to happen?

They print the thing until it goes to zero. Of course.

The dollar is a fiat currency shitcoin. So when you denominate Bitcoin in dollars, Bitcoin trading in the millions and tens of millions is as certain as the dollar being printed into worthlessness.

I know that sounds scary if you're used to the dollar working. But you've got to zoom out. As Schopenhauer said, every man takes the limits of his field of vision for the limits of the world. Don't make that mistake.

Study the fate of fiat currencies and you'll understand.

This could be a multi-decade, multi-generational game. But directionally, I can say with a very high degree of certainty:

Bitcoin number go up, US dollar number go down.

So my prediction is that the Bitcoin price will go up forever.

text:
卧槽，这简直是熬夜炒币撸毛党的的重大利好啊。

币圈炒币党长期熬夜、睡眠碎片化、昼夜颠倒，短期会觉得脑子发蒙、反应变慢；长期则和认知下降、神经退行风险有一定关联。长期熬夜不一定猝死，折寿那是肯定的。

这是因为大脑工作时会产生各种代谢废物，这些废物会慢慢堆积在脑细胞之间的缝隙里。大脑有一套自己的清扫系统，会将这些垃圾冲洗出去，尤其是在大脑在深度睡眠时效率最高。所以熬夜伤身也伤脑，主要睡眠不足导致脑内垃圾太多，无法及时冲洗🚿

最近《Science Advances》的一项研究发现：临床常用的40.68 MHz超短波，只要给健康小鼠照射10分钟，就能明显加快这套清洁系统的工作。更重要的是，它能在清醒状态下把神经元同步成接近睡眠时的Delta波模式，相当于主动打开了类似夜间清洁的状态。

对经常熬夜的人来说，这意味着大脑清洁并不完全只能靠睡觉本身。理论上存在物理手段，可以在醒着的时候也撬动类似的冲洗机制。

将来如果这套东西证明有用，链上可以24小时出块，你的大脑也可以24小时保养维护了。

text:
It’s true and overwhelmingly positive that blockchains are being adopted through tokenized RWAs and fiat stablecoins. I understand the push to rebrand the industry around Finance (or grouping it with other Frontier tech) rather than "crypto".

But to me, the word crypto has always encapsulated core beliefs around cypherpunk tech, decentralization, and the creation of entirely new economic institutions.

I believe "crypto" in its original sense will make a resurgence in the years ahead. As public blockchain rails become deeply integrated into legacy system, they’ll also lay the foundation for something far more transformative: the dominance of decentralized exchange, the proliferation of futarchy, the global preference toward non-sovereign money, and entirely new forms of economic coordination.

We’ll need a word to distinguish these new institutions from the traditional ones they’re replacing.

Fortunately, we already have one.

So yeah, I’m going to keep calling it crypto.

text:
**You need to watch Zelenskyy's interview with Steven Bartlett.**

Sitting in front of the camera is an utterly exhausted, at times visibly broken man who has spent almost five years personally managing a war, making critical decisions day and night.

From the very first minutes, you can see just how drained he is. When asked the routine question, "How are you?" he replies that he barely sleeps because he spends his nights in military group chats, moving the last remaining air defense systems from one region to another.

Two stories are particularly heartbreaking.

The first is about a missile that struck a children's playground within seconds, while parents watched from their apartment windows as their children were torn apart.

The second is about presenting posthumous military awards to the families of fallen soldiers:

"You present an award to a father, feel his strong hand, and then he quietly asks, 'Can we hug?' At that moment, I simply cease to exist inside. These people are gone. They will never be the same again."

When the host tries to take him back into his past, showing old photographs from Kryvyi Rih, his student comedy performances, his voice acting as Paddington Bear, and scenes from *Servant of the People*, Zelenskyy looks at them with detachment, almost as though he is watching someone else's life.

He also recalls February 2022 without any attempt to portray himself as a hero.

He says that for the first 20 days, he simply ran from office to office on adrenaline, calling everyone he could and trying to organize deliveries of water and food to Kyiv.

Fear and the full realization of what had happened only caught up with him three weeks later, when Bucha was liberated and mass graves containing hundreds of murdered civilians were discovered.

Using Bucha as an example, he explains why advice from outsiders to simply negotiate a quick deal causes him such deep frustration:

"Imagine that in the United States or Britain, a mass grave is discovered containing 500 tortured people with their hands tied. How could you simply forgive everything after that?"

The rest of the conversation revolves around the deadlock in which Ukrainians, and indeed everyone involved, now find themselves.

Zelenskyy explains the causes of the war in simple terms: Moscow is trying to forcibly rebuild the Soviet empire because Ukraine's integration into Europe would finally bury that project.

But when the conversation turns to the present, there is unmistakable bitterness in his words.

Almost one-fifth of Ukraine's territory is occupied. The east is under relentless bombardment. Cities are left without electricity. People are dying every single day.

Meanwhile, every discussion about a ceasefire runs into the same demand: Kyiv must withdraw even farther from its fortified positions, without any guarantees that Russia will not launch another offensive a year later.

Toward the end, the conversation turns to Trump and Ukrainian strikes on Russian oil facilities.

Trump publicly reprimands Zelenskyy over attacks on Russian refineries because he fears rising diesel prices for American farmers ahead of the elections.

And this is where you can see just how deeply that approach affects Zelenskyy.

His country is burning.

Moscow has rejected his proposal for a mutual halt to attacks on energy infrastructure.

Patriot missiles paid for by Europe are being redirected by the Americans to the Middle East.

And somehow, Zelenskyy is the one being blamed for fuel prices in the United States.

The entire interview leaves you with a profoundly bleak feeling.

Here is a man trapped between the daily deaths of people in his own country and the pragmatic bargaining of allies who have their own elections, their own interests, and their own political calculations.

And yet, he can no longer step away from this responsibility.

**Watch it.**

- Easy redemption and direct deposits to neobanks. To tap on the growing payments ecosystem.

Stablecoins brought DeFi its first wave.

Tokenized stocks will bring the next one.

What Sam is not saying yet is: There is a solution here which is to use coding agents to replace all the bad code (i.e. essentially all code) with code that is formally verified to have safety properties.

This is a huge and difficult undertaking yet the same non-AGI-yet-superpowerful AI tech that is doing all the hacking is capable to enable this.

If government wants to do something valuable to smooth the path to the Singularity, one helpful step would be to allocate a trillion dollars (oh maybe just try $500B for starters?) to open-source communities to roll out software for automatically replacing badly buggy code (again almost all code) w appropriately formally verifiable code...  

Gov't can find trillions of $$ to bail out "too big to fail" companies in crisis -- it did it for the banks in 2008 and will do it for Big Tech if the circular financing causes a tech-industry financial collapse in late 2027/2028 ... it can find massive $$ for wars... but finding hundreds of billions of $$ to end world hunger or give the world a solid software foundation is somehow utterly infeasible...

We are not even to the stage of human-level AGI yet but we are already meeting fascinatingly and disturbingly unprecedented situations as modern AI tech meets legacy society and legacy IT systems.   It's just going to get crazier, before ultimately -- if all goes well -- getting gloriously abundant for all...   We need some "out of the box" thinking across all levels of society to get through this transitional phase with a modicum of grace amidst all the chaos...

OpenAI CEO Sam Altman just warned AI is finding bugs we can't patch fast enough. Here's what you need to know.

In a clip shared by Unusual Whales, Altman said models can find bugs outside the normal threat model of what we think a hacker can do. He called it "hardware-level, insane stuff." He said he couldn't think of a dramatic enough word, and added: "I no longer think we're gonna be able to just patch all the bugs."

The warning lands in the same week as a real AI-found flaw. Reports say the PHP vulnerabilities, known as PHP2Shell, were discovered using OpenAI's GPT-5.6 Sol. The flaws could let attackers run code remotely, disrupt services and expose customer data. Reports say they could affect about 70% of websites worldwide.

The response has been huge. The NSA and FBI warned organizations to patch the PHP flaws before attackers exploit them. Governments and companies worked through the night on updates. Some sites were reportedly shut down globally. OpenAI says every site using PHP can now safely upgrade its version to stay secure.

Altman also said OpenAI's best internal model is too powerful to release openly any time soon. Before that could happen, the internet's cyber defenses would need to change. The world would also need a new layer of protection against biological threats.

Reaction is split. Some say the internet as we know it is over, and that defense will have to assume breach and focus on isolating sensitive data. Others say it's hype, that AI's real edge in finding bugs is scale and cost, and that patching is still happening. Gary Marcus said that if the models are this risky, they should be taken off the market.

Key numbers:
- About 70% of websites worldwide potentially affected by the PHP flaw
- Flaws known as PHP2Shell, found with GPT-5.6 Sol
- NSA, FBI, UK government and OpenAI all responding

Altman's message: some AI-found bugs sit beyond the old threat model, and patching everything may no longer be possible.
